- the sense is the only sense of its entry, unless the entry stays a variant of an entry or sense that has a stem analysis (see `compose-delete-sense`);
- the sense is a sub-sense; only a top-level sense moves;
- a sub-sense has an analysis different from the sense's own;
- a parser analysis (morph bundle) still refers to the sense, because its morph and analysis would no longer match; retarget it first;
- the morph type and the analysis disagree, for example a stem analysis on a suffix.

A Draft may move several senses out of one root. Each move is composed against the Draft's earlier steps, so the second move sees the first one's result. The Dry Run lists the old entry's senses, the new entry's senses and the sense's analysis; each operation carries a rationale, and the Draft still needs its own (`proposal rationale`) before Finalize.

Use this editor through the CLI. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` (at most 300 characters) to cite every operation this command produces. Review the Dry Run effects before Finalize; only a person can Apply the Proposal.

entries.title: Reorder sound rules
entries.description: Moves phonological rules to a new order, with the fewest moves, so a later rule sees the output of the earlier ones. Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Reorder sound rules

Use this command to change the order in which phonological rules apply. A later rule sees the output of the earlier ones, so order decides whether a chain such as a class-to-nasal rule and a nasal deletion works at all.

```sh
motif compose-order-phonological-rules --project language.fwdata --draft rule-order \
  --intent '{"rule":"<rule-id>","before":"<other-rule-id>"}'
```

Give either one move (`rule` with `before` or `after`) or the whole new order (`order`, every rule once). The command plans the fewest moves and refuses an unknown rule, an incomplete order, or an order that changes nothing. Rules keep their contexts, features and disabled state.

Dry Run and Trial the Proposal on a word that needs the chain, then Finalize it for a person to review and Apply.

entries.title: Stage a Parsimony ruling
entries.description: Stages a keep, fix, ask, or defer decision for one exact Parsimony finding in a Draft Proposal. A pending keep does not suppress current findings, and only a person can Apply it.
entries.helpPage:
# Stage a Parsimony ruling

Use this command to stage a decision about one finding in a Draft Proposal. The intent names an existing Notebook record type, the finding's exact subject and evidence digest, and one ruling: `keep`, `fix`, `ask`, or `defer`. A reason is optional; `ask` requires a question.

```sh
motif compose-record-parsimony-disposition --project language.fwdata --draft review-one --intent '{"recordTypeId":"...","measureId":"P-allo-duplicate-form","subject":{},"disposition":"keep","evidenceDigest":"...","evidenceContract":"...","subjectCaption":"...","measureCaption":"...","reason":"..."}'
```

The command appends bounded Notebook and reserved-field operations to the Draft. Review the Proposal with Dry Run before a human Applies it. A pending keep does not change the live findings; it becomes project data only after Apply and a later Refresh.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` (at most 300 characters) to record the source on every operation this command produces.

entries.title: Stage a source-validated decision
entries.description: Stages, in a Draft, a decision a named program made from cited sources: an approval or disapproval of one existing analysis under a non-human agent, or the evidence for a wordform or analysis alone. It is never a person's decision and never sets spelling status; only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Stage a source-validated decision

`compose-record-source-validated-decision` stages a decision that a named program, not a person, made from cited sources. It has two forms.

To approve or disapprove an analysis, give the existing analysis as `target`, an `agent` (a `name` and the `version` of the source release it stands for) and a `member` of `approves` or `disapproves`. FieldWorks will show the decision under that non-human agent. A person's approvals and disapprovals are never touched, and a new release of the sources is a new agent. Agents are told apart by name and version, so if release 1 approved an analysis and release 2 disapproves it, `difference produce --reference source-validated` marks the word `conflicting-decisions` and counts neither; stage the later release only after you have decided what to do with the earlier one.

To record why a word form is wrong or right without deciding anything in FieldWorks, give the wordform or analysis as `target` and leave `agent` and `member` out. This never changes spelling status, which stays a person's.

Either way, `evidence` says why: a `tier` (for example `source-approved`, `misspelled-typo` or `ill-formed`), the cited `sources` (a dictionary, a grammar, a corpus or an example, each with an optional locator) and the facts the tier requires: a typo needs `intendedForm` and `editType`, an ill-formed word needs `violatedRule`, a nonstandard variant needs `standardForm`, and a source-approved analysis needs a dictionary, a grammar and a corpus source. Read the records back with `evidence show`.

Motif stages the change in a Draft for a person to review. Only a person can Apply.

entries.title: Relink natural-class users
entries.description: Moves explicitly named environments and rewrite-rule contexts to a replacement class created earlier in the Draft. Other users remain on the source class. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Relink natural-class users

Use this command when a class should keep its current meaning for most of the grammar, but selected users need a new class. It changes only the environment and rewrite-rule contexts you name.

```sh
motif compose-relink-natural-class --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '{"source":"<sourceClassId>","replacement":"<newClassId>","replacementCreationOperation":"<createOperationId>","environments":[{"target":"<environmentId>","expectedLeft":[{"naturalClass":"<sourceClassId>"}],"expectedRight":[]}],"ruleContexts":["<ruleContextId>"]}'
```

Create the replacement class earlier in the same Draft and use both its entity id and the operation id returned by that create. Each environment entry supplies its exact current typed left and right contexts; Motif compares their rendering with the saved environment string before replacing the source-class references. Each listed rule context must currently point to the source class. Unlisted users stay on the source class; the composer response lists the current users so you can review the declared scope, and the Dry Run records the actual references that change.

Finish the Draft, inspect its Dry Run to confirm the intended scope, and run a bounded Trial across corrected, held-out and contrastive forms. Only a person can Apply the Proposal.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` (at most 300 characters) to record the source on every operation this command produces.

entries.title: Remove an alternate form
entries.description: Removes one alternate form (allomorph) of an entry that nothing refers to; Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply. It refuses the lexeme form and a form that a parser analysis or any other object refers to.
entries.helpPage:
# Remove an alternate form

Remove one alternate form (allomorph) of an entry. Use it when an alternate form stands in for something that now has its own entry, or is redundant.

```sh
motif compose-remove-alternate-form --project language.fwdata --draft ceb-d004 \
  --intent '{"entry":"<entry-id>","form":"<form-id>"}'
```

`entry` and `form` are required and the intent is closed. The form must be an alternate form owned by the entry; the lexeme form cannot be removed this way.

The command refuses, and changes nothing, when anything refers to the form: a morph bundle of a parser analysis, an ad hoc prohibition, or any other object. The message names the referrer; retarget or remove that reference first. The Dry Run shows the entry's alternate forms before and after and a preview of the removed form, with its class, its text in every writing system, its morph type, its position and its number of environments. A writing system the project cannot resolve is shown by its numeric handle.

Use this editor through the CLI. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` (at most 300 characters) to cite every operation this command produces. Review the Dry Run effects before Finalize; only a person can Apply the Proposal.

entries.title: Remove exception feature
entries.description: Deletes one exception feature and clears every use of it in one Proposal, reporting the counts first. Affix restrictions are counted, not edited. Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Remove exception feature

Use this command to take one exception feature out of the grammar's uses in one step: every stem that carries it, and every phonological rule branch that requires or excludes it. It reports the counts first.

```sh
motif compose-remove-exception-feature --project language.fwdata --draft drop-retains \
  --intent '{"feature":"<feature-id>","expectedName":"Retains initial cluster"}'
```

`expectedName` must match the feature's current name in some writing system, so a stale id is refused. `keepFeature: true` removes the references but leaves the feature in the Exception Features list.

The command finds the references in one pass over the analyses and the rules, so its cost grows with their number and it starts no parser. It then deletes the feature and its Phonological Rule Features wrapper in the same Proposal, as FieldWorks does when you delete an exception feature, unless you keep it or an affix still names it.

Read the output before you finalize:

- **Affixes.** It does not edit affix From or To Exception Features. An affix that requires the removed feature matches no stem afterwards and its readings disappear. The output counts these analyses and keeps the feature; edit them with `compose-edit-exception-features` or `compose-edit-derivational-affix-restriction`.
- **Widening.** A rule branch that required only this feature applies to every stem afterwards; the output warns you.

Run a Trial after Dry Run. The Trial prints the reading-identity proof (ADR 0015) for the words it parsed: how many words kept the same readings, and each reading lost or newly allowed.

The command stages operations in a Draft and does not change the saved FieldWorks project. Finalize the Proposal for a person to review and Apply.

entries.title: Remove a feature value
entries.description: Stages the removal of one feature's specification from a stem's MsFeatures, an inflectional affix's InflFeats, or a derivational affix's FromMsFeatures or ToMsFeatures, so the stem stops carrying the feature or the affix stops requiring or giving it. The feature structure stays. Refuses a feature the structure does not specify. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Remove a feature value

Use this command to take one feature's specification off a feature structure: a stem's MsFeatures, so the stem no longer carries the feature, or an inflectional affix's InflFeats, so the affix no longer requires it. It undoes [authoring a feature value](cmd:compose-author-feature-value).

```sh
motif compose-remove-feature-value --project language.fwdata --draft agreement \
  --intent '{"featStruc":"<feature-structure-id>","feature":"<feature-id>"}'
```

The intent has exactly `featStruc` and `feature`. The structure stays even when it ends up empty; an empty structure requires nothing. To change a value, remove the specification and author the new one in a later Draft step, because a second specification for the same feature is refused while the first exists.

Refusal messages contain a stable name:

- `feature-value-not-found`: the structure has no specification for that feature.
- `feature-structure-not-grammatical-info`: the structure belongs to none of a stem, an inflectional affix or a derivational affix.

The command stages operations in a Draft and does not change the saved FieldWorks project. Dry Run and Trial the Proposal, then Finalize it for a person to review and Apply.

entries.title: Retire an affix slot
entries.description: Deletes an inflectional affix slot that no affix analysis and no template uses any more. It refuses a slot still in use and names what uses it; Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Retire an affix slot

Delete an inflectional affix slot that nothing uses any more.

```sh
motif compose-retire-affix-slot --project language.fwdata --draft slot-cleanup \
  --intent '{"slot":"<slot-id>"}'
```

`slot` is required and the intent is closed. The command refuses, changing nothing, while any inflectional affix analysis still names the slot or any affix template still lists it, and the message says how many of each. Move the affixes to another slot with `compose-edit-inflectional-affix` and take the slot out of its templates with `compose-edit-affix-template` first, in the same Draft or an earlier one; nothing is reassigned or cascaded for you.

A template that loses its last slot is allowed, and the grammar check then warns that the template has no slots. Use `compose-edit-affix-slot` to rename a slot or change whether it is optional instead of retiring it.

Use this editor through the CLI. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` (at most 300 characters) to cite the operation. Only a person can Apply the Proposal.

entries.title: Retire a boundary marker
entries.description: Removes a stray duplicate of the word or morpheme boundary marker from the first phoneme set, so a phonological rule with a boundary can be authored again. It refuses the standard marker and any marker a rule, environment or other object still uses; Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Retire a duplicate boundary marker

Remove a stray second copy of the word boundary (`#`) or morpheme boundary (`+`) marker from the first phoneme set. Motif refuses to author a rule with a boundary while the set holds two markers for the same boundary, because it cannot tell which one the rule should name; retiring the unused copy clears that refusal.

```sh
motif compose-retire-boundary-marker --project language.fwdata --draft boundary-fix \
  --intent '{"marker":"<marker-id>"}'
```

`marker` is required and the intent is closed. The refusal that sends you here names the stray marker and the standard marker the rule must use. The command retires only a marker whose every spelling is `#` or `+` and whose standard marker, with the same spelling, is still in the set. It refuses the standard marker itself, and refuses, changing nothing, when any rule, environment or other object still refers to the marker; the message names the referrer. Retarget that use to the standard marker in FieldWorks first. Nothing is retargeted or cascaded for you.

The Dry Run shows the phoneme set's boundary markers before and after. Use this editor through the CLI. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` (at most 300 characters) to cite the operation. Only a person can Apply the Proposal.

entries.title: Rewrite lexeme forms
entries.description: Rewrites existing lexeme forms with expected-current guards while preserving their identities and references. Give explicit new forms to retain underlying distinctions until ordered grammar rules realize running spelling; Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Rewrite lexeme forms

```sh
motif compose-rewrite-lexeme-form --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '{"foldStressMarks":false,"entries":[{"entryGuid":"<id>","writingSystem":"qaa","expectedForm":"pata","newForm":"pātaʔ"}]}'
```

Rewrites the lexeme forms of existing entries, many in one Draft, preserving each form's identity, references, conditions and other writing-system alternatives. Each entry names its writing system and the `expectedForm` it holds now; a different current form refuses the whole batch and stages nothing. Give an explicit `newForm` with `foldStressMarks=false` to restore an underlying distinction from selected evidence.

A parser form may carry represented segments, vowel quantity or lexical stress that running spelling omits. Keep the form nonabstract and each phoneme's representation nonempty. Morphology and sound rules use those distinctions before final ordered rules realize the unmarked written word. Marked dictionary spellings may stay in Citation Form. Restoring information requires source evidence; the command cannot infer missing stops or quantity from plain spelling.

The initial proof targets unmarked running text using simultaneous regular rules ordered on Morphology, with empty Clitics and Surface strata, `NotOnClitics=true`, empty `HC/Strata` and `HC/DelReapps=0` (the FieldWorks default). A value of 0 still permits inverse deletion. Attached clitics and multiple cycles require separately proved domains. PanGloss 0.15.2 completes the generic `patʔa` → `pat-a` proof; the reference hc.dll hangs beyond 600 seconds on `pat-a` with the full simultaneous chain, so parity for that case is unproved.

The legacy `foldStressMarks` option computes the new form from `expectedForm` and requires `newForm` to be omitted: decompose to NFD, remove only U+0300 (grave), U+0301 (acute), U+0302 (circumflex), U+0304 (macron) and U+030C (caron), recompose to NFC. Every other mark, such as the tilde of n-tilde, is kept. This is a destructive spelling fold, not a phonological realization. In Wolff's Cebuano notation acute marks length, grave marks a following glottal stop, and caron marks exceptional stress. Do not fold a distinction needed by the grammar; retaining it only in Citation Form cannot condition parsing.

`setEmptyCitationForm` copies the old lexeme spelling into an empty Citation Form in that writing system. It leaves an existing Citation Form alone and skips an entry whose lexeme form would not change. To preserve a different selected source headword, use [Edit a citation form](cmd:compose-edit-citation-form). To edit an existing ordinary alternate, use [Edit an allomorph form](cmd:compose-edit-allomorph-form).

The command stages writes in the Draft. Finish the Draft, inspect its Dry Run and Trial the actual written words; only a person can Apply a Proposal. A spelling-only result cannot prove quantity or stress erased before output.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` (at most 300 characters) to record the source on the operations this command produces.

entries.title: Set an affix's repeat count
entries.description: Stages one explicit change to how many times one affix may apply to a word, for an affix the language stacks (a verb extension said twice, a repeated converb suffix). The parser applies each affix once unless the project says otherwise; the expected value guards against stale evidence, and only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Set an affix's repeat count

```sh
motif compose-set-affix-max-apps --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '{"msa":"<affix MSA id>","expectedMaxApps":1,"maxApps":2}'
```

The parser applies each affix rule once per word. When the language stacks the same affix (a verb extension said twice, a repeated converb suffix), give that affix a higher count instead of repeating a template slot. `msa` is the id of the affix's morphosyntactic analysis: inflectional, derivational or unclassified. `maxApps` is a whole number from 1 to 3; 1 is the default and removes the setting. `expectedMaxApps` must match the count Motif reads while preparing the Draft (1 when none is set); a stale value is refused.

Only that affix's count changes. Every other parser setting in the project is kept (the XML is re-serialised, so its content is unchanged but its spacing may differ). If the affix has equal analyses on its entry, the count is written on the one FieldWorks builds the rule from and the result names it. Setting the count the project already holds changes nothing. A bigger count makes the parser try more analyses for that affix; PanGloss measured on Swahili that new parses stop at 3 while ambiguity keeps growing, so 3 is the most Motif sets.

The count is stored in the project's parser settings as `HC/AffixRules/AffixRule[@guid][@maxApps]`. PanGloss reads it. FieldWorks's own parser does not read it yet, so FLEx parses the affix once until FieldWorks does.

The command stages one write in the Draft. It does not change the FieldWorks project. Finish the Draft, inspect its Dry Run, and compare bounded before and after Trials with the same words, repeated forms included. Review the after Report; only a person can Apply a Proposal.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` (at most 300 characters) to record the source on the operation this command produces.

entries.title: Set a character's class
entries.description: Stages one change that makes named characters of a project writing system part of a word or punctuation, such as making the curly quotes punctuation so they stop being part of a word. The Trial re-reads the Texts with the changed writing system; only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Set a character's class

```sh
motif compose-set-character-class --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '{"ws":"ceb","class":"punctuation","characters":"\u2018\u2019"}'
```

Moves the named characters of one project writing system between word-forming (part of a word) and punctuation (not part of a word). `class` is `wordForming` or `punctuation`; `characters` lists the characters together, one visible character each. Motif refuses punctuation for a letter, mark or modifier, because no writing-system setting can make one so.

The command stages one write in the Draft. It does not change the FieldWorks project. Finish the Draft, inspect its Dry Run, and Trial the affected Texts: the Trial re-reads them with the changed writing system, so a word such as `‘baba’` becomes `baba`. Review the after Report; only a person can Apply a Proposal. Apply writes the project's writing-system file and re-reads the Texts that contain the changed characters.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` (at most 300 characters) to record the source on the operation this command produces.

entries.title: Tag entries with their source
entries.description: Stages, for many lexical entries at once, the Attribution tag <source>@<revision> <licence> in each entry's Bibliography, written after any Bibliography text already there. An entry that already carries the tag stages nothing, so the command is safe to run again. Give one intent with many entries, or --entries-file and --tag; only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Tag entries with their source

Records where lexical entries came from, in the Bibliography of each entry, as the Attribution tag `<source>@<revision> <licence>`, such as `lang-sme@9ba7be7 GPL-3.0`. It is the per-entry half of how a project keeps the licence of imported data. The Lexical entries and glosses Subject explains when to use both parts and what goes in the project half.

```sh
motif compose-set-entry-attribution --project language.fwdata --draft my-draft \
  --intent '{"tag":"lang-sme@9ba7be7 GPL-3.0","entries":[{"entry":"<entry-id>"},{"entry":"<entry-id>"}]}'
```

For a long list, give a text file of entries and the tag instead of `--intent` (the two cannot be combined):

```sh
motif compose-set-entry-attribution --project language.fwdata --draft my-draft \
  --entries-file entries.txt --tag "lang-sme@9ba7be7 GPL-3.0" [--analysis-ws en]
```

The file holds one entry per line, as an entry id or as a FieldWorks GUID. Blank lines and lines starting with `#` are skipped. A line that is neither an id nor a GUID, and an entry the project does not have, are refused together in one message, each with its line number, so one run lists everything to fix. Nothing is staged when any line is refused.

The tag is written in an analysis writing system: `--analysis-ws` (the intent's `analysisWs`) when given, otherwise the project's default analysis writing system; a vernacular-only writing system is refused. The entry's Bibliography keeps whatever it already holds in that writing system, and the tag follows it after `; `. The command is idempotent: an entry that already carries the tag exactly stages nothing, so a repeated run adds no second copy. A different revision of the same source is added beside the first. An entry that already carries the same source and revision under a different licence is refused, because which licence applies is for a person to decide.

Each staged operation sets the whole Bibliography alternative for that writing system, so text added in FieldWorks after the Dry Run is caught by the Proposal's anchor at Apply. The Bibliography is exported as a bibliography note in a LIFT export, so the tag survives a round trip. Changing it moves no parse, so a Trial of this Proposal measures only what it names.

The command stages a change in the Draft; it does not change the project. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` (at most 300 characters) to record a source on every operation. Only a person can Apply a Proposal.
usage: Usage: motif compose-set-entry-attribution --draft <name> --project <fwdata> --intent '<closed intent JSON>', or --entries-file <file> --tag '<source>@<revision> <licence>' [--analysis-ws <tag>] in place of --intent [--cite-source <text> [--cite-locator <text>]]

entries.title: Set entry parsing flag
entries.description: Stages the FieldWorks do-not-parse flag on a lexical entry. The flag does not stop the entry parsing: PanGloss, FieldWorks HermitCrab and XAmple all parse a flagged entry, whole entry and not just compounds; to stop a stem parsing, retype it with compose-set-stem-part-of-speech or delete it.
entries.helpPage:
# Set entry parsing flag

```sh
motif compose-set-entry-do-not-parse --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '{"target":"<entry-id>","expectedDoNotParse":false,"doNotParse":true}'
```

This stages the FieldWorks `DoNotUseForParsing` flag on one lexical entry. Its intended scope is the entire entry, including its morphs and analyses: it is not a restriction on compounds alone. Set `doNotParse` to `false` to clear it. The composer refuses a missing or wrong-type target and an `expectedDoNotParse` value that does not match the saved project.

Neither FieldWorks' HermitCrab nor its XAmple transform reads this flag, and PanGloss parses a flagged entry too, so the flag changes no parse, in a Trial or in FieldWorks. It is only a note kept in the project and is not a way to retire an entry. To stop a stem parsing, retype it to the category it belongs to with `compose-set-stem-part-of-speech` (a particle, determiner or interjection takes no inflection or derivation), or delete the entry; otherwise disable the rule or template that lets it parse. Setting the flag deletes nothing, and a Proposal that sets `doNotParse` back to `false` (with `expectedDoNotParse` `true`) clears it.

To flag many entries in one Proposal, put one `compose-set-entry-do-not-parse` intent per entry in a [`compose-batch`](cmd:compose-batch) file; but to change how words parse, retype the stems the same way instead.

The command stages a change in the Draft; it does not change the project. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` (at most 300 characters) to record a source on the operation. Only a person can Apply a Proposal.

entries.title: Set default compounding
entries.description: Stages one explicit change to the parser's built-in default compounding in a Draft. A project with no compound rules of its own still has the parser join any two stems unless default compounding is turned off; the expected value guards against stale evidence, and only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Set default compounding

```sh
motif compose-set-no-default-compounding --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '{"expectedNoDefaultCompounding":false,"noDefaultCompounding":true}'
```

The parser joins any two stems into a word by default, even when the project has no compound rules, unless the project's parser settings say otherwise. This composer sets that choice: `true` turns the built-in default compounding off, `false` turns it on again. `expectedNoDefaultCompounding` must match the value Motif reads while preparing the Draft; a stale value is refused.

Only the one setting changes. Every other parser setting in the project is kept. Setting the value the project already holds changes nothing.

The command stages one write in the Draft. It does not change the FieldWorks project. Finish the Draft, inspect its Dry Run, and compare bounded before and after Trials with the same words, real compounds included. Review the after Report; only a person can Apply a Proposal.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` (at most 300 characters) to record the source on the operation this command produces.

entries.title: Set rules on clitics
entries.description: Stages one explicit change to whether the parser's phonological rules also run on a word with its clitic attached. By default the rules run on the word before a clitic attaches; the expected value guards against stale evidence, and only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Set rules on clitics

```sh
motif compose-set-not-on-clitics --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '{"expectedNotOnClitics":true,"notOnClitics":false}'
```

The parser runs the project's phonological rules on a word before any clitic attaches to it, unless the project's parser settings say otherwise. This composer sets that choice: `true` keeps the rules off the clitic, so a clitic keeps its own spelling; `false` runs the rules on the word with its clitic attached, so a rule can change the clitic's sounds too. A project that never set the choice holds `true`. `expectedNotOnClitics` must match the value Motif reads while preparing the Draft; a stale value is refused.

Only the one setting changes. Every other parser setting in the project is kept. Setting the value the project already holds changes nothing the parser reads.

The command stages one write in the Draft. It does not change the FieldWorks project. Finish the Draft, inspect its Dry Run, and compare bounded before and after Trials with the same words, clitic forms included. Review the after Report; only a person can Apply a Proposal.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` (at most 300 characters) to record the source on the operation this command produces.

entries.title: Approve or clear an Occurrence of a Source
entries.description: Stages the approval of one word of a Paratext Source with an analysis, or clears it back to a guess. Approving also approves the analysis when its Opinion is Unknown, and adds the analysis first when only a parser reading exists.
entries.helpPage:
# Approve or clear an Occurrence of a Source

Stage the approval of one word of a Paratext Source with an analysis, or clear it back to a guess. Approving also approves the analysis when its Opinion is Unknown. A Disapproved Opinion is left as it is. When only a parser reading exists, give the stored wordform and the reading, and the analysis is added in the same Draft.

```sh
motif compose-set-occurrence-approval --project language.fwdata --draft pending --intent '{"source":"WEB","anchor":"MAT 5:3#2","action":"Approve","analysis":"<analysis id>"}'
```

entries.title: Turn a sound rule off or on
entries.description: Disables or enables one phonological rule. A disabled rule stays in place but the parser does not load it. Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Turn a sound rule off or on

Use this command to disable or enable a phonological rule. A disabled rule stays in the project, in its place, but the parser does not load it.

```sh
motif compose-set-phonological-rule-disabled --project language.fwdata --draft rule-off \
  --intent '{"target":"<rule-id>","expectedDisabled":false,"disabled":true}'
```

`expectedDisabled` must match the rule's current state; a stale value is refused. Use this to test a grammar without a rule, or to hold a rule back until its words are in.

entries.title: State the project's source
entries.description: Stages one notice in the project's Description saying which source, revision and licence imported data came from, after any Description text already there. A project that already states the notice stages nothing. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# State the project's source

States once, in the project's Description, which source, revision and licence imported data came from. The notice reads `Attribution: <source>@<revision> <licence>`, such as `Attribution: lang-sme@9ba7be7 GPL-3.0`. It is the project half of how a project keeps the licence of imported data. The Lexical entries and glosses Subject explains when to use both parts, and [Tag entries with their source](cmd:compose-set-entry-attribution) stages the per-entry tag.

```sh
motif compose-set-project-attribution --project language.fwdata --draft my-draft \
  --intent '{"tag":"lang-sme@9ba7be7 GPL-3.0"}'
```

The notice is written in an analysis writing system: `analysisWs` when given, otherwise the project's default analysis writing system. It follows whatever the Description already holds in that writing system, on a new line, and the existing text is kept. The command is idempotent: a Description that already states the notice exactly stages nothing. A different revision of the same source is added as a second notice. A Description that already states the same source and revision under a different licence is refused, because which licence applies is for a person to decide.

The change is an edit of the whole Description for that writing system, so a change made in FieldWorks after the Dry Run is caught by the Proposal's anchor at Apply. It moves no parse.

The command stages a change in the Draft; it does not change the project. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` (at most 300 characters) to record a source on the operation. Only a person can Apply a Proposal.

entries.title: Re-point a meaning's analysis
entries.description: Points a meaning, top level or nested, at a different analysis of the same entry, keeping all its content; Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply. If no sense would use the old analysis afterwards, LibLCM removes it, and the operation's rationale says so. It refuses an analysis of another entry, a stem analysis on an affix, an affix analysis on a stem, a meaning that already uses the analysis, and an old analysis something else still refers to.
entries.helpPage:
# Point a sense at an analysis

Point an existing sense at another analysis of the same entry. The sense keeps its identity, glosses, definitions, examples and sub-senses.

```sh
motif compose-set-sense-msa --project language.fwdata --draft ceb-d003 \
  --intent '{"sense":"<sense-id>","analysis":"<analysis-id>"}'
```

Both fields are required and the intent is closed. `analysis` must be an analysis the sense's own entry already has, and must suit the entry's lexeme form: a stem analysis for a stem, an affix analysis for an affix. A sub-sense may be pointed too.

The command refuses, and changes nothing, when:

- the sense does not exist or the id names another kind of object;
- `analysis` is not an analysis of the sense's entry; the refusal lists the entry's analyses and names `compose-add-morphosyntax-analysis` for one the entry lacks;
- the sense already uses that analysis;
- a stem analysis would go on an affix, or an affix analysis on a stem;
- the sense is the last to use its analysis and a parser analysis (morph bundle) or an ad hoc prohibition still refers to it.

When no other sense uses the old analysis, LibLCM removes it, and the operation's rationale says so, naming any slot membership that goes with it. The Dry Run shows the sense and its entry; run a Trial to see which parses change.

Use this editor through the CLI or the MCP tool `motif_set_sense_msa`. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` (at most 300 characters) to cite the operation. Review the Dry Run effects before Finalize; only a person can Apply the Proposal.

entries.title: Change a Source's Context
entries.description: Stages the books and chapters a Source covers, read in the Source's versification.
entries.helpPage:
# Change a Source's Context

Stage the books and chapters a Source covers. The Context is read in the Source's versification.

```sh
motif compose-set-source-context --project language.fwdata --draft pending --intent '{"source":"WEB","context":"MAT-ACT"}'
```

The command refuses a Context that does not read in the versification.

entries.title: Rename a Source
entries.description: Stages a new display name for a Source in the project or staged in the Draft.
entries.helpPage:
# Rename a Source

Stage a new display name for a Source that is in the project or was added earlier in the Draft.

```sh
motif compose-set-source-name --project language.fwdata --draft pending --intent '{"source":"WEB","name":"World Bible"}'
```

A later rename of the same Source replaces an earlier one in the Draft.

entries.title: Remove or restore a Source
entries.description: Stages a Source as Removed or Active again. A removed Source stays in the list, so its id is never reused.
entries.helpPage:
# Remove or restore a Source

Stage a Source as Removed, or as Active again. A removed Source stays in the list and keeps its id.

```sh
motif compose-set-source-status --project language.fwdata --draft pending --intent '{"source":"WEB","status":"Removed"}'
```

entries.title: Change a Source's versification
entries.description: Stages a new versification for a Source; its Context must still read in it.
entries.helpPage:
# Change a Source's versification

Stage a new versification for a Source. Its present Context must still read in the new one.

```sh
motif compose-set-source-versification --project language.fwdata --draft pending --intent '{"source":"WEB","versification":"Original"}'
```

The command refuses a versification Motif does not know.

entries.title: Set a stem's part of speech
entries.description: Sets the part of speech of one existing stem analysis after checking the expected current value. A sub-category keeps the class and features it inherits; a class or feature the new category cannot hold is dropped by LibLCM and named in a warning; Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Set a stem's part of speech

Set the part of speech of an existing stem analysis. The expected value is the stored part of speech, or `null` when the analysis has none.

```sh
motif compose-set-stem-part-of-speech --project language.fwdata --draft numerals \
  --intent '{"target":"<stem-analysis-id>","expectedPartOfSpeech":null,"partOfSpeech":"<part-of-speech-id>"}'
```

All three intent fields are required and the intent is closed. The target must be a stem analysis. A sub-category inherits its parent's inflection classes and feature selections, so moving a stem to a sub-category keeps both. When the move would drop the stem's inflection class or a feature selection that neither the new part of speech nor one of its ancestors holds (LibLCM removes them on the move), the command does not refuse: the operation's rationale says `Warning: the move drops ...` and the Dry Run shows the result for a person to judge. To keep a feature, make it bearable by the new part of speech or an ancestor first. When the expected and desired values are the same, the command adds no operations. The command only sets a part of speech; it never clears one.

Run many at once with `compose-batch`, so a whole clean-up becomes one Proposal. Each operation carries a rationale; the Draft still needs its own Rationale (`proposal rationale`) before Finalize.

Use this editor through the CLI; it is not exposed as an MCP tool. Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` (at most 300 characters) to cite every operation this command produces. Review the Dry Run effects and run a Trial on affected words before Finalize; only a person can Apply the Proposal.

entries.title: Split a spelling into a phoneme
entries.description: Stages the move of one spelling of a phoneme into a new phoneme of its own, which undoes a merge. The phoneme keeps its other spellings, and the new phoneme starts with no natural class and no features. It refuses a spelling an environment writes. Dry Run and Trial before a person Applies the Proposal.
entries.helpPage:
# Split a spelling into a phoneme

Use this command to move one spelling of a phoneme into a new phoneme of its own. It undoes `compose-merge-phoneme`, and it also separates a spelling that turns out to be a real contrast.

```sh
motif compose-split-phoneme --project language.fwdata --draft sounds \
  --intent '{"source":"<phoneme-id>","representation":"o","name":"o"}'
```

The intent has exactly `source`, `representation` and `name`. The phoneme keeps its other spellings. The new phoneme has the given name and the one spelling, and no natural class and no features, so add it to its natural classes afterwards with `compose-edit-natural-class`.

Refusal messages begin with a stable name:

- `phoneme-not-in-inventory`: the source is not a phoneme of the first phoneme set.
- `phoneme-representation-not-found`: the phoneme has no such spelling.
- `phoneme-split-last-representation`: the spelling is the only way the phoneme is written, so nothing would stay behind.
- `phoneme-split-name-missing`: the new phoneme has no name.
- `phoneme-representation-referenced`: an environment writes the spelling; change that environment first.

The command stages operations in a Draft and does not change the saved FieldWorks project. Dry Run and Trial the Proposal, then Finalize it for a person to review and Apply.

entries.title: Strip copied variant senses
entries.description: Turns variants that copy their main sense into sense-less variants of that sense: repoints the variant at the main sense, deletes the copied senses and analyses, keeps the form and environment, and reports the exception-feature change per entry; Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Strip the copied senses of variants

Turn variant entries that copy their main entry's sense (a gloss and an analysis of their own) into sense-less variants of that sense. The variant keeps its lexeme form, its allomorph and its environment; it loses the copy. The parser then reads the variant as the main sense's stem, with the main sense's gloss and analysis, so a stem with two shapes is one analysis instead of two copies.

```sh
motif compose-strip-variant-senses --project language.fwdata --draft my-draft \
  --intent '{"entries":[{"entry":"<variant-entry-id>"},{"entry":"<other-variant-id>","component":"<main-sense-id>"}]}'
```

Each item has an `entry` (the variant) and an optional `component`. The variant must have exactly one variant reference with one component and one variant type. The main sense is the one the variant already points at; when it points at the main entry instead, the command repoints it at the main entry's only sense, or at the `component` you name when the main entry has several. The main sense must have a stem analysis.

What goes: the variant's senses with their sub-senses and examples, and the analyses only they used. The command refuses, and changes nothing, when anything refers to a copied sense or analysis (a relation, a component of another variant, a parser analysis), when the main sense has no stem analysis, or when the main sense belongs to another entry than the one the variant varies.

The Dry Run reports, per entry, the exception features the copied analysis had that the main sense lacks (the variant loses them) and the ones the main sense has that the copy lacked (the variant gains them), and a copied gloss that differs from the main sense's. Review those before a person Applies the Proposal. A sense-less variant of a sense is what LibLCM's CreateVariantEntryAndBackRef makes (ADR 0003).

entries.title: Tag stems by query
entries.description: Gives one exception feature to every stem a query selects (category, final letters, an existing feature, a gloss), reporting how many match and how many are tagged first. For a rule gate it tags whichever of the matching or the other stems is fewer; an affix gate can only require the feature. Motif stages a Draft for a person to review and Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Tag stems by query

Use this command to give one exception feature to every stem that matches a query, instead of one intent per stem. It reports the count first: how many stems match, how many are tagged, and which polarity was chosen.

```sh
motif compose-tag-stems-by-query --project language.fwdata --draft tag-d-final \
  --intent '{"query":{"finalLetters":"d"},"exceptionFeature":"<feature-id>","gate":"rule"}'
```

`query` takes `category`, `finalLetters`, `hasFeature`, `lacksFeature` and `glossContains`. Give at least one; every one given must hold. The query reads each stem once, so its cost grows with the number of stems and does not depend on how many conditions you give. `exceptionFeature` must already be in the project's Exception Features list.

**Polarity.** The query selects the stems the rule or affix should treat as in the class. What FieldWorks can express decides which stems carry the tag:

- `"gate":"rule"`: a phonological rule can require a feature or exclude it. Motif tags the smaller of the matching stems and the other stems in scope, and says which: tag the matching stems and give the rule `requiredFeatures`, or tag the others and give it `excludedFeatures` (`compose-edit-phonological-rule-features`).
- `"gate":"affix"` (the default): an affix's From Exception Features only require a feature. Motif tags the matching stems even when the others are fewer, and says so in its output as a FieldWorks limitation. It adds no negative mechanism (ADR 0003).

`"action":"untag"` removes the feature from the matching stems that carry it. A stem already in the wanted state is skipped, so the command can be repeated.

The command stages operations in a Draft and does not change the saved FieldWorks project. Dry Run and Trial the Proposal on stems that should and should not take the rule, then Finalize it for a person to review and Apply.

entries.title: Show project settings
entries.description: Reads the project's Assessment scopes and settings, including declared gate word sets. Use it to see the limits and policies Motif will use for later Trials and Autonomous Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Show project settings

`config show` reads the named Assessment scopes and related settings stored beside one FieldWorks project.

## When to use it

Use it before measuring when you want to confirm which Assessor, Assessment kinds, or resource limits a named scope selects. A scope provides context for an Assessment; it does not gate whether two measurements can be compared. The Default Selection's parsing limits are saved separately; use [selection show](cmd:selection%20show) to read them.

## Example

```powershell
motif config show --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata"
```

## What it prints

The command prints the saved project settings, or their structured form when `--json` is supplied. It reads configuration and does not run PanGloss.

Each Assessment scope's `timing-detail-words` limits the number of costliest words whose individual object timings are stored. The default is 2,000 and the allowed range is 0–10,000. Set it in `<project>.motif.toml` beside the project, for example:

```toml
[[scope]]
name = "default"
timing-detail-words = 1000
```

Motif keeps the newest 20 standalone Assessments per kind, as well as Assessments needed by current or cited evidence. To change the count, add this project setting:

```toml
[retention]
standalone-assessments-per-kind = 20
```

## Set a parser work limit for the project

A word that needs more parser work than the limit stops, and a Trial reports it as capped, so the gate cannot measure it. To give every parse the same higher limit, add this project setting:

```toml
[parser]
work-limit = 60000000
```

The value is a positive whole number or `unbounded`. Trial, Assess and the Trial an Apply runs all use it. The order is the same everywhere: an explicit `--parser-work-limit` flag, then the limit a saved Default Selection or the scope itself carries, then the project's `[parser] work-limit`, then the default of 20,000,000 work units. A Selection or scope limit equal to the default of 20,000,000 counts as unset, because a Selection saved without a limit stores the default; the project's `[parser] work-limit` then applies. A Selection limit that differs from the default always beats the project setting, so a Selection cannot pin exactly 20,000,000 against a project limit. An invalid setting is refused with `config.invalid` on Trial and Assess as well as on trace. `parse --trace`, `trace` and `why-lost` pass the limit to PanGloss as `--work-cap`: the frozen limit of the Trial they explain when there is one, otherwise the limit a Trial would freeze now, and they say which. A value that is not a positive whole number or `unbounded` is refused with `config.invalid`, naming the line. `config show --json` reports it as `parserWorkLimit`, and a Trial and its evidence export report the limit that measured their words.

## Declare an Autonomous Apply gate

Add this to `<project>.motif.toml`, beside the project, to require the saved Selection named Gold words:

```toml
[gate]
word-sets = ["gold"]

[[review-word-set]]
id = "gold"
name = "Gold words"
role = "regression"
selection = "Gold words"
```

Save that Selection before running a Trial. To use a review word-set JSONL manifest instead, replace `selection` with `manifest = "gold.jsonl"`; relative paths resolve beside the TOML file. The list must be nonempty and name distinct declared review sets. An absent `[gate]` refuses Autonomous Apply with `apply.gate-undeclared`; it does not imply a default gate. `config show --json` reports the required ids as `gateWordSets` when declared and omits that field otherwise.

Required sets are measured even with `trial --review-set none`. The Trial freezes their source, membership, expectation and policy digests. Autonomous Apply requires complete measurement and the current declaration; changing a Selection, manifest or policy requires a fresh Trial.

The gate reuses these existing settings:

```toml
[gain-gate]
mode = "advisory"
min-attested-per-object = 1.5

[parsimony]
block-on = []
```

Gain modes are `off`, `advisory` (default) and `hold`. `hold` keeps a declared gate from being green below the threshold. Added phonological rules and affix processes are exempt. Parsimony blocks only opted-in measures: `R-word-disapproved-produced`, `R-word-negative-accepted`, and `P-variant-same-shape`. Missing required measurement remains unmeasured. A person's Apply keeps its existing Readiness checks.

## Related commands

- [Measure a Selection](cmd:assess) uses the configured scope when one is named.
- [Show the Default Selection](cmd:selection%20show) reads the project's usual word list.
- [Set Selection limits](cmd:selection%20set-limits) changes its parser work limit or time policy.

entries.title: List Corpora
entries.description: Lists the Corpora and their recorded provenance. Use it to find a Corpus id before adding or inspecting a Document.
entries.helpPage:
# List Corpora

`corpora` lists the Corpora recorded for a FieldWorks project with their provenance summaries.

## When to use it

Use this to find a Corpus id before inspecting it or adding a Document. A Corpus is material Motif holds with provenance; it is not a Text inside the FieldWorks project.

## Example

```powershell
motif corpora --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --json
```

## What it prints

Human output lists the recorded Corpora. JSON returns their ids and descriptive details for scripts that need to select one.

## Related commands

- [Describe a Corpus](cmd:add-corpus) records a new Corpus.
- [Show a Corpus](cmd:show-corpus) reads one Corpus in detail.

entries.title: Measure word type coverage
entries.description: Reads a lane ledger, its sidecar and a pinned frequency list and reports where every word type stands (Expected, Unverified, Disposition, Open or Lost), what is still Open by mechanism, and the three Done tests. It reads and never writes, takes saved checks and dispositions from the Motif store, and is not the report verb's coverage kind, the share of words the parser analysed.
entries.helpPage:
# Measure word type coverage

`coverage` answers whether a lane is Done. It reads a lane ledger TSV, its sidecar JSON and the pinned frequency list, joins them by word type, and reports where every type stands, what is still Open, and the three Done tests. It reads and never writes. The MCP tool `motif_coverage` takes the same fields in camelCase.

This is not `report --kind coverage`, which is the share of a scope's words the parser analysed, measured from one stored Assessment. `coverage` counts word types against a ledger and asks whether each one is accounted for: parsed and expected, set aside with a disposition, or Open.

## Example

```text
motif coverage --project <fwdata> --ledger ledger.tsv --sidecar ledger.meta.json --frequency accept-dev.tsv --json
```

- `--ledger`, `--sidecar` and `--frequency` are required. `--frequency-format tsv|tsv-header|json` names the list's shape; a `.json` file is read as a word-to-count object and anything else as two tab-separated columns.
- The project's Motif store, when it exists, adds its saved checks and its word type dispositions. A type with a current check at the ledger's grammar revision is proved; the rest carry the ledger's state and are counted as stale.
- `--audit-dir` and `--protected` name the frozen audit sample and protected set that the Correct and Stable tests read; without them those tests are unmeasured.
- `--limit N` caps `open.ranked`, 50 by default and at most 200. `--tokens` adds `tokenShare`, the share of eligible tokens carried by Open singletons; it is absent otherwise.

## What it prints

`done.verdict` is `fail` when any of `accounted`, `correct` and `stable` fails, `pass` when all pass, and `unmeasured` otherwise; each test lists its `reasons` and `counts`, such as `recurring-open-current`. `byState` gives types and tokens per state, split into `current` and `stale`. `open.byMechanism` groups Open types by the ledger row's class, keeping the 20 heaviest by type count; `open.mechanismTotal` counts every mechanism and `open.otherMechanisms` sums the ones cut (absent when none were), and `open.ranked` lists the heaviest recurring Open types. A malformed ledger, sidecar or frequency list is refused with a `coverage.*` code that names the file and a next step and, for a ledger row, its line number. An `--audit-dir` or `--protected` path that does not exist is refused with `coverage.file-unreadable`; leave the flag out to leave that check unmeasured.

## Related commands

- [Read an Assessment report](cmd:report) with `--kind coverage` is the share of words the parser analysed.
- [Give word types a disposition](cmd:wordform%20dispose) records the dispositions this command counts as accounted for.

`current get` reads the Current chapter of each Source from this machine's local file (`scripture-local.json`, per user, never synced). Each row carries where that chapter sits against the Source's Context. Nothing set is a normal, empty answer.

## Example

entries.title: Delete a closed Proposal
entries.description: Deletes a declined, superseded or withdrawn Proposal that never applied, with its Trials. An applied Proposal is never deleted.
entries.helpPage:
# Delete a closed Proposal

`delete --proposal` deletes a declined, superseded or withdrawn Proposal that never applied, together with its [Trials](term:trial).

## When to use it

Use it to clear away Proposals nobody will apply. An applied Proposal is final: it is never deleted, and its Receipts are kept. A Proposal that is still open, or is being tried, is refused. A Proposal that a saved phonology Example Set cites is refused with `proposal.retained-by-example-set`; the set keeps the Proposal's evidence, so it stays until the set is gone. A Proposal whose Trial results are still pinned, kept as current evidence, or cited by another Proposal's report is refused with `proposal.evidence-retained`, and nothing is removed; release the pin or the report, then delete it again.

## Example

```powershell
motif delete --proposal <id> --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --json
```

## What it prints

The deleted Proposal's id and how many Trials were removed with it. In the window, a closed card on **Proposals** offers **Delete** for the same.

## Related commands

- [List Proposals](cmd:proposals) lists closed Proposals with `--include-set-aside`.

entries.title: Compare a Trial with decisions
entries.description: Compares a completed Trial's parses with the approved, disapproved and misspelled decisions FieldWorks records for one Text, and saves the result. It reads stored evidence, runs no parser and never blocks an Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Compare a Trial with decisions

`difference produce` compares what the parser did with a [Trial](term:trial) against the decisions FieldWorks already records for one Text: approved and disapproved analyses, and words marked as misspelled. It saves the result, so later reads do not depend on the Trial's working files.

Pass the Proposal with `--proposal`, the Text with `--text` and, optionally, a specific completed Trial with `--job`. Without `--job` the newest completed Trial is used. The command reads stored evidence only; it does not run the parser. If the project was captured again after the Trial, it refuses with `difference.baseline-changed` because the recorded decisions may no longer be the ones the Trial was measured against. Trial the Proposal again.

Each word is placed in one state before and after the Proposal: no parse, parse without an approved match, approved match with alternatives, or one approved match. A word with no approved decision shows only how its parses changed. Words that gained, lost or changed readings, or that gained a misspelling or a disapproved reading, are listed as could be bad. Words that gained an approved match or lost a disapproved or misspelled parse are listed as improved. These are advice: they never decide whether a Proposal can be applied.

Every word is counted, but only words that changed or fall in a category are saved as rows, and each before and after pair, category and limitation keeps its best 100 words, those with the most places in the Text first and the spelling breaking a tie. Each saved word keeps at most 10 of its places, the first in reading order; the word's count of places is always the whole Text's. A word that did not change and is in no category is counted and not listed, so the saved comparison stays a few megabytes however long the Text is. `difference show` says how many words are counted but not listed.

By default the decisions are the ones people made in FieldWorks. With `--reference source-validated` the parses are read instead against the decisions a named program staged from cited sources through Applied Proposals. They are not a person's decisions, and the summary says so. If staged agents disagree about an analysis, the word is marked `conflicting-decisions` and neither opinion counts as approved. A typo or ill-formed record makes a word form count as incorrect for this reference only; a person's spelling decision is never changed. Each listed word names the evidence tier and agent behind it; `evidence show` gives the full record. A Proposal keeps one comparison per Text and reference, so a comparison against each sits beside the other; producing again replaces only the one for the same Text and reference.

Only Applied Proposals count; the compared Proposal's own staged decisions never do. An Applied Proposal that cannot be read is named in a warning and left out, and the rest still count. The MCP surface offers this reference only through the `motif_difference_produce_source_validated` tool of the opt-in `source-validated` profile; `motif_difference_produce` always compares with people's decisions.

A token in the Text is counted as unmatched, never guessed, when it cannot be tied to exactly one measured word.

Running the command again for the same Trial, Text and reference returns the saved one, unless the saved word rows can no longer be read, in which case it makes the comparison again; a different Trial replaces it, and comparisons for other Texts or the other reference are left alone. The saved summary names the parser, grammar, Selection and tokeniser of both sides, so it stays readable after the Assessments behind it are removed. A parser or tokeniser that differs between the two sides is shown as a warning, not a refusal.

Once the Proposal is applied, rejected, withdrawn, superseded or deferred, the word list is deleted and only the small summary stays. For an applied, rejected, withdrawn or superseded Proposal the command then returns the saved summary, and refuses with `difference.proposal-decided` if there is none for that Trial. A deferred Proposal is set aside rather than decided, so the command makes the comparison again, which brings its words back until the Proposal next changes status.

```powershell
motif difference produce --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --proposal <proposalId> --text <textGuid> --json
```

entries.title: Read a saved comparison
entries.description: Reads a saved comparison of a Trial with FieldWorks' recorded decisions: totals, a before and after table and a page of changed words. Filter to words that could be bad, to one category, to one approval state or to one limitation, and page through one word's places in the Text. Every word is counted, but only changed or categorised words are listed: each count keeps its best 100 words and each word its first 10 places, and the response says how many are counted but not listed (WordsListed, Listed).
entries.helpPage:
# Read a saved comparison

`difference show` reads a comparison saved by `difference produce`. It always starts with the totals, the before and after table and the count of words in each category, then lists one page of words.

Choose the comparison with `--difference`, or give `--proposal` to read that Proposal's newest. A Proposal keeps one comparison per Text and reference, so add `--text` (a Text GUID) and `--reference human|source-validated` to read a particular one; they are refused without `--proposal`. The output says which Text and reference the comparison belongs to, and lists the Proposal's other saved comparisons the same way, newest first and at most 50 (the JSON has `Saved` and `SavedTotal`). A saved comparison whose stored summary can no longer be read is left out of that list and counted, with a line saying how many could not be read (`SavedUnreadable` in the JSON) and one line naming each by Text, reference and time (`SavedDamaged`), and the others still show. When every saved comparison of the Proposal is damaged, the command refuses with `difference.unreadable` and names each one by Text, reference and time instead of saying there is none; `difference produce` for one of them makes it again. Without `--difference`, the newest comparison that can be read is shown even when a newer one is damaged; `difference produce` for that Text and reference replaces the damaged one. Narrow the words with `--could-be-bad`, `--bucket` (a category code such as `delta.regression` or `delta.improved.unique`), `--before` and `--after` (an approval state such as `approved-unique`, `approved-with-alternatives`, `no-approved-match` or `no-parse`). Use `--limitation` to list only the words one side of which a limit held back (a code such as `capped`, `timed-out`, `projection-unavailable` or `parser-refused`); a word counts for a limitation that touched either side, as the totals do. Page with `--offset` and `--limit`; the default page holds 25 words and the maximum is 200.

A comparison counts every word of the Text but lists only the words that changed or fall in a category, and each before and after pair, category and limitation keeps its best 100 words, those with the most places in the Text first. A word kept by one group counts as listed in all of its groups, so a count can list more than 100 words. The totals, the table and the category counts are always the whole Text's. Where a list is cut, the output says how many words are listed and how many are counted but not listed (`WordsListed` on the response and `Listed` on each count in the JSON; a comparison saved before these existed lists every word). A count of words that are counted but not listed is never an empty list. A word that did not change and falls in no category is only counted. A listed word keeps at most 10 of its places, the first in reading order (line, then position in the line).

Give `--word` to list one exact word together with the places in the Text where it occurs, a page at a time: `--occurrence-offset` and `--occurrence-limit` (default 25, maximum 200), which are refused without `--word`. Each place has the Text, the line, the line's number and the word's position in the line. The places are word detail, so they are kept only while the Proposal is undecided and not deferred. A word with more than 10 places lists only the first 10: `Total` is how many places it has in the Text, `Listed` (in the JSON; absent when every place is listed) is how many can be paged, and the output says how many are counted but not listed. Paging stops at the listed places, and the rest of them are found in the Text itself.

When the Proposal has been applied, rejected, withdrawn, superseded or deferred, the word list is no longer kept; for a deferred Proposal, `difference produce` makes the comparison again to see the words. The command still succeeds: it shows the summary, no words, and says that word detail is no longer kept. In the JSON, `WordDetailKept` is `false`.

If the saved words of a comparison cannot be read, for example because their stored rows were damaged, the command still shows the summary, lists no words and says that the word detail cannot be read. In the JSON, `WordDetailKept` is `false` and `WordDetailUnreadable` is `true`. Run `difference produce` for the same Text and reference to make the comparison again.

Categories are advice about parses and recorded decisions. A word with no recorded approval shows only that its parses changed, and a search that did not finish never proves that a reading disappeared.

```powershell
motif difference show --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --proposal <proposalId> --could-be-bad --json
```

entries.title: List word type dispositions
entries.description: Lists the word types that have a disposition in key order, with how many stand in each category, by page and optionally for one category. It reads and never writes.
entries.helpPage:
# List word type dispositions

`disposition list` lists the word types that have a standing disposition, in word type key order, with the category and evidence of each and how many types stand in every category. It reads Motif's store and never writes. The MCP tool `motif_disposition_list` takes `category`, `limit` and `page`.

## Example

```text
motif disposition list --project <fwdata> --as name --limit 100 --page 2
motif disposition list --project <fwdata> --format json
```

- `--as <category>` keeps one category: `name`, `loan`, `other-language`, `abbreviation`, `numeral`, `non-word` or `misspelling`. The counts by category always cover the whole store.
- `--limit N` is the number per page, 50 by default and at most 200. `--page N` reads the next page, starting at 1; the output says when more pages exist.
- `--format table|json` (or `--json`) chooses the output.

## Related commands

- [Show a word type's disposition](cmd:disposition%20show) shows one type with its history.
- [Give word types a disposition](cmd:wordform%20dispose) records one.

entries.title: Show a word type's disposition
entries.description: Shows the disposition a word type stands under, who recorded it and why, and the dispositions it had before. It reads and never writes.
entries.helpPage:
# Show a word type's disposition

`disposition show` reports the disposition a corpus word type stands under, who recorded it, when, and the evidence, then the dispositions it had before and how each ended (`replaced` or `cleared`). A type with no disposition answers with none. It reads Motif's store and never writes. The MCP tool `motif_disposition_show` takes `form`.

## Example

```text
motif disposition show Nairobi --project <fwdata>
motif disposition show Nairobi --project <fwdata> --json
```

The `scope` in the JSON is always `word-wide`: a disposition covers every occurrence of the type, and none is kept for a single occurrence. Spellings that differ only in Unicode composition are one type.

## Related commands

- [Give word types a disposition](cmd:wordform%20dispose) records one.
- [List word type dispositions](cmd:disposition%20list) pages through all of them.

entries.title: Dry Run a Proposal
entries.description: Queues a Dry Run of a Draft or finalized Proposal on a throwaway copy of its Baseline. Its effects are bound to that content and project state.
entries.helpPage:
# Dry Run a Proposal

Queues a Dry Run of a Draft or finalized Proposal on a throwaway copy of its Baseline. Its effects are bound to that content and project state. Read the summary, revise the Draft when needed, then Trial it before Finalize.

With `--wait`, Motif prints operation counts by kind, the number of effects, warnings and the Baseline's semantic project hash when available. It writes the complete effects list under the project's worker-root `artifacts/effects` folder. Add `--effects` to print that list in the terminal too. `--json` keeps the full `operations` and `effects` arrays and adds an `effectsSummary` object.

## Usage

```text
motif dry-run --project <fwdata> <proposalId> --wait [--wait-terminal] [--wait-timeout-ms <ms>] [--effects] [--json]
```

After Motif's own Apply, the next Dry Run captures a new Baseline by itself, so no step is needed. After a save made outside Motif, such as one from FieldWorks, a Dry Run is refused with `change.refresh-required` until you capture a new Baseline with `motif baseline capture` (in the window, Refresh). The evidence it would give is otherwise about a project that no longer exists.

Add `--wait-terminal` to cancel this Dry Run at the wait limit or on Ctrl+C. Motif allows up to eight more seconds to record cancellation and confirm cleanup. The refusal includes the job ID, the last observed status and whether cleanup was confirmed.

With an ordinary wait, poll a job that is still running with `motif jobs show <jobId> --project <fwdata> --json`, using the returned job id. See [jobs show](cmd:jobs%20show).


The summary shows at most ten warnings, each limited to 240 characters, with total and omitted counts. Complete warnings remain in the effects list. Effects files expire after seven days; a per-project 64 MiB budget may remove files older than one day sooner.

## Foreground-only

`--no-background` (MCP `no_background`) needs `--wait`. The Dry Run itself runs on the job runner, but no Parsimony Baseline bundle job is queued around it, so nothing commits after the command returns.

The default wait is 120 seconds (`--wait-timeout-ms 120000`). When it expires the job keeps running, and the command exits with code 3 and the `job.wait-timeout` refusal, which is not a failed Dry Run: its `jobId` fact names the job, and `motif jobs wait <jobId> --project <fwdata> --wait-timeout-ms <ms>` resumes the wait.

entries.title: Read a Dry Run
entries.description: Waits for a Draft or finalized Proposal's Dry Run and prints operation counts, warnings, the Baseline hash and the effects-file path. Add --effects for the full terminal list; --json keeps the full operations and effects arrays with an effectsSummary.
entries.helpPage:
# Read a Dry Run

Waits for the Dry Run of a Draft or finalized Proposal and reads its effects. Content and Baseline identify whether the evidence remains current.

Add `--wait-terminal` to cancel the exact job when the wait deadline expires and return after its execution has stopped. The timeout refusal reports the terminal job status.

entries.title: Export decision evidence
entries.description: Writes every source-validated decision's evidence as one JSON file, or to standard output, read a page at a time so a large store stays out of memory. An agent reads the same records page by page with a cursor. It changes nothing.
entries.helpPage:
# Export decision evidence

`evidence export` writes the evidence behind every decision that programs staged from cited sources through Applied Proposals. It reads Motif's store only: the FieldWorks project is not opened and nothing is changed.

Give `--out` a file path to write one JSON file, or leave it out to send the same JSON to standard output. The file holds a `format` name, then every record under `rows`, then `total` and `tierCounts`, which come last because they are counted as the records are written. Each record is labelled source-validated and is never a person's decision. Narrow the export with `--tier` (for example `misspelled-typo`).

The export reads a page at a time, 500 records by default, so a large store does not fill memory; `--page-size` (1 to 500) changes the page and never the result. A file is written beside its final name and moved into place only when the whole export succeeded, so a refused export leaves an earlier file as it was. Standard output cannot be taken back: if a read fails part way, the error is reported and the output is incomplete.

An agent reads the same records through the evidence export tool, one page at a time (50 records unless it asks for up to 500): each page returns a `next` cursor to pass as `after` until `next` is absent. A cursor remembers the tier filter and how many Applied Proposals there were, so it is refused if you change the tier or if a Proposal is applied part way through; start the export again.

```powershell
motif evidence export --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --out "C:\Work\koro-evidence.json" --tier misspelled-typo
```

entries.title: List decision evidence
entries.description: Lists source-validated decisions staged by Applied Proposals, with a count for each tier first and then one page of records. Filter to one tier.
entries.helpPage:
# List decision evidence

`evidence list` lists the decisions programs staged from cited sources through Applied Proposals. It starts with how many records each tier holds, then shows one page of records.

Narrow the list with `--tier` (for example `misspelled-typo`). Page with `--offset` and `--limit`; the default page holds 50 records and the maximum is 500. Each record is labelled source-validated and is never a person's decision.

```powershell
motif evidence list --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --tier misspelled-typo --json
```

entries.title: Read decision evidence
entries.description: Reads why a program, not a person, decided about one wordform or analysis: its tier, the cited sources, the named non-human agent and the Proposal that staged it. It never shows a person's decision as source-validated.
entries.helpPage:
# Read decision evidence

`evidence show` reads the evidence Motif kept for one wordform or analysis whose decision a program staged from cited sources. Give the identity of the wordform or analysis after the command name.

Each record names its tier (for example `source-approved`, `misspelled-typo` or `ill-formed`), the sources it cites, the facts that tier requires, and the Proposal that staged it. When the record supports an approval or disapproval, it also names the non-human agent that decided and the source release it stands for. Every record is labelled source-validated and is never a person's decision: people's approvals, disapprovals and spelling marks stay as FieldWorks holds them.

The records come from Applied Proposals, as they were staged. If a person later changed the decision in FieldWorks, the record still shows what was staged.

```powershell
motif evidence show <wordformOrAnalysisId> --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --json
```

entries.title: Finalize a Proposal
entries.description: Finalizes a Draft as an immutable Proposal revision for a person to review. The Draft needs both a short label and a Rationale. Evidence for unchanged content on the same Baseline remains current.
entries.helpPage:
# Finalize a Proposal

Finalizes a Draft as an immutable Proposal revision for a person to review. Evidence for unchanged content on the same Baseline remains current.

The Draft must have both a short label and a Rationale before it can be finalized. If either is missing, set the label with `motif label` or the Rationale with [`proposal rationale`](cmd:proposal%20rationale), then retry Finalize. Finalize also refuses a Rationale with findings, and lists them with their lines and columns. When the Rationale links to the project and the Baseline cannot be read to check it, Finalize refuses until it can.

entries.title: Find a composer
entries.description: Finds the composing commands that fit a goal in a linguist's words, or lists every composer that serves a Subject. Each result gives its title, when to use it, its Subjects and its intent schema; detailed adds a worked example and the Subject's page. Reads only; nothing is staged.
entries.helpPage:
# Find a composer

Finds the composing commands that fit a goal in a linguist's words, or lists every composer that serves a Subject. Reads only; nothing is staged and no project is opened.

Give exactly one of a goal or a Subject.

```sh
motif find-composer --goal "add a plural suffix to nouns"
motif find-composer --subject affix-slots-and-templates --detail detailed
```

`--goal` takes a few words and returns at most five composers, best first. Words are matched against each composer's example goals, its title and its description, and against the titles of the Subjects it serves. `--subject` takes a Subject id and returns every composer that serves it, ordered by command name.

A goal that no composer covers is not answered with a weak list. The rule has two steps. First, every Subject, including the reserved ones (infixation, reduplication, example sentences, grammar explanation, and outside authoring for exports, imports, counts, recordings and the like), has a list of distinctive terms; if the Subject whose terms the goal names most is a reserved one, including on a tie, the answer is no match with that Subject as the nearest.
