`parsimony --group grammar|text|all` runs a whole group of Parsimony measures in one job, waits, and returns one stored Report per measure. The Grammar group reads the grammar alone and just works: when the project has no current Baseline it captures one first, and it never recaptures an existing one. The Text group reads the saved Parsimony Selection.

## Groups

- `grammar` has twelve measures that need only the grammar: duplicate ad hoc prohibitions, duplicate allomorph forms, subsumed allomorph forms, duplicate lexical entries, duplicate environments, environments made only of literal segments, exception features with few carriers, glosses that only repeat the entry form, stems with no part of speech, unused statements, unconditioned allomorphs and allomorph alternation families.
- `text` has the measures that read Approved analyses of the chosen Texts, plus the two parser-tier measures, which also need a ParseTime Assessment.
- `all` runs both. With no saved Parsimony Selection it runs the Grammar group and says once how to set the other up.

## Example

```powershell
motif parsimony --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --group grammar --json
motif selection set-parsimony --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --name Texts --texts <guid>,<guid>
motif parsimony --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --group all --json
```

The Parsimony Selection is saved once and reused on every later run; `selection show` lists it beside the Default Selection. Name one measure of the group with `--measure` to run only that measure. `--evidence-scope` is not used with `--group`. Use `--wait-timeout-ms` to set the wait bound. Press Ctrl-C while waiting to cancel the job.

## Related commands

- [Review grammar parsimony](cmd:parsimony) queues a single measure without waiting.
- [Save the Parsimony Selection](cmd:selection%20set-parsimony) chooses the Texts the Text group reads.
- [Read a Parsimony Report](cmd:parsimony%20show) opens one stored result.

entries.title: Run every Parsimony measure
entries.description: Runs every Parsimony measure this build supports in one job over one verified evidence bundle, then waits and returns one stored Report per measure. It does not capture a Baseline or require an Assessment.
entries.helpPage:
# Run every Parsimony measure

`parsimony --measure all --wait` runs every Parsimony measure this build supports in one job and waits for the result. The job copies the current Baseline, has PanGloss import it and write grammar facts, builds and verifies the evidence once, and stores one Report per measure on that one bundle.

## Example

```powershell
motif parsimony --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --measure all --wait --json
```

The JSON answer lists the job id, the shared bundle id, and every stored Report in measure order. Each Report is the same Report `parsimony show` reads, so a later page or command reads them one by one without running PanGloss again. Fourteen separate runs would verify the same evidence fourteen times; this runs the checks over one verified copy.

Capture a Baseline first. Use `--wait-timeout-ms` to set the wait bound; omit `--wait` to receive the queued job id. The job reports the stage it is in, which `jobs show` prints while it runs. Press Ctrl-C while waiting to cancel the job; a cancelled job stores no Report.

## Weekly sweep

Add `--trend <file.tsv>` to append one row per counted class (date, class, eligible objects, findings) after the run. The rows come from the counts the stored Reports already hold, so the trend costs a few rows of work and runs no extra parse. The file gets a header the first time.

Motif installs no scheduled task. To run the sweep weekly, schedule the same command yourself, for example a Windows Task Scheduler weekly trigger that runs `motif parsimony --project "<fwdata>" --measure all --wait --trend "<folder>\parsimony-trend.tsv"`, or on Linux or macOS a crontab line `0 6 * * 1 motif parsimony --project "<fwdata>" --measure all --wait --trend "<folder>/parsimony-trend.tsv"`. Capture a Baseline first when the project has none current.

`--measure all` applies to a Baseline review only. With `--dry-run`, name one measure.

## Related commands

- [Review grammar parsimony](cmd:parsimony) queues a single measure without waiting.
- [Read a Parsimony Report](cmd:parsimony%20show) opens one stored result.
- [List Parsimony measures](cmd:parsimony%20measures) shows registered checks and views.

entries.title: Check a batch for same-shape additions
entries.description: Reads a compose-batch intents file and reports groups of five or more variants that share one shape and have no recorded rule try. It reads the current Baseline only and runs no parse.
entries.helpPage:
# Check a batch for same-shape additions

`parsimony --rule-attempts --plan <intents.json>` reads the intents file you would give `compose-batch` and groups the variants it adds by shape. A shape is the variant type, the environments and the spelling change from the main form, such as a lost final vowel. Five or more variants of one shape need a recorded rule attempt: the rule you tried, its prediction test, and why it failed. Without one, the check reports the group.

## Example

```powershell
motif parsimony --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --rule-attempts --plan ".\variants.json" --json
```

The answer lists each group of five or more with its shape, its size and whether an attempt is on record. It reads the intents and the main entries' forms from the current Baseline. It runs no parse and changes nothing.

The check is advice. It holds a package only when the project opts in, in `<project>.motif.toml`:

```toml
[parsimony]
block-on = ["P-variant-same-shape"]
```

A hold clears when the hypothesis ledger holds a passed or failed hypothesis on the shape: record it with `hypothesis add --change "<shape key from the report>"` (or the correspondence, such as `V>@final`), test it, and decide it.

The same finding appears in the Trial review summary. An opted-in hold keeps a [declared Autonomous Apply gate](cmd:config%20show) from being green. A person's Apply keeps its existing Readiness checks.

## Related commands

- [Review grammar parsimony](cmd:parsimony) queues a single measure without waiting.
- [Run every Parsimony measure](cmd:parsimony%20--measure%20all%20--wait) includes the variant-shape count.

entries.title: Wait for a Parsimony Report
entries.description: Queues the requested Parsimony measure and waits for its stored Report. It does not capture a Baseline or require an Assessment.
entries.helpPage:
# Wait for a Parsimony Report

`parsimony --wait` queues the requested measure over the current Baseline and waits for its stored Report.

## Example

```powershell
motif parsimony --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --measure P-statement-unused --wait --json
```

Capture a Baseline first. PanGloss imports that Baseline to create grammar facts; showing the completed Report later does not run PanGloss.

Use `--wait-timeout-ms` to set the wait bound. Omit `--wait` to receive the queued job id.

## Related commands

- [Review grammar parsimony](cmd:parsimony) queues the same review without waiting.
- [Read a Parsimony Report](cmd:parsimony%20show) opens a stored result.
- [List Parsimony measures](cmd:parsimony%20measures) shows registered checks and views.

entries.title: Stage a finding ruling
entries.description: Stages a keep, fix, ask, or defer decision from one finding in a stored Parsimony Report. It derives the exact subject and evidence from that finding and appends the existing Notebook operations to a Draft Proposal. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Stage a finding ruling

```sh
motif parsimony dispose --project language.fwdata --report <reportId> --finding <findingId> \
  --disposition keep|fix|ask|defer --record-type <portableId> --draft <name> \
  [--reason <text>] [--question <text>] [--json]
```

This command reads one finding from a stored Parsimony Report and derives its exact subject, evidence digest, evidence contract, and readable captions. The Report must belong to the project's current Baseline; a Report measured just before an Apply can still answer that its decision is already recorded, but it cannot stage a new one. `--record-type` must be a portable ID from `parsimony record-types`. Supply `--question` only with `--disposition ask`.

The command appends the existing Notebook judgment operations to a Draft Proposal. Review them with Dry Run, then a person uses `apply` to write the judgment to FieldWorks. When the bound Dry Run shows only these Notebook effects, Readiness does not require a Correctness Assessment because the judgment cannot change parsing. A mixed Proposal keeps the normal Assessment requirement. A pending keep does not suppress a current finding.

The same decision is never staged twice. Two rulings are the same decision when they agree on the finding's subject, measure and evidence, the ruling, the reason and the question; the record type, and the Report and the Draft they came from, do not count.

- If the saved project already holds this decision as its current judgment, the command succeeds and stages nothing. It prints `This decision is already recorded; nothing was staged in draft '<name>'.`, and with `--json` the response's `outcome` is `already-recorded` and its operation list is empty.
- If the Draft already stages this decision, the command is refused with `parsimony.decision-already-staged`: `This decision is already staged in Draft '<name>'.`
- If the finding ID names more than one finding in the Report, the command is refused with `parsimony.finding-ambiguous` and stages nothing, because no single finding can be disposed.

entries.title: Read Parsimony expectations
entries.description: Reads human-confirmed negatives and native Approved and Disapproved readings from the saved FieldWorks project. The versioned projection keeps surface negatives, exact reading negatives, and native Opinions separate for later Parsimony measures and paired verification.
entries.helpPage:
# Read Parsimony expectations

```sh
motif parsimony expectations --project language.fwdata [--json]
```

Reads the saved project's `parsimony-expectations/v1` projection. It lists human-confirmed [reviewed negatives](term:reviewed-negative) by case and revision, then reports FieldWorks' default-human Approved and Disapproved readings in separate sections. Native Disapproved Opinions reject one exact reading and do not become whole-word negatives.

Conflicts and unavailable identities are included in `issues`; callers must not count them as qualified evidence. This command reads the FieldWorks project and does not run PanGloss or change it.

entries.title: Find the newest Report
entries.description: Names the newest stored Parsimony Report and the bundle it was measured from. It reads the project's store only and does not run PanGloss.
entries.helpPage:
# Find the newest Report

`parsimony latest` names the newest stored Parsimony Report for a project and the bundle it was measured from. It reads the project's store only and does not invoke PanGloss.

## Example

```powershell
motif parsimony latest --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --json
```

The response returns `reportId` and `bundleId`. Pass the Report id to [Read a Parsimony Report](cmd:parsimony%20show) to read its findings.

When the project has no Parsimony Report yet, the command is refused with `parsimony.no-report`. A stored Report that cannot be read is refused with `parsimony.report-damaged`.

## Related commands

- [Review grammar parsimony](cmd:parsimony) creates a Parsimony Report.
- [Read a Parsimony Report](cmd:parsimony%20show) reads one by id.

entries.title: Confirm a reviewed negative
entries.description: Confirms a forbidden surface form or exact reading as a human and stages its Notebook record in a Draft Proposal. A negative may have no grammar owner; only Apply writes it to the FieldWorks project.
entries.helpPage:
# Confirm a reviewed negative

```sh
motif parsimony negative confirm --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '<closed intent JSON>' \
  --confirm "I confirm this form or reading is forbidden in the stated context." [--json]
```

This HumanOnly command stages a human-confirmed surface or exact reading negative as Notebook operations in a Draft Proposal. Supply the Notebook `recordTypeId`, stable `caseId`, vernacular `writingSystem`, `form`, `context`, and a `target` with discriminator `"type":"surface"` or `"type":"reading"`. A reading target carries an ordered `morphs` array; each `identity` names the exact `form`, `msa`, and optional `inflType` portable IDs. `wordformId` and `analysisId` are optional, so the negative can exist without a wordform or grammar owner. `reason`, human actor fields, timestamp, and source `reportId` are optional.

Example surface target:

```json
{
  "recordTypeId": "record-type/<22-character-base64url-id>",
  "caseId": "case_0000000000000000000002",
  "writingSystem": "qaa",
  "form": "example",
  "context": "the stated environment",
  "target": { "kind": "surface" }
}
```

The command appends the existing Notebook create, description, and reserved-field operations to the Draft. Review the Draft with `dry-run`, then a person uses `apply` to save the judgment in FieldWorks. Until Apply succeeds, the negative is not part of the saved project. Run `parsimony expectations` to read it back.
usage: Usage: motif parsimony negative confirm --project <fwdata> --draft <name> --intent '<closed intent JSON>' --confirm "I confirm this form or reading is forbidden in the stated context." [--json]

entries.title: Retract a reviewed negative
entries.description: Withdraws a reviewed negative by naming its exact current revision heads and stages a retraction in a Draft Proposal. The Notebook history remains in the FieldWorks project, and only Apply records the withdrawal.
entries.helpPage:
# Retract a reviewed negative

```sh
motif parsimony negative retract --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --intent '<closed retraction JSON>' \
  --confirm "I confirm this reviewed negative should be withdrawn." [--json]
```

This HumanOnly command stages a retraction revision for a saved reviewed negative. The closed intent names the Notebook `recordTypeId`, `judgmentId`, and every current `expectedHeads` entry as a revision ID and content digest; the composer refuses stale heads. An optional `reason`, human actor, and explicit UTC timestamp can record why the judgment was withdrawn.

The command appends the retraction's Notebook operations to a Draft Proposal and preserves the earlier revisions. Review the Draft with `dry-run`, then a person uses `apply` to save the retraction in FieldWorks. Run `parsimony expectations` to confirm the negative is no longer effective.
usage: Usage: motif parsimony negative retract --project <fwdata> --draft <name> --intent '<closed retraction JSON>' --confirm "I confirm this reviewed negative should be withdrawn." [--json]

```sh
motif parsimony record-types --project language.fwdata [--json]
```

Lists the saved record types in the project's Notebook with each type's portable ID and readable name. Choose a type by its ID; Motif never picks one by English name.

entries.title: Read a retirement review
entries.description: Reads the review state for one staged rule-based allomorph retirement Draft. It returns its latest matching Dry Run and names evidence that is not available yet; it never invents a finding or parser result.

entries.title: Retract a ruling
entries.description: Stages a withdrawal of a saved Parsimony ruling using its exact current Notebook heads and digests. The history stays in FieldWorks, and the finding returns to Active after a person Applies the current retraction.
entries.helpPage:
# Retract a ruling

```sh
motif parsimony retract <recordId> --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --expected-heads '[{"revisionId":"<portableId>","contentDigest":"sha256:<64 lowercase hex>"}]' [--json]
```

Use the `recordId` of a current ruling record. `--expected-heads` must name every current head and its exact digest; include both heads to resolve a conflict. Motif refuses a stale digest, a superseded record, or a record from another project.

Retraction appends a new Notebook record and retains the earlier judgment history. It stages an agent-attributed Draft Proposal; a person must Apply it. After the retraction is applied and current, refresh the project evidence to see the finding return to Active.
usage: Usage: motif parsimony retract <recordId> --project <fwdata> --draft <name> --expected-heads '<revisionId and contentDigest JSON array>' [--json]

entries.title: Revise a ruling
entries.description: Stages a revision to a saved Parsimony ruling using its exact current Notebook heads and digests. The revision keeps the same finding subject and evidence, and only a person can Apply it.
entries.helpPage:
# Revise a ruling

```sh
motif parsimony revise <recordId> --project language.fwdata --draft <name> \
  --expected-heads '[{"revisionId":"<portableId>","contentDigest":"sha256:<64 lowercase hex>"}]' \
  --disposition keep|fix|ask|defer [--reason <text> | --clear-reason] [--question <text>] [--json]
```

Use the `recordId` of a current ruling record. `--expected-heads` must name every current head and its exact digest; include both heads to resolve a conflict. Motif refuses a stale digest, a superseded record, or a record from another project.

The revision appends a Notebook record and preserves the finding's subject and evidence binding. Supply a reason to replace it, use `--clear-reason` to remove it, or omit both to preserve it. `ask` requires `--question`; other choices must omit it. This command stages an agent-attributed Draft Proposal. Review it with Dry Run and Preflight; only a person can Apply it.
usage: Usage: motif parsimony revise <recordId> --project <fwdata> --draft <name> --expected-heads '<revisionId and contentDigest JSON array>' --disposition keep|fix|ask|defer [--reason <text> | --clear-reason] [--question <text>] [--json]

entries.title: Read a Parsimony Report
entries.description: Reads a stored Parsimony Report by id. It uses the saved Report and does not run PanGloss.
entries.helpPage:
# Read a Parsimony Report

`parsimony show` reads a previously stored Parsimony Report by id. It reads the saved Report and does not invoke PanGloss.

## Example

```powershell
motif parsimony show --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" <reportId> --json
```

The response returns the Report id, its frozen Baseline and artifact identities, its Assessment references, findings, and rendered text.
A check that could not look appears as a note: an information line in the rendered text and in `notes`, never a finding. A Report also lists authored grammar settings the parser ignores, as information only.

## Related commands

- [Review grammar parsimony](cmd:parsimony) creates a Parsimony Report.

entries.title: Read a Proposal's Parsimony status
entries.description: Says whether Parsimony has measured a Proposal's candidate after its Trial: not set up, not yet run, queued, running, ready, stale or failed, with a Grammar group and a Text group. It reads stored jobs and Reports only and never starts a run. Parsimony is advisory and never changes the Trial, Readiness or Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Read a Proposal's Parsimony status

`parsimony status` says whether Parsimony has compared a Proposal's candidate grammar with the Baseline. A committed Trial queues that comparison on its own, behind all other work, so the answer is usually "queued", "running" or "ready" without anyone asking for it.

The overall state is one of `not-set-up` (PanGloss is missing), `not-yet-run`, `queued`, `running`, `ready`, `stale` (an input changed since the run, with the reasons listed) or `failed` (with a plain category such as `timed-out` for a very large grammar). The Grammar group runs every time. The Text group needs a saved Parsimony Selection and reports `not-set-up` until there is one.

Parsimony is advisory. A failed, timed-out or cancelled run never changes the Trial, Readiness or Apply, and there is no single score: each measure reports its own new, resolved, unchanged and changed-evidence findings. This command reads stored jobs and Reports and never starts a parse.

## Example

```powershell
motif parsimony status --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --proposal proposal/AbCd --json
```

## Timeouts and freshness

When PanGloss ran past its time limit on a grammar, Motif does not queue another automatic run for the same Baseline and PanGloss; the status reads `failed` with category `timed-out`. Run `motif parsimony` by hand to try again. A new Baseline or a new PanGloss clears this by itself.

A `ready` status was checked against the Baseline, the Proposal, its prerequisites, PanGloss and the measures. A changed human judgment or Parsimony Selection is not checked.

## Related commands

- [Review grammar parsimony](cmd:parsimony) runs a measure or group by hand.
- [Show a Parsimony Report](cmd:parsimony%20show) reads a stored Report.

entries.title: Read a Parsimony view
entries.description: Reads a bounded page from a fixed view over one frozen bundle. Parser views use a Report id to bind the exact Assessment references; filters and cursors are bound to the bundle. Only the declared view filters are accepted.
entries.helpPage:
# Read a Parsimony view

`parsimony view` reads one page from a fixed, documented evidence view in a published bundle. The cursor is bound to the bundle, view, and filters; the command accepts no SQL and does not build missing artifacts. Supply the Report id when reading parser cases so Motif can restore the exact Assessment references.

Use `--report <reportId>` with `parsimony-active-findings`, `parsimony-suppressed` or `parsimony-suppression-history` to compare saved judgments with that exact Report and show evidence freshness. Active and suppressed finding rows include the current head IDs and `contentDigest` values; include every head for the same `judgmentId` when revising or retracting a conflict. Suppression-history rows include each revision's `contentDigest` as well, and every row names its judgment by `visibleId` (for example `MJ-7K3Q-9XDF`) and `recordTitle`, which match the Notebook record. `unresolved-judgment` rows list records that need a look: a `check` of `hash-failed` means "hash failed on this record entry" and the judgment does not suppress its finding, and a `state` of `warning` means an edited ID or sentence that still applies. Narrow those views with `--measure-id`, `--disposition`, `--state`, `--search` or `--subject-key`.

The `environment-excess` and `natural-class-excess` views cap each name list at 30 names when read whole, and list every name when you pass `--object-id`; each row's `totals` give the full count of every list.

## Example

```powershell
motif parsimony view allomorph-context --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --bundle <bundle-id> --object-id <allomorph-guid> --json
```

Read parser outcomes from the Report that named their Assessment:

```powershell
motif parsimony view parser-cases --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --bundle <bundle-id> --report <report-id> --json
```

Use `parsimony measures` to list view codes and their required inputs. A view with missing facts or Assessment material reports that capability as unavailable rather than returning an empty result.

## Related commands

- [List Parsimony measures](cmd:parsimony%20measures) lists registered checks and views.
- [Read a Parsimony Report](cmd:parsimony%20show) opens stored findings.
usage: Usage: motif parsimony view <view-code> --project <fwdata> --bundle <id> [--object-id <guid> | --category-id <guid> | --statement-kind environment|natural-class] [--scope project-approved|default-selection] [--case-key <key>] [--report <id>] [--measure-id <id>] [--disposition keep|defer|fix|ask] [--state <state>] [--search <text>] [--subject-key <key>] [--cursor <cursor>] [--limit <n>] [--json]

entries.title: Check phonology examples
entries.description: Queues an advisory check of one saved Example Set revision against the current Baseline's grammar and records the result as an Assessment. It never changes the FieldWorks project, Readiness or Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Check phonology examples

`phonology-examples check` queues an advisory check of one saved Example Set revision against the grammar in the project's current [Baseline](term:baseline). For each example it asks PanGloss to generate surface forms from the underlying form in the example's declared context and reports whether the expected form was observed. A check never changes the FieldWorks project, never changes Readiness, and Apply ignores it.

## When to use it

Use this after saving examples with a cited source, to see whether the grammar as captured produces the forms you expect, and which rules applied. A result is `agree` when an expected form was observed, `disagree` when the search completed without it, and `unavailable` when nothing usable was measured (for example no parser, an empty lexicon, or a context that names no entry). Unavailable is never a pass.

## Example

```powershell
motif phonology-examples check --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" <revisionId> --wait --json
motif jobs assessments --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" <jobId> --json
```

## What it prints

The id of the queued job. With `--wait` it waits for the job to finish and prints the job's status. The job records one Assessment of kind `PhonologyExamples`; `jobs assessments` gives its id, and [phonology-examples results](cmd:phonology-examples%20results) reads it. `--work-cap` and `--timeout-ms` bound the whole check. If no Baseline has been captured the command is refused; if the Baseline changes before the job runs, the job fails and the check must be requested again.

## Related commands

- [Save phonology examples](cmd:phonology-examples%20save) records the revision this command checks.
- [Read phonology check results](cmd:phonology-examples%20results) reads the stored result.

entries.title: List phonology examples
entries.description: Lists the current revision of each saved advisory phonology Example Set in stable order. Use the returned cursor to read another page.
entries.helpPage:
# List phonology examples

`phonology-examples list` reads the current revision of each saved phonology Example Set from the project's Motif store. Example Sets are advisory evidence and do not affect Readiness or Apply.

## When to use it

Use this to find a set and its current revision before reading or revising it. The command reads stored headers and does not capture the FieldWorks project or run PanGloss.

## Example

```powershell
motif phonology-examples list --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --json
```

## What it prints

Each item gives the set name, current revision id, and example count. A response with a continuation cursor has another page; pass that cursor as JSON with `--continuation`.

## Related commands

- [Save phonology examples](cmd:phonology-examples%20save) creates a new set or advances one at its exact current revision.
- [Show a saved phonology revision](cmd:phonology-examples%20show) reads the complete examples a page at a time.

entries.title: Read phonology check results
entries.description: Reads the stored result of one advisory phonology check as a page of per-example summaries or one complete example. It reads stored evidence without capturing a project or running PanGloss.
entries.helpPage:
# Read phonology check results

`phonology-examples results` reads the stored result of one phonology check: a page of per-example summaries, or one complete example. A check is advisory evidence about a saved Example Set against a [Baseline](term:baseline); it never changes Readiness and Apply ignores it.

## When to use it

Use this after a check has finished to see, for each example, whether the expected surface form was `agree` (observed), `disagree` (a completed search without it) or `unavailable` (no usable measurement, such as a missing parser or lexical context). Unavailable is never a pass. The command reads stored rows only: it does not capture the project or run PanGloss.

## Example

```powershell
motif phonology-examples results --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" <assessmentId> --json
motif phonology-examples results --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" <assessmentId> --example front-vowel --json
```

## What it prints

A page lists each example with its disposition, completion, observed form and how many rules applied, in authored order. A response with a continuation cursor has another page; pass that cursor as JSON with `--continuation`. A summary lists at most 32 applied rule ids and says how many it left out. `--example <id>` prints the complete retained example with every ordered, visited and applied rule, and `--out <path.json>` also writes that JSON to a file. `--example` cannot be combined with `--page-size` or `--continuation`.

## Related commands

- [Show a saved phonology revision](cmd:phonology-examples%20show) reads the examples a check measured.
- [List saved phonology examples](cmd:phonology-examples%20list) finds each set's current revision.

entries.title: Save phonology examples
entries.description: Saves underlying forms, expected surface forms and their context, with optional citations, as an immutable advisory Example Set revision. Saving does not change the FieldWorks project.
entries.helpPage:
# Save phonology examples

`phonology-examples save` records underlying forms, expected surface forms and the grammar context for each example as an immutable revision, with an optional citation on each. A saved set is advisory evidence: it never changes Readiness and Apply ignores it. Saving does not change the FieldWorks project.

## When to use it

Use this to keep a set of underlying forms and expected surface forms, with their sources, next to the project. To revise a set, save it again with its exact current revision id as `expectedRevisionId`.

## Example

Create a UTF-8 JSON file with a `name` and an `examples` array. Each example has an `id`, `underlying`, one or more `expected` forms, and a `context` tagged with `kind`. An optional `citation` has a `source` and `locator`.

```json
{
  "name": "Vowel harmony",
  "examples": [
    {
      "id": "front-vowel",
      "underlying": "a-ku",
      "expected": ["e-ki"],
      "context": {"kind": "hcXmlEntry", "entryId": "entry-17"},
      "citation": {"source": "Field notes", "locator": "example 12"}
    }
  ]
}
```

Then save it:

```powershell
motif phonology-examples save --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --file examples.json --json
```

## What is checked

An example whose context is a FieldWorks entry (`entryGuid` and `msaGuid`) is checked against the project's current Baseline, by reading the Baseline's saved project file. The entry must exist, and the stem MSA must belong to that entry. If one does not, nothing is saved and the refusal `phonology-examples.entry-not-found` names the example ids and the GUIDs that were not found, up to ten, with a count of the rest.

An example whose context is an HC XML entry id (`hcXmlEntry`) is not checked against FieldWorks: those ids belong to a grammar export, not to the project.

If the project has no Baseline yet, the set is still saved, because authoring examples before capturing a Baseline is a normal order of work. The response then says `not-verified-no-baseline`, and the check command will report any entry it cannot find as unavailable. A Baseline file that is missing or unreadable gives `not-verified-baseline-file-missing` the same way.

## What it prints

The response names the saved set and revision, including its executable and cited revision digests, and an `entryVerification` value: `verified` when every FieldWorks entry was found in the Baseline, `not-applicable` when no example names a FieldWorks entry, or `not-verified-no-baseline` and `not-verified-baseline-file-missing` when the check could not run. A citation-only edit creates a new cited revision while leaving the executable digest unchanged.

## Related commands

- [List saved phonology examples](cmd:phonology-examples%20list) shows each set's current revision.
- [Show a saved phonology revision](cmd:phonology-examples%20show) reads its examples and citations.

entries.title: Show phonology examples
entries.description: Reads a bounded page from one exact saved Example Set revision, including its citations. It reads stored evidence without capturing a project or running PanGloss.
entries.helpPage:
# Show phonology examples

`phonology-examples show` reads one exact saved revision and returns its examples in authored order, including source context and any citations. Example Sets are advisory evidence and do not affect Readiness or Apply.

## When to use it

Use this to inspect a current or historical revision. The command reads Motif's stored rows and does not capture the project or run PanGloss.

## Example

```powershell
motif phonology-examples show --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" <revisionId> --json
```

## What it prints

Each example includes its underlying form, expected forms, generation context, and optional citation. A continuation cursor marks another page; pass that cursor as JSON with `--continuation`.

## Related commands

- [List phonology examples](cmd:phonology-examples%20list) finds the current revision of each set.
- [Save phonology examples](cmd:phonology-examples%20save) records a new immutable revision.

entries.title: Read Progress
entries.description: Counts approved and misspelled places in saved Texts, or eligible places in an indexed Source. Source approval counts are unavailable; read a summary or page through Passages.

entries.title: Prepare a project for Motif
entries.description: Creates Motif's reserved human judgment field in a FieldWorks project after explicit confirmation. It does not add a judgment or create a writing system.
entries.helpPage:
# Initialize a project

Prepare a FieldWorks project to hold human judgments about Parsimony recommendations. Motif creates two reserved Notebook fields, one for the judgment data and one for its visible ID, and saves them in the project after you confirm.

```text
motif project initialize --project <fwdata> --confirm "Initialize this project to work with Motif Proposals?" [--json]
```

This command is available in the CLI and is never exposed as an MCP tool. The confirmation text must match exactly. Initialization does not create a judgment, a Notebook record, a Proposal, or a writing system.

The project must have an analysis writing system. If Motif finds an incompatible or duplicate definition with a reserved name, resolve it deliberately in FieldWorks and run initialization again. Motif does not rename or repair an existing definition.

A project that still has the older single field named `MotifHumanJudgment` is refused: delete Motif's test/demo judgment records and that field in FieldWorks, then initialize again. Motif does not convert old records.

Motif keeps a byte-checked recovery copy of the original project before it saves. Motif cannot undo a save, so the project is recoverable from that copy. If Motif cannot establish whether the save completed, the refusal names the recovery copy and gives the restore step: Close FieldWorks, then copy the recovery copy over the project file. Motif never restores the project by itself. A successful run that keeps a copy names it but gives no restore step, because restoring would undo the initialization. Inspect the saved project before you restore or retry.
usage: Usage: motif project initialize --project <fwdata> --confirm "Initialize this project to work with Motif Proposals?" [--json]

entries.title: Read a project tag
entries.description: Reads the tag Motif stores for this project on this machine. When its vernacular language code is already used, Motif tries the exact folder name and refuses if that choice is invalid or taken.
entries.helpPage:
# Read a project tag

Read the tag Motif stores for this project on this machine. For a project without a tag, Motif uses its vernacular language code when that code is available. If the code is already used, Motif tries the exact folder name and refuses if that name is invalid or taken.

```text
motif project tag --project <fwdata>
```

Use `--json` to receive the tag as structured output. If Motif cannot choose a valid, unused tag, choose one with `project tag --set`.

entries.title: Set a project tag
entries.description: Chooses the tag Motif stores for this project on this machine. The tag must follow the lowercase rules and be unused by every other Known project.
entries.helpPage:
# Set a project tag

Choose the tag Motif stores for this project on this machine. A tag starts with a lowercase letter, uses lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, contains at most ten characters, and must be unused by every other Known project.

```text
motif project tag --set cebu --project <fwdata>
```

Use `--json` to receive the saved tag as structured output. The new tag remains in place when Motif records the project again.

entries.title: Add a Proposal Comment
entries.description: Adds a Comment to an open Proposal, in Markdown. A person or an assistant may add one; an assistant says what it calls itself, and the Comment shows as author for person.
entries.helpPage:
# Add a Comment to a Proposal

Adds a Comment to an open Proposal, in FieldWorks Markdown. A person or an assistant may add one; an assistant says what it calls itself with `--author`.

## Example

```text
motif proposal comment add <proposalId> --project <fwdata> --text "Please keep the second gloss"
motif proposal comment add <proposalId> --project <fwdata> --file comment.md --author "Claude (Opus 5.5)"
```

Give the full Proposal id. Without `--author` the Comment is the person's; `--person` names the person, and defaults to the computer's user name. An author label and a person name hold at most 100 characters, and a Comment shows as "author for person". The label is only a label: Motif does not check it, and nothing depends on it.

A Comment is checked as a [Rationale](cmd:proposal%20rationale) is, and the findings are returned, but it is always saved, and its findings never stop a Proposal being finalized or applied.

A Comment stays outside the Proposal's changes and remembers which content it was written for. It can be added until the Proposal is applied, declined, withdrawn or superseded; reopening the Proposal allows Comments again. When a person's Comment is newer than the [Rationale](cmd:proposal%20rationale), `show` reports `commentsChanged`, and an assistant is told to read it.

entries.title: Delete a Proposal Comment
entries.description: Deletes a Comment from an open Proposal. Only a person deletes a Comment.
entries.helpPage:
# Delete a Comment on a Proposal

Deletes a Comment from an open Proposal. Only a person deletes a Comment; an assistant cannot.

## Example

```text
motif proposal comment delete <proposalId> <commentId> --project <fwdata>
```

Give the full Proposal id and the Comment number that `show` lists. A deleted Comment is gone. Comments cannot change once the Proposal is applied, declined, withdrawn or superseded.

entries.title: Edit a Proposal Comment
entries.description: Replaces the text of a Comment on an open Proposal. Only a person edits a Comment; it then shows that it was edited, and when.
entries.helpPage:
# Edit a Comment on a Proposal

Replaces the text of a Comment on an open Proposal. Only a person edits a Comment; an assistant cannot.

## Example

```text
motif proposal comment edit <proposalId> <commentId> --project <fwdata> --text "Keep the second gloss, drop the third"
motif proposal comment edit <proposalId> <commentId> --project <fwdata> --file comment.md
```

Give the full Proposal id and the Comment number that `show` lists. The Comment then shows that it was edited, and when; the earlier text is not kept. A Comment cannot be empty: [delete it](cmd:proposal%20comment%20delete) instead. Comments cannot change once the Proposal is applied, declined, withdrawn or superseded.

entries.title: Compare Proposals
entries.description: Compares two to eight Proposals side by side from each one's Trial before and after and by the approved analyses each keeps and loses. It reads retained Trial evidence and the project's approved analyses and measures nothing.
entries.helpPage:
# Compare Proposals

Run `motif proposal compare <proposalId> <proposalId> [...] --project <fwdata> --json` to see two to eight Proposals side by side. The MCP tool `motif_proposal_compare` takes `project`, `proposalIds`, `at`, `jobs`, `snapshot` and `page`.

This compares each Proposal's own Trial before and after, and the approved analyses each Proposal keeps and loses. Each Proposal uses its newest completed Trial (newest by creation time; equal times go to the greater job ID) and the evidence that Trial retained, or the Trial you pin with `--job <jobId>` (repeat it once per Proposal; MCP `jobs`), so the call measures nothing, starts no Trial and applies nothing.

The summary names each Proposal and counts of forms that gained a Reading, lost a Reading, were unchanged, were not measured and stopped early. A form a Trial did not measure on both sides is counted as not measured, never as unchanged, and an incomplete Trial makes the comparison incomplete with a typed limitation. Use `--page 1` for the form rows, 100 to a page, with diverging forms first. Each row has one cell per Proposal in request order, with the Reading IDs gained and lost. Forms are joined on writing system, form key and Reading ID.

Approved analyses are the ones the project's default user agent approves, read from the Baseline the Trials were measured on. An approved analysis counts as **kept** by a Proposal when its word's Trial after side has a Reading that is the same Reading apart from sense and does not choose a different sense: it resolves the approved sense or lists it among its candidates. It counts as **lost** when the before side yielded it and the after side no longer does, and both sides finished. An approved analysis the before side did not yield is never lost; if the after side yields it, it counts as kept, and if neither does it is in neither count. Approved analyses on forms a Trial did not measure count nowhere. Each approved analysis counts once per Proposal even when its word has forms in several writing systems; if it is kept for one form and lost for another, it counts as kept. Each column has `approvedKept` and `approvedLost`, and each row cell has `approvedKeptIds` and `approvedLostIds`, the approved Readings' IDs. `approvedSkippedOtherAgents` counts analyses approved only by a human agent other than the default user agent; they are not counted as approved and the comparison is incomplete with the typed limitation `approved-other-agents`.

`approvedTotal` is every analysis the default user agent approves in the Baseline. `approvedUncounted` is how many of them no column counts: the analysis has no Reading identity (no morph bundles, or a bundle that does not verify), or no Trial measured its word on both sides. A non-zero `approvedUncounted` makes the comparison incomplete with the typed limitation `approved-uncounted`, so a missing approval never reads as kept or lost.

A Trial that no longer matches its Proposal's current content, or whose Proposal is no longer stored, carries `trial-stale`. A Proposal with a newer Trial attempt than the one compared that did not fail or get cancelled (including a pinned older Trial), or one that has been superseded by another Proposal, carries `trial-superseded`. When the PanGloss version differs between a Trial's before and after sides, or between the Trials, the limitation `parser-version-differs` names the versions in `detail`. Each of these makes the comparison incomplete.

`--snapshot` is checked against the Trials a page reads, so it needs `--page`. Page reads of one snapshot reuse the form join the first read built in the same process instead of rebuilding it.

All Trials must have been measured on one Baseline. Different Baselines refuse with `proposal.compare-baseline-mismatch` and name each Baseline. If that Baseline is no longer retained, or its approved analyses cannot be read, the call refuses with `hand-analysis.snapshot-expired` or `hand-analysis.index-unavailable`. `--at <digest>` requires each Trial to match that Baseline digest or its own Proposal revision, else `proposal.compare-at-mismatch`. A Proposal with no completed Trial refuses with `proposal.compare-trial-missing`.

entries.title: Write a Proposal's Rationale
entries.description: Writes or replaces what a Proposal changes and why, in Markdown. The Rationale stays outside the Proposal's content, so rewriting it never changes what the Proposal does, and it can be rewritten until the Proposal is applied or closed.
entries.helpPage:
# Write a Proposal's Rationale

Writes or replaces a Proposal's Rationale: what the Proposal changes and why, in FieldWorks Markdown. Whoever builds the Proposal, usually an assistant, writes it.

## Example

```text
motif proposal rationale <proposalId> --project <fwdata> --text "Plural -s was missing from the noun template"
motif proposal rationale <proposalId> --project <fwdata> --file rationale.md
motif proposal rationale <proposalId> --project <fwdata> --text "..." --author "Claude (Opus 5.5)"
```

Give the full Proposal id, the one `new` or `proposals` returned; a name or a prefix is refused. A Draft that has never been finalized has a Proposal id too, so write the Rationale before [`finalize`](cmd:finalize), which refuses a Proposal without one.

The Rationale is kept apart from the Proposal's changes, so rewriting it never changes what the Proposal does. It remembers which content it was written for: after the Proposal changes, the person sees it marked out of date, and a rewrite clears that mark. It can be rewritten until the Proposal is applied or closed, and it holds at most 64 KiB.

The Rationale is checked when it is written. Unmarked text is the project's default analysis writing system, and links, writing systems and styles are checked against the current Baseline. The findings are only what a reader would see as wrong: markup that does not read, a link to something not in the project, an unknown writing system or style, a list with no blank line before it, or a numbered list that does not start at 1. A code span in backticks is plain text, never a finding: write a word or morpheme of the language as `[form]{.v}`, or `[form]{ws=code}` for another writing system, so it links to its writing system. The Rationale is saved as written; when it is clean, line endings and trailing space at its end are tidied and a link written as a path gains its `guid=`. A Draft's Rationale with findings is saved as written and the findings are returned, but [`finalize`](cmd:finalize) refuses it until they are fixed. Once the Proposal is Ready, a Rationale with findings is refused and the last clean one stays.

If the person left a [Comment](cmd:proposal%20comment%20add), a new Rationale is one answer to it. `--author` says what an assistant calls itself, as it does for a Comment; each rewrite is kept, with its author, until the Proposal is decided.

entries.title: Review a Proposal's changes
entries.description: Lists every change in one Proposal in the order to read them: grammar changes first, then word changes. Each entry says whether it has been looked at, and the list carries the Proposal's latest Trial.
entries.helpPage:
# Review a Proposal's changes

`motif proposal review` prints one Proposal's changes as a single list, in the order a person reads them. Grammar changes come first, a change that others depend on before the changes that depend on it; word changes follow.

## When to use it

Use it to see what a Proposal would do before you try or apply it. The Proposal's document in **Proposals** shows the same list. Without `--proposal` it reads the pending changes.

## Example

```text
motif proposal review --project <project> --proposal <id> --json
```

## What it prints

Each entry has a title, the operations it owns, what it depends on, and `lookedAt`. An entry counts as looked at only while neither the entry nor the Trial it was judged against has changed. Looking at an entry is attention, not approval: applying never requires it. The response also carries the latest Trial and whether its Correctness evidence permits Apply.

## Related commands

See [Apply one Proposal](cmd:apply%20--proposal) to write a reviewed Proposal, and [Apply pending changes](cmd:apply%20--all-pending) for the pending changes.

entries.title: Read a Trial report
entries.description: Reads the saved report of a Proposal's Trial: red flags, incomplete cases, named losses, stopped words with their causes and second-reading holds. It reads stored evidence and does not rerun the parser.
entries.helpPage:
# Read a Trial report

`proposal trial` reads the saved report of a Proposal's Trial: observed red flags, incomplete cases, counts and stopped words. It reads stored evidence, does not rerun the parser, and needs no developer setting.

```powershell
motif proposal trial --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" <proposalId> --json
```

Use `--job` or `--report` to pick a particular Trial or saved report, and `--detail failures` or `--detail full` for more of its cases. [Trial a Proposal](cmd:trial) describes every selector.

With no selector, the command reads the newest Trial job for this Proposal, even if it failed or was cancelled. The Autonomous Apply gate uses the same job. Use `--latest` by itself to read the job ID, status and, when saved, `reportId` and `reportDigest` without expanding the report. This live identity response is bounded to 2 KiB in JSON, including the MCP success envelope. An identity above the limit is refused. A Proposal with no Trial returns a "no Trial" result that names the command to start one.

A report is current when it belongs to the newest completed Trial, its Proposal and Baseline identities match, and the active parser executable matches both checkpoint digests. A known parser mismatch marks it historical. A missing or unlaunchable parser, or a missing checkpoint pin, leaves freshness unknown unless another check establishes staleness. An exact report read keeps its saved ID, digest and gate verdict.

Every stopped word is retained in `report.stoppedWords` with its before or after side, reason codes and specific cause. The same cause appears on the word’s full review page when detail is available. An invalid shape means the parser could not segment the spelling with the phoneme inventory; inspect the recorded explanation before changing the grammar.

The stored result keeps its `gate` and `report.losses`: `newNoParseWords` and `newApprovedLossWords` name every affected word, and `newlyLostReadings` names each word and frozen reading identity. These lists survive when the optional detail index exceeds the store budget. For each word listed in `--expect-loss`, `newlyLostReadings` also carries one row per lost Reading with its canonical `signature` (ordered morphemes), the lost copy `count` and `remainingReadingCount` (lexicon-backed Readings still emitted); a word that lost every Reading lists them all with zero remaining. `losses.retirementAttestation` is bound to the report digest and its `complete` is true only when those rows cover the full retirement multiset of the waived words across every measured case; `limitations` says why not. The saved report keeps every retirement row; a read returns the rows filled to a 16 KB bound and `retirementAttestation.page`, `pageCount` and `rowCount` say how many exist, and `--page <N>` reads the others (`--report` pins the exact saved report). Nothing is refused for size. Rows with a `signature` (the retirement multiset) and rows without one (confirmed losses of frozen expectations) describe the same loss from two sides: a gate must read each kind on its own and must not sum across the two kinds. Expected losses are frozen when the Trial is queued; later reads keep that Trial’s verdict.

When a word had a Baseline analysis but its spelling cannot be segmented by the candidate phoneme inventory, the parser may mark it `skipped`. This is a named loss, including any confirmed readings it lost, rather than a pass or an unknown search result. Malformed evidence cannot establish that loss. A listed intended inventory loss is covered by the Trial's saved expected losses.

The summary names lost and regressed words in `report.regressions`: at most 10 per cause, each with its analyses before and after, then the count of the rest and the `nextStep` command that pages them all. Each word also carries the canonical entry, analysis and form ids of its analyses (`beforeReadings`, `afterReadings`), the commands that trace it at the Baseline and at this Proposal's Trial copy (`traceBaseline`, `traceTrial`, both `motif parse <word> --trace --at ...`), and `touchedBy`: the Proposal operations that name an object a Baseline analysis of the word uses. `touchedBy` is an overlap of ids, never a cause; an empty list says nothing about what caused the loss. To see what PanGloss recorded for a lost word, run `motif proposal why-lost <word> --proposal <id>` ([Why a word lost a Reading](cmd:proposal%20why-lost)). When the overlap could not be computed, `touchedBy` is null and a `regression-overlap-not-computed` Limitation says why.

A new second reading on an attested word is named in `report.heldWords` and keeps the gate unmeasured until independent approval and a fresh Trial. The held names survive the detail budget too. Observed stops with no morphology packet retain their producer outcome; undispatched cases receive no invented stop.

Older reports without compact gate facts are explicitly unmeasured. Use `--refresh-report` to rebuild from exact retained evidence, or rerun the Trial if those inputs are unavailable. Autonomous Apply requires a [declared gate](cmd:config%20show), its current required scope and policy, and a green newest Trial for the live project state.

entries.title: Read a Trial's Reading changes
entries.description: Lists the words a Trial lost, gained, changed or doubled by Reading signature, from the evidence the Trial already retained, and writes the expected-retired and expected-added manifests. It measures nothing.
entries.helpPage:
# Read a Trial's Reading changes

Run `motif proposal trial delta --project <fwdata> --job <jobId> --json`, or `--proposal <id>` for the newest completed Trial with retained evidence. It reads the evidence the Trial already retained, so it measures nothing and needs no second gate run.

The counts cover every measured form. Each class shows a page of rows ordered by spelling, with `--limit` (1 to 200) and `--offset` or `--page`:

- `lost`: parsed before the change and has no Reading after it.
- `gained`: had no Reading before and has one after.
- `changed`: parsed on both sides and the two sides share no Reading.
- `doubled`: keeps every old Reading and has more copies after.
- `stopped-negative`: a known non-word that parsed before and no longer does. It is an improvement, never lost. Ask for it with `--classes`.

Each row keeps `caseKey`, the id the report and regression rows use, and lists the retired and added Readings by signature id with a copy count and the signature as a manifest row writes it. Only lexicon-backed Readings count; guessed Readings do not.

`--write-manifests <dir>` writes `expect-retired.jsonl` and `expect-added.jsonl` there, one row per word and Reading: `{"word": ..., "signature": [...], "count": n}`. The format is the one the grammar lanes write, with the gate's own spellings: words are lower-cased and composed (`--keep-case` keeps them as measured), and ids the Proposal creates are renamed `created:N` in order of first appearance, as the gate renames them (`--alias-created false` keeps real ids). Name the directory; a bare `--write-manifests` is refused. Only the CLI writes files. Together they enumerate the whole delta: a lost word's Readings are in the retired file, and a known non-word that stopped parsing has no row. Review them before use; nothing is accepted automatically. The command refuses when any form was not measured on both sides or has a Reading without a complete identity, because a manifest must not leave part of the delta out. The summary reports Reading and word counts per entry, MSA and allomorph so a reviewer can check the swap names the expected objects.
usage: Usage: motif proposal trial delta --project <fwdata> (--job <jobId> | --proposal <id>) [--classes lost,gained,changed,doubled,stopped-negative] [--write-manifests <dir> [--alias-created true|false] [--keep-case]] [--limit <1-200>] [--offset <n> | --page <N>] [--json]

entries.title: Read a Trial export
entries.description: Finds the retained evidence file for an exact Trial job. The file contains the observed forms and Readings on both sides, the completion counts and the provenance used to measure the Trial.
entries.helpPage:
# Read a Trial export

Run `motif proposal trial export <jobId> --project <fwdata> --json` with the exact job ID from [Trial progress](cmd:trial%20--wait). Use `--at <digest>` to require its frozen Proposal revision, Baseline digest or saved report digest. The MCP tool `motif_proposal_trial_export` takes `project`, `jobId`, `at` and `page`.

The receipt gives the file's path, byte count, SHA-256, publication time, and counts for the Before and After sides. When the path is too long for the compact receipt, append the reported suffix to the paired store's path. Use `--page 1 --json` for the first 100 word cases and follow `nextPage` for more. Read the complete file for gate provenance, parser causes and ordered Readings. Each case keeps the configured set memberships and the explicit witness marker independently. That marker preserves the first submitted spelling and order after trimming, omitting blank lines and merging canonically equivalent spellings in NFD. Case distinctions are preserved.

Motif writes the complete file during Trial and retains it with the paired store through Assessment and review detail pruning. A Trial that predates retained exports needs a fresh measurement. The export is a historical read of the requested job, including interrupted jobs. Before Apply, resolve the newest Trial across all states, require completion, match its saved report ID and digest to the receipt, and check the parser executable pins for both sides. The file checksum verifies the exported bytes.

entries.title: Why a word lost a Reading
entries.description: Compares a word's parse at the Baseline with its parse on a Proposal's Trial copy and, for each lost Reading, reports the stop PanGloss recorded and the Proposal operations that overlap the earlier form it names. The overlap is not a cause; use it to find which edits to look at.
entries.helpPage:
# Why a word lost a Reading

`proposal why-lost <word> --proposal <id>` compares one word's parse at the Baseline with its parse on a Proposal's latest Trial copy, and says which Readings the Proposal lost. For each lost Reading it reports the stop PanGloss recorded and the Proposal operation that names the form PanGloss says blocked it. It changes nothing, and Motif runs no parser of its own: every cause is something PanGloss recorded. Both traces run under the work limit that Trial froze, and a note says which. A trace stops a word at the parser work limit, so a word that once traced to completion can now say "work limit reached" with its work count. To trace it further, raise the limit with `[parser] work-limit` in the project's `motif.toml` (see [Show the project configuration](cmd:config%20show)). The MCP tool `motif_why_lost` takes the same fields.

```powershell
motif proposal why-lost mirusi --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --proposal <id>
```

## What you get

- **Lost, gained and kept.** Both traces run under one parse lease, so they describe one project state. Readings are compared by the canonical ids of their morphs: entry, analysis and form.
- **A recorded stop.** When PanGloss recorded an `allomorph_blocked` stop on some Trial path that names a form the lost Reading uses, the answer names the blocked form and the earlier form that blocked it, with the form's written text where the Trial copy holds it.
- **Overlap, not cause.** The earlier form's id is joined to the Proposal's operations. An operation is listed when it creates the form, edits it, places a form beside it, adds a member to it, or names an object the form belongs to. That is an overlap of ids, not a recorded cause. If none does, the answer says so. The Baseline's describe is reported but only the Trial's decides whether a stop could be read.
- **Not recorded stays not recorded.** Where PanGloss recorded no stop for a lost Reading, the answer says `not-recorded` and names no operation. Motif never infers a cause. A PanGloss whose `--describe` does not list an `allomorph_blocked` stop gets the same answer, with that reason.
- **Which copy.** The answer names the Trial job whose copy it read. A later Trial of the same Proposal changes the copy.

## Bounds

`--max-paths` (1 to 64, default 64) caps the terminal paths read on each side. When paths or events were left out, a not-recorded answer says a stop may be among what was not read.

## When it refuses

It refuses a request it cannot compare, a Proposal with no Trial or whose Trial details were cleared, a project with no Baseline, and two traces whose grammar hashes do not compare, each with its own code and a sentence. Every refusal of [Explain a word's parse](cmd:parse) applies to either side.

## Related commands

- [Explain a word's parse](cmd:parse) shows where each candidate path of a word stopped on one side.
- [Why a word did not parse](cmd:why-not) asks PanGloss about morphs you expected.
- [Read a Trial report](cmd:proposal%20trial) lists the lost words this command explains.

entries.title: List Proposals
entries.description: Lists every Proposal with what it changes and the numbers its latest Trial measured beside today's. Proposals are grouped by what to do next; applied and set-aside ones are counted unless asked for.
entries.helpPage:
# List Proposals

`proposals` lists every Proposal in a project, grouped by what to do with it, with what each one changes and the numbers its latest [Trial](term:trial) measured beside today's.

## When to use it

Use it to see what is waiting for review, what needs another try, and which changes are your own and not yet applied. The Proposals page in the window reads the same list.

## Example

```powershell
motif proposals --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --json
motif proposals --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --include-set-aside --json
```

## What it prints

Each Proposal carries its label, status and group: **WaitingForYou** (a complete Trial matches the project and the Proposal as they are now), **NeedsAnotherTry** (the project or the Proposal moved since the Trial, or its latest Trial is running or did not finish), **NotTried** (no Trial exists), **NotAppliedYet** (your own collected changes) or **SetAside** (closed: applied, rejected, superseded or withdrawn). Closed Proposals are counted in `setAsideCount` and listed only with `--include-set-aside`. A deferred Proposal is still open and is grouped by its Trial like a proposed one.

A stored Proposal or Draft whose content cannot be read is left out of the list and named in `unreadable`, with its id, its label when it has one, its draft name when it is a Draft, and why. Motif does not change or delete it. The window says how many could not be read and names them.

A Proposal also lists its change kinds, such as two rules, one allomorph and one approved parse, and the ids of other Proposals that change one of the same words. Its Trial summary pairs five numbers, each as a value before and after: Text Coverage, approved words kept, approved words, parse time on this computer and the warning count. The Trial's parser work, in parser work against the Baseline, is reported beside them, and that is the figure to compare. The window shows it as **Work**, blank when the Trial cannot be compared with today's parse, and adds the time on this computer last. A Trial over only the touched words still pairs the totals: every word it did not measure keeps today's value. Chips count approved words the Trial lost and changes that no longer fit.

## Trying a Proposal again

In the window, **Try again** on a card measures the Proposal on a copy of the project. The copy is thrown away and your FieldWorks project is not changed. A card whose Trial is still running says **Trying…** and offers no second button.

## Related commands

- [Read the project Overview](cmd:overview) reads one Proposal's Trial with `--proposal`.
- [Delete a closed Proposal](cmd:delete%20--proposal) removes a closed Proposal that never applied.

entries.title: Query forms of a word list
entries.description: Reads a plain word list with no project and returns the words that satisfy a query expression, including phon(...) and env(...) patterns, which PanGloss evaluates against the grammar given by --grammar; unsegmentable words are counted and sampled, never dropped.
entries.helpPage:
# Query corpus forms

`motif query --corpus <words.tsv|weights.json|folder>[,<more>] forms where <expression>` (also `forms --where <expression>` or `forms --query-json <file|->`) lists the words of a plain word list that satisfy a query expression, with no project, Trial or parse. The corpus is read as for `query pairs`; the expression is the text form of `motif.query.v2`, over the columns `form`, `tokens`, `parse.state`, `shape`, `syllables`, `fold`, `initial:n` and `final:n`.

```powershell
motif query --corpus words.tsv forms where 'phon(Stop V Stop V)' --grammar project.fwdata
motif query --corpus texts/ forms --where 'env([V] / # _ Stop) and tokens > 2' --grammar project.fwdata --json
```

`phon` and `env` need `--grammar <path>`, the grammar file `pangloss serve` loads; PanGloss segments the words with its surface character table and names the natural classes. Without it they are refused with `query.phon-needs-grammar`. Rows come by token count then form, `--limit` (default 100) keeps the first; a cut says `TRUNCATED`. The header counts the words the grammar cannot segment and lists a sample; `--json` writes `motif.query.corpus-forms.v1` with each row's `matches`. See `query forms` for the pattern language.

`realizes(<morpheme>, attested)` finds the words that carry a morpheme in any surface form the grammar gives it. With `--grammar <path>`, PanGloss parses every word type of the corpus once with `batch --analyses --morph-spans` (PanGloss v0.34.0 or later; an older one is refused as `query.realizes-index-failed` with `needs-pangloss-v0.34.0`) and Motif keeps the result as a parse index under its cache folder (`SIL/Motif/cache/realizes-parse-index` in the user data folder), keyed by the grammar file, the corpus's word types and the PanGloss build; the first query writes "building parse index" to standard error and takes about a minute and a half on a large grammar, and later queries load the index in a few seconds. The index records, for each analysis, each morph's ids and the surface text PanGloss places it at, so a matching word gives the morpheme's own piece with nothing traced. A morph PanGloss could not place (a typed null such as `span_lost_by_rule`, `span_ambiguous_copy` or `compound_unsupported`), or whose spans do not add up to the word's surface, stands in as its whole word and the header says `piece_unplaced` or `piece_inconsistent`. With `--project <fwdata>`, Motif also reads that project's stored analyses (never writing it), and the forms from both sources are joined and labelled. The morpheme is `entry:msa` or one id (an analysis or form id), which need no project; a form such as `sfx:-an` (optionally led by `root:`, `pfx:` or `sfx:`) needs `--project` to name the entry.

The forms compile to one search over the words' surface text, anchored at the start for a prefix and the end for a suffix. The header says what was searched for, whether the set is complete, how many word types the parse index answered, how many pieces came from spans and how many words stand in whole, and that the search can over-match, because it reads characters and not the grammar's segments; each row names the forms it carries. A word the grammar cannot segment, a parse stopped at a limit, a word the batch gave no answer for and a missing or untrusted surface piece each make the set not complete, so `not realizes(...)` is refused as `query.realizes-negation-incomplete`. If PanGloss fails to parse the corpus, or what it wrote is malformed, the query is refused as `query.realizes-index-failed` with the error output or the line number. An unreadable cached index is deleted and rebuilt once, with a note on standard error, and the cache keeps the eight newest indexes. A morpheme found in no parsed word type is refused as `query.realizes-no-parses`. The tiers `possible` and `generated` parse and are refused as not yet available.

`realizes(<id>, possible)` asks PanGloss which phonological rules can change the morpheme (`effects`), drops the rules its form rules out, and lists "These N rules can change M" with each rule's environment. It searches the words for the written form and for every surface variant it can compute by applying the rule's replacement, and, for a rule it cannot apply by hand, for PanGloss's own pattern for the rule's target, narrowed to the morpheme's edge. The morpheme must be named by `entry:msa` ids and the grammar must be given (`--grammar` or `--project`). The set is not complete, and `not realizes(...)` is refused, when a rule is unknown, unprintable, non-local or a metathesis, or the written form is only part of the morpheme.

`realizes(<id>, generated)` picks real roots (or affixes, for a stem) from the project's lexicon whose edge satisfies each rule environment, two per environment (three with `--thorough`), plus a control that triggers nothing, generates the morpheme on each with PanGloss, and reads the morpheme's own piece of each surface from the engine's morph spans. Where the engine cannot place the morpheme, the whole word stands in, labelled `whole-word`. Each surface carries the rules that fired and the test root. An environment no real root satisfies is named as uncovered and the set is not complete.

## Readings, causes and retirement

With `--grammar <path>` the corpus is parsed once (the same cached parse index as `realizes`) and each word type gets its readings. Three things read them.

- `readings` is a number column: `forms where 'readings > 3'`. `parse.state` then comes from the parse, not the word list: `parsed`, `none`, `capped`, `timed-out`, `unsegmentable` or `failed`. Rows show the reading count.
- `--group-by cause` groups the matching words that have more than one reading by why, and returns `{groups:[{cause, detail?, benign, words, tokens, example:{word, readings:[{morphs:[{form, msa, text, entry, kind, gloss}]}]}}]}` (under `causes`). Each word gets its most specific cause, narrowest first: the structural kinds that any pair of its readings shows come first, then the kinds every differing pair must show, then the segmentation differences. In priority order: `lexicalised-vs-derived` (one reading has a single stem over a span another covers with a root plus derivational affixes), `same-morphs-reordered` (the same morphs in another order), `homophonous-affix` (readings differ only in inflectional affixes that spell the same but have different analyses, such as SM and OM; `benign:true`; a stem, a derivational affix or a morph of unknown class is never benign), `same-segmentation` (every reading cuts the word at the same places with the same text, and only the entry or analysis of some morphs differs; never benign; `detail` is `stems` for homograph roots, `affixes` when only affixes differ, `mixed` when both do or a class is unknown), `clitic-or-stem-split` (one reading has a single stem over a span another splits into several morphs, such as a stem and a clitic), `boundary-shift` (the same number of morphs cut at different places, or the same morphs at shifted spans), and `other`. A word with many homograph readings and one boundary-shifted reading is `boundary-shift`, the narrower claim. `--group-by cause` needs `--project <fwdata>` (or a `.fwdata` as `--grammar`): each morph then carries its entry, class and gloss, so a harmless homophone is told from a different root; without one it is refused with `query.readings-needs-project`.
- `only-via(entry:<guid>)` (JSON `{"only-via": {"entry": "<guid>"}}`) matches words that have a reading and whose every reading uses the morpheme; `msa:` and `form:` name an analysis or a form id. PanGloss's batch gives each morph its form and analysis ids but not its entry; an analysis belongs to exactly one entry, so `entry:` needs `--project` (or a `.fwdata` as `--grammar`) and is refused with `query.readings-needs-project` otherwise.
- `--what-if-retire <id>[,<id>...]` (ids as `entry:`, `msa:`, `form:` or a bare id) lists, for the matching words, `readings`, `readingsVia`, `readingsOther`, `lost` (every reading goes) and `reduced` (some stay), with type and token totals. It is an estimate read from the cached reading sets and is labelled `estimate: true`: confirm with a Trial. Words with a finished parse are counted in `affected`, `lost` and `reduced`, and a `reduced` word lists the readings that stay as `alternative`. A word whose parse was capped or timed out goes in its own `capped` count and a word the batch gave no answer for in `failed`, so the totals add up and nothing capped is called lost. An id that no morph of the parse carries (a bare entry id with no `--project`, a misspelt guid, an entry the project does not have) is refused with `query.retire-id-unknown`, never answered with zero. A morph whose analysis the project's lexicon lacks is counted in `readingsInfo.unknownMsa` and makes the result incomplete.

A word whose parse was capped, timed out or got no answer may have more readings than the grammar gives, so the header says `Readings: INCOMPLETE` and the JSON `readingsInfo.complete` is false; the counts are then lower bounds. `--group-by` and `--what-if-retire` need no `where`; with one they cover only the matching words, and `rows` still lists the matches.

## Several sources, groups, totals, samples and word files

- `--corpus` takes several sources as one corpus: repeat the flag or separate the paths with commas (a path that exists is never split). A source is a `.tsv` word list, a weights file (a `.json` file holding one object of form to whole-number count, such as `bible_h.weights.json`) or a folder of `.txt` files. The counts of a form are summed across the sources, so the corpus has each form once; with more than one source the header names each with its kind and its own type and token counts, and `corpus.sources` in the JSON carries them. `pairs` reads the same sources.
- `--group-by <column>[,<column>]` counts the types and tokens of every matching word per distinct value of one or two columns (`parse.state`, `readings`, `shape`, `syllables`, `fold`, `initial:n`, `final:n`, `tokens`, `form`) and returns `groups:{columns, groups:[{key, values, types, tokens}]}` with `totals:{types, tokens}`, groups by tokens then key. A word with no value in a column is keyed `(none)`; two columns key as `a | b`. `parse.state` and `readings` come from the grammar's parse when `--grammar` is given (`parsed`, `none`, `capped`, `timed-out`, `unsegmentable`, `failed`), and from the word list otherwise; `readings` needs `--grammar`. It needs no `where`; with one, only the matching words are counted. A grouping lists no rows unless `--limit` asks for some. `--group-by cause` is the separate readings grouping above and takes no other column.
- `--sum tokens` adds `totals:{types, tokens}` for the matching words without a grouping. Tokens are always counted in a grouping, so `--group-by parse.state --sum tokens` and `--group-by parse.state` give the same answer; `tokens` is the only sum.
- `--sample <n> [--seed <s>]` keeps n of the matching words, chosen by a hash of the seed and the form (default seed 0), so the same seed over the same matches gives the same words, whatever the corpus order or the frequencies; a smaller match set is kept whole, and a different seed draws a different set. `--limit` is a different thing: it shows the first rows by token count, the most frequent words, and is the way to see the top of the list. The sample is the rows (and the `--write-words` file) unless `--limit` is given; groups and totals still cover every match, and `matched` is the full count; the JSON says `sample:{count, seed, of}`.
- `--write-words <file> [--with-counts]` writes the matching words (or the sample), every one and not just the first `--limit`, one per line, or `form<TAB>count` with `--with-counts`, by tokens then form, in UTF-8 with no BOM. An existing file is never overwritten unless `--force` is given; without it the query is refused as `query.write-words-exists` and nothing is written. The file is written beside the target and moved into place, so a failure leaves no half-written file. The JSON says `written:{path, words, withCounts}`.

```powershell
# Tamil -க்காக, types and tokens, parsed against unparsed, in one command
motif query --corpus bible_h.weights.json --corpus bible_x.weights.json forms where 'form ~ ".*க்காக"' --group-by parse.state --sum tokens --grammar tam.fwdata
# 50 unparsed words of a pattern, chosen by seed, as a working set with counts
motif query --corpus a.tsv,b.weights.json forms where 'parse.state = none and form ~ ".*ப்பட்.*"' --grammar tam.fwdata --sample 50 --seed 7 --write-words work.tsv --with-counts
```

## Ordered morphs: `morph`, `seq`, `--count-by morph-seq`

`morph(<item>)` keeps the words with a reading that has the morph; `seq(<item>, <item>, ...)` keeps the words with a reading whose morphs match the items in that order. Both read the readings of the cached corpus parse, so they need `--grammar` (refused as `query.readings-needs-grammar` without it). Gaps between the matched morphs are allowed; `seq(a, b, adjacent=true)` (JSON `{"seq": {"items": ["a", "b"], "adjacent": true}}`, a single `morph` as `{"morph": "a"}`) or `--adjacent` for every `seq` of the query needs them next to each other. Each morph matches one item, so `seq(x, x)` needs two morphs. An item is one of:

- `entry:<guid>`, `msa:<guid>` or `form:<guid>`: the morph's entry, analysis or form id; a bare guid is an analysis or form id. `entry:` needs the project.
- `root:<form>`, `pfx:<form>` or `sfx:<form>`: a form in the project's lexicon, resolved to its entry exactly as `realizes` resolves it (`root:` takes a stem, the others an affix); a form of several entries or analyses is refused as ambiguous, and then `entry:` or `msa:` names the one. Needs `--project` (or a `.fwdata` as `--grammar`).
- `text:<surface>`: the surface text the morph occupies, ignoring case; needs no project.
- any other token, such as `CAUS` or `RECP`: a class token.
