It matches a morph whose entry gloss, class (`stem`, `derivational`, `inflectional`, `affix`) or PanGloss inflection type equals the token, ignoring case. The gloss and class come from the project's lexicon, so a class token needs `--project`; without one it is refused as `query.readings-needs-project`.

A class token matches gloss, class or inflection type exactly (case-insensitive, never a substring, so `CAU` does not match `CAUS`); it shares its namespace with the stem glosses, so prefer `root:` or `entry:` to name a stem. An item that matches no morph of any reading of the parse is refused as `query.seq-item-unknown`, never answered with zero (a misspelt `CUAS` is caught that way). `not morph(...)` and `not seq(...)` are refused as `query.seq-negation-incomplete` unless the corpus parse is complete (no capped, timed-out or unanswered word), because a capped word may hide the reading. `readingsInfo.complete` says whether it is.

`--count-by morph-seq` counts the distinct morph sequences of the readings that satisfy the query's `morph` and `seq` predicates (every reading when there are none; a `not`, a field or another predicate says nothing about a single reading, so it never removes one: `not seq(A, B) --count-by morph-seq` lists the sequences of every reading of the words without the sequence, including readings of other words that contain it, and `seq(A) or form = x` keeps every reading of a word that matches only the second branch). A sequence is written by its morphs in surface order, each as its text, then `/` and the entry gloss when the project gives one (`fany/do`, `ish/CAUS`, `an/RECP`). A word counts once per distinct sequence, however many readings give it. The JSON adds `morphSeqs:{complete, words, tokens, distinct, sequences:[{seq:[...], types, tokens, examples:[word]}]}`, by tokens; `--limit` (default 100) caps how many sequences are listed, `distinct` is how many there are, and `complete` is false when a capped or unanswered word may hide readings, so the counts are lower bounds. It needs no `where` and lists no rows unless `--limit` is given.

```powershell
# how many words carry root fanya + CAUS + RECP in that order, and in what exact chains
motif query --corpus swh.weights.json forms where 'seq(root:fanya, CAUS, RECP)' --count-by morph-seq --grammar swh.fwdata --project swh.fwdata --json
# the same chain with the morphs next to each other
motif query --corpus swh.weights.json forms where 'seq(root:fanya, CAUS, RECP, adjacent=true)' --grammar swh.fwdata
```

## A stem list: `realizes(@file, attested)` and `--by-morph`

`realizes(@stems.txt, attested)` reads one morpheme spec per line (the same syntax as the single argument: `entry:msa`, `entry:<guid>` or a bare entry id, which means any analysis of the entry as `morph(entry:)` does and needs `--project`, an analysis or form id, or `root:`, `pfx:`, `sfx:` and a form with `--project`; blank lines and lines starting `#` are skipped) and means any of them. One index parse serves the whole list, from the parse's spans; nothing is traced. A line whose morpheme no parsed word carries stands for no word and is listed in `realizes` with the reason `no-parses`, where a lone `realizes(M, attested)` would be refused; `not realizes(@file, ...)` over such a list is refused as `query.realizes-negation-incomplete`. A guid that no morph of the parse and no entry of the project carries is refused as `query.realizes-id-unknown`, never answered as `no-parses`; a refusal about one line names the file and the line number. A line is not trimmed of an inline `# comment`. An unreadable file is refused as `query.corpus-unreadable`, and a file with no spec as `query.corpus-invalid`.

`--by-morph` groups the matches per morpheme of a `realizes` query as `byMorph:[{morpheme, types, tokens, examples}]`, by tokens; every line of the file has a group, with zero for one no word carries. It needs a `realizes` predicate in the query.

```powershell
# the corpus forms of eleven Tamil stems, per stem
motif query --corpus tam.weights.json forms where 'realizes(@stems.txt, attested)' --by-morph --grammar tam.fwdata --project tam.fwdata --json
```

## A paradigm twin: `--twin`

`--twin <template>` rewrites each word the where's `form ~ "regex"` (or `form matches`) predicate matches, from the regex's capture groups, and describes the rewritten form, its twin. The template writes `$1` or `${name}` for a group, `$0` for the whole match and `$$` for a dollar sign (use `${1}2` before a digit). The first match is replaced where it stands and the rest of the word stays, as a substitution does, so `~` rewrites the matched span and `matches` the whole word. The where must have exactly one such regex, not under `not`; several different ones, or one under `or`, are refused as `query.twin-regex-ambiguous`. Twin forms are normalised as corpus forms are (NFC, and lower case with `--fold-case`) before the corpus lookup. The regex uses the same engine as the query: non-backtracking, which supports groups and named groups but not lookarounds or back-references. A template that names a group the regex lacks is refused as `query.twin-group-unknown`, and `--twin` with no such regex as `query.twin-needs-regex`.

The columns of a lone `--twin` are `twin.form`, `twin.tokens` (0 when the corpus lacks the form), `twin.inCorpus` (`true` or `false`), `twin.parse.state` and `twin.readings`. With several `--twin` the templates are `twin1`, `twin2` in the order given (`twin1.form`, `twin2.parse.state`). A word the regex does not match has no twin values. The columns work in `where` (`twin.inCorpus is false`, `twin.tokens > 10`), in `--group-by` (`parse.state,twin.parse.state`) and in the JSON rows as `twins:[{label, form, tokens, inCorpus, parseState, readings}]`. The parse columns need `--grammar`: the parse state of a twin that is a corpus word comes from the corpus parse index, and the forms the corpus lacks are parsed by one more batch over just those forms, cached like the corpus (more than 100,000 such forms is refused; the batches are kept in their own `twins` cache folder, so they never evict the corpus index). A twin that is capped, timed out or gets no answer counts in `readingsInfo` and makes the report incomplete. Without `--grammar` the rows carry the form, tokens and `inCorpus` only.

```powershell
# which -ிலிருந்து words are stem gaps and which only lack the -ில் suffix form
motif query --corpus a.weights.json,b.weights.json forms where 'form ~ "(.*)ிலிருந்து$"' --twin '$1ில்' --group-by parse.state,twin.parse.state --grammar tam.fwdata
```

## Comparing two grammars: `--baseline-grammar`

`--baseline-grammar <path>` parses the corpus with a second grammar (the baseline, usually the original of a scratch copy) and compares it, word by word, with `--grammar` (the target, the copy you changed). It needs `--grammar`, and naming the same file for both is refused as `query.baseline-same-grammar`. Each grammar has its own cached parse index, keyed by the grammar, so a baseline is parsed once however many variants are compared with it. To compare several variants with one baseline, run the query once per variant with a different `--grammar` and the same `--baseline-grammar`: one table per variant, and every run after the first reads the baseline from its cache.

The columns are `base.parse.state` and `base.readings` (the baseline's values; the plain `parse.state` and `readings` are the target's) and `change`:

- `gained`: no reading in the baseline, at least one now.
- `lost`: at least one reading in the baseline, none now.
- `more-readings` and `fewer-readings`: both parse, with more or fewer readings now.
- `readings-changed`: both parse with the same number of readings, but the analyses differ (by PanGloss's signature of each reading, else by its morphs' form and analysis ids, in any order).
- `same`: nothing differs.
- `unknown`: a word that either grammar's parse stopped at the work limit, stopped at the word timeout or got no answer for. It is never `gained` or `lost`, and it makes the header say `Readings: INCOMPLETE` and `readingsInfo.complete` false, with the number of such words in the note. `baselineInfo` is the baseline parse's own report.

The columns work in `where` (`change = lost`, `change = more-readings`), in `--group-by` (`--group-by change --sum tokens`, or `change,base.parse.state`) and in the JSON rows as `baseline:{parseState, readings, change}`; the columns without `--baseline-grammar` are refused as `query.corpus-invalid`. A comparison may omit the `where`: `--group-by change --sum tokens` alone counts every word.

```powershell
# what the variant gained and lost against the original, in types and tokens
motif query --corpus swh.weights.json forms --grammar variant-b/swh.fwdata --baseline-grammar base/swh.fwdata --group-by change --sum tokens
# the words it lost, most frequent first
motif query --corpus swh.weights.json forms where 'change = lost' --grammar variant-b/swh.fwdata --baseline-grammar base/swh.fwdata --limit 50
```
usage: Usage: motif query corpus forms --corpus <words.tsv|folder> (forms where <expression> | forms --where <expression> | forms --query-json <file|->) [--grammar <path>] [--project <fwdata>] [--thorough] [--segments <file>] [--fold-case] [--split-hyphens] [--limit <n>] [--segment-test engine|identity] [--group-by cause|parse.state|readings|shape] [--sum tokens] [--sample <n>] [--seed <n>] [--write-words <file>] [--with-counts] [--force] [--what-if-retire <ids>] [--count-by morph-seq] [--adjacent] [--by-morph] [--twin <template>] [--baseline-grammar <path>] [--json]

entries.title: Query forms
entries.description: Filters and groups forms, stems, uses or objects from available Trial evidence with and, or, not and typed field predicates, reads forms from the Baseline or a Proposal's Trial copy with parse state and analyses (--as-of, --sides both), runs a motif.query.v2 JSON document (--query-json) or prints its schema (--schema), or runs the saved query of a Parsimony Measure.
entries.helpPage:
# Query forms

`query forms`, `query stems`, `query uses` and `query objects` read the sources below, and `query saved` runs the saved query of a Measure. `query forms` reads forms and their bases from the latest available Parsimony evidence for a Trial. It does not change the FieldWorks project. Run a Trial and wait for its evidence job. If the project changes or a newer Trial completes, the result marks the older evidence as stale.

Use repeated `--where` selectors to combine conditions. The operators are `=`, `in`, `not`, `has`, `~`, `<` and `>`; regular expressions use the non-backtracking engine. For example:

```powershell
motif query forms --project "project.fwdata" --where kind=alternate --where 'change=d>r'
motif query forms --project "project.fwdata" --where kind=alternate --group letters.dropped --json
```

A `--where` can also be a boolean expression: predicates `column op value` joined by `and`, `or` and `not`, with parentheses. `not` binds tighter than `and`, which binds tighter than `or`. The text ops are `is`, `not`, `in`, `not in`, `has`, `<`, `>`, `~` (unanchored regular expression), `matches` (a regular expression that must match the whole value), `exists` and `missing`. A value is a bare word or a double-quoted string, and `in`, `not in` and `has` take comma-separated values. A `--where` that starts with `(` or `not `, or that holds the words `and` or `or` and parses as an expression, is read as an expression; every other `--where` is read as a v1 selector first, so a v1 line keeps its meaning unless it uses an unquoted `and`, `or` or `not` as an operator; words inside double quotes never count. Wrap a single predicate in parentheses to force the expression reading, for example `--where "(kind not in a,b)"`.

```powershell
motif query forms --project "project.fwdata" --where "kind is variant or (kind is alternate and tokens > 5)" --limit 20
```

`--limit` keeps at most that many rows, groups or ids. A `--as-of` run takes a conjunction of `is`, `not`, `in`, `has`, `<`, `>` and `~` selectors only.

## The JSON form: `--query-json` and `--schema`

`motif query --project "project.fwdata" --query-json <file|->` runs one `motif.query.v2` document, from a file or from standard input with `-`, and takes no other query flag. `motif query --schema` prints its JSON Schema, which is generated from the same records the engine reads; it lists every op, source and column with its type, and the reserved kinds. The MCP tool `motif_query` takes the same document as its `query` argument, and `motif_query_schema` returns the schema. Every response carries `schemaVersion`.

```json
{ "version": "motif.query.v2", "from": "forms",
  "where": { "and": [ { "field": "kind", "op": "in", "value": ["alternate", "variant"] },
                      { "not": { "field": "form", "op": "regex", "value": "sa.*" } } ] },
  "limit": 50 }
```

A predicate is `{field, op, value}` with op `eq`, `ne`, `in`, `nin`, `lt`, `gt`, `has`, `regex`, `contains` or `exists`. `regex` must match the whole value and `contains` matches anywhere; both use the non-backtracking engine and are limited to 256 characters. An op that does not fit its column (`lt` on text, `has` on a single value, `regex` on a number) is refused with `query.op-type-mismatch`. `morph`, `seq` and `realizes` are reserved: a document that uses one is refused with `query.not-yet-available`. `phon` and `env` are real; see the next section. A malformed document is refused with `query.document-invalid`, naming the path.

`--group` accepts comma-separated columns, `--min-count` filters groups, and `--examples` selects examples ordered by form. `--ids` includes ids for use by other commands. `--trial` selects the Trial whose evidence is available; only one evidence bundle has query rows. Token frequency is not available in this phase. Forms use the project's graphemes; `--raw-letters` uses individual characters instead.

## Reading the Baseline or a Proposal: `--as-of` and `--sides both`

`motif query forms --as-of baseline` reads the lexicon's forms from the current Baseline and needs no Trial. `--as-of <proposalId>` reads that Proposal's latest completed Trial copy, which carries the Proposal's grammar. A Proposal with no completed Trial is not an error: the run succeeds with that side marked `pending` and no rows. `--sides both --as-of <proposalId>` returns the Baseline and the Proposal side by side. Nothing is saved; a run is always read afresh. These runs print JSON. They read only the forms source and refuse `--change`, `--score`, evidence, `--members`, `--context`, `--exception`, `--unit` and `--trial`. An unknown Proposal, no Baseline, a revision digest, or a Trial whose copy was cleared is refused with `query.as-of-unavailable`.

Each row carries its form's columns and, under `parse`, the state and analyses of the word of the Texts whose spelling is the form: `state` is `approved`, `parsed`, `unparsed`, `failed` (it has analyses and a person disapproved every one) or `absent` (the form is not a word of the Texts); `tokens` counts its occurrences in the Texts (the form's `tokens` column); `analyses` lists each analysis's `category`, `approved` flag and morph cut, each `morphs` entry having `form`, `gloss`, `category` and the lexicon `entry` id.

`--where` selectors work as above and also on `parse-state` (`=`, `in`, `not`) and `parse-tokens` (`=`, `not`, `<`, `>`). With `--sides both`, prefix a column with `baseline.` or `proposal.` to apply it to that side only, for example `--where proposal.parse-state=parsed`; a row stays only if it passes every prefixed selector, and an unprefixed selector must pass on at least one side read. A selector on a pending side is not applied. `--sort [baseline.|proposal.]<column>[:desc]` orders the rows by `form`, `base`, `kind`, `entry`, `id`, `morph-type`, `variant-type`, `environments`, `category`, `tokens`, `parse-state` or `parse-tokens`; with `--sides both` the side is required, rows lacking that side come last, and the default is `baseline.form`. A single side may also use `--group`; the groups then appear under `result` and `sides.rows` is empty.

```powershell
motif query forms --project "project.fwdata" --as-of baseline --where kind=alternate --sort form --json
motif query forms --project "project.fwdata" --as-of <proposalId> --sides both --where proposal.parse-state=parsed --sort proposal.form:desc --json
```

The JSON keeps the usual fields and adds `sides` (the usual `result.rows` repeats the rows without parse data for a single side, and is empty for `--sides both`; `trialId` is the proposal side's Trial, and `grammarHash` and `bundleId` are empty):

```json
{
  "sides": {
    "version": 1,
    "mode": "both",
    "states": [
      { "side": "baseline", "status": "ready", "source": "baseline" },
      { "side": "proposal", "status": "pending", "source": "<proposalId>", "reason": "no-trial" }
    ],
    "rows": [
      {
        "id": "<form id>",
        "baseline": { "form": { "id": "", "form": "kaon", "base": "kaon", "kind": "lexeme", "entry": "", "morphType": "stem", "variantType": "", "environments": [], "category": [], "tokens": 3 },
                      "parse": { "state": "approved", "tokens": 3, "analyses": [ { "category": "", "approved": true, "morphs": [ { "form": "kaon", "gloss": "eat", "category": "", "entry": "" } ] } ] } }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

`version` is the shape version; it rises when a property changes meaning or is removed, and a consumer should tolerate unknown values in the closed sets below. `status` is `ready` or `pending`; `reason` (only when pending) is `no-trial`, `trial-not-completed`, `no-baseline` or `trial-cleared`; `parse.state` is `approved`, `parsed`, `unparsed`, `failed` or `absent`. A pending proposal side is not an absence of changes: read `states` first. `absent` means no data, not a failed parse: the form is matched to a word of the Texts by its exact spelling, so a lexeme stem that is not itself a word of the Texts is `absent` even when its inflected words are parsed. `parse.tokens` counts the word's occurrences in this side's own copy, and the row's `form.tokens` repeats it (omitted when 0), so it differs from the `tokens` column of a latest-Trial query; sorting or filtering on `tokens` or `parse-tokens` treats a missing count as 0. Each row's `id` is unique: a form's id, and for a variant form that varies two or more entries, the variant form's id, `@`, then the main entry's id, so one row per main entry.

A side that was not read, is pending, or lacks the form is omitted from its row. A ready Proposal state also gives `trialId`. `mode` is `baseline`, `proposal` or `both`.

## Other sources

| Source | One row per | Columns |
|---|---|---|
| `stems` | stem MSA | `form`, `entry`, `category` (set, `none` when the MSA has no part-of-speech row), `features` (set), `gloss` (`none` when blank), `msa-count`, `alternates` |
| `uses` | reference to an environment, natural class, exception feature, category, slot or inflection class | `target-kind`, `target`, `user-kind`, `user`, `role`, `effect` |
| `objects` | environment, natural class, exception feature, category, slot or inflection class | `class`, `label`, `uses`, `applied`, `carriers`, `users`, `key` |

`stems` and `forms` also have `shape` (the consonant and vowel skeleton), `syllables`, `initial:n` and `final:n` (the first or last n segments) and `fold`. `<` and `>` compare `tokens`, `syllables`, `msa-count`, `alternates`, `uses`, `applied`, `carriers` and `users`. `fold` uses `--fold`, comma-separated from `nfc`, `case`, `iy~y`, `o~u`, `e~i`, `c~k`, a raw `from>to` and `project` (the project's `[parsimony] fold` rules); the default is `nfc,case`. `--distinct <column>` keeps only groups that hold two different values of that column.

A Trial built on light facts has no `uses` rows for exception features, categories, slots or inflection classes, and no measured `uses` or `applied` for objects of those classes (their columns are empty, not 0). A `uses` query that selects such a target kind, or an `objects` query that compares `uses` or `applied` for such a class, is refused with `query.not-measured`; otherwise the result lists what was not measured under `NotMeasured`. The same applies to target kinds left out by the 250,000-row `uses` cap.

```powershell
motif query stems --project "project.fwdata" --where 'final:2~[aiu]d' --group shape
motif query objects --project "project.fwdata" --where class=environment --where applied=0
```

## Testing a hypothesised change

`motif query stems --change X>Y` tests a hypothesised change without changing the project. `--at initial|final` and `--affixes a,b` say where X is dropped and which affixes can follow, and `--wordset <id>` names the project's `[[review-word-set]]` of role `sampled-tokens` that serves as the attested evidence. It adds the columns `predicted` (the form with X replaced by Y), `evidence` (`rule`, `base`, `both` or `none`: which of the predicted and the original form the word set attests) and `collides` (`entry`: another entry already has the predicted form; `parses`: the current parser run analyses it; `none`; or `not-measured` when there is no parser evidence).

`--score` takes `tolerance` (the exceptions e must stay below N/ln N), `reliability` (the lower confidence limit (h+0.5)/(n+1) with z = 0.674; its version is printed; it is a sort key, not a verdict) and `control`. `control` follows the rule-hypothesis control test: with `--discovery <id>` and `--heldout <id>` it counts held-out hits against control letters (`--controls`, `--control-letters`) and returns counts only. A held-out set cannot also be the `--wordset`. Scorers count one unit; a scorer that would mix stems and MSAs is refused with `query.mixed-units` (`--unit msa|stem`, `--exception` selectors). `--test-result` prints the control result as the JSON that `motif hypothesis test --file` accepts. Anything Motif did not measure is listed under `NotMeasured`, never shown as 0.

```powershell
motif query stems --project "project.fwdata" --change d>r --at final --affixes an,un,on,i,a --wordset union --score reliability,tolerance
```

## Splitting a pattern and weighing its size

`--score split` asks whether a grouping of rows is a rule. The deviants are the rows `--exception` selects, the ids in a `--members` file, or, under `--change` with a `--wordset`, the rows whose unchanged form alone is attested. In one pass it tallies about 30 context values (edges, shape, category, features, environments, the change itself) and keeps a context only if it covers the deviants, predicts them reliably, is smaller than listing them, can be stated in shapes FieldWorks itself can create, and holds on the held-out set. Outcome A is a sub-rule, B is predictable but not expressible as a rule, and C is a lexical list. Split, size, member and same-shape counts use distinct stem forms by default on the stems source (`--unit msa` counts MSAs instead), and form records on the forms source. Tag references use that declared unit. Missing parser measurements are excluded from context judging and their missing measurement counts are reported. Environment text remains `not-checked` because the query snapshot has no resolved, validated FieldWorks rule context. A context that covers fewer than 20 units is reported only as too few to tell. A second context is looked for once, among the rows the first leaves. Anything it could not decide reads `not-checked`; held-out words are never shown, only counts, and only from 20 words. `--score size` weighs the encodings in objects plus tag references, for the context a `--context <selector>` names, or against the opposite polarity when none is given.

## One screen of evidence

`motif query evidence stems|forms --where <selector>` (or `--members <file>`) prints the shared contexts, the counter-examples, the tolerance, reliability and control, the size, the same-shape count with ledger neighbours, the top examples and the words whose evidence is undecided as questions for a speaker. Scorers that need a change or word sets and did not get them are listed as not measured. Five or more units of one shape mean a rule attempt is required.

```powershell
motif query evidence stems --project "project.fwdata" --where "final:2=ad" --change d>r --at final --affixes an,un --wordset union
```

## Saved queries

`motif query saved <measure-id>` runs the query that detects the same items as the Measure: `P-msa-no-category`, `P-statement-unused`, `P-env-duplicate`, `P-feature-few-carriers` and `P-lexeme-near-duplicate`. The Measure remains the command that records findings; the saved query lists the items and nothing else.

## Phonological patterns: `phon` and `env`

`{"phon": "Stop V Stop V"}` keeps the forms the pattern matches somewhere; `{"env": "[Voiced] / # _ V"}` keeps the forms in which the target occurs between the left and right patterns. In text they are `phon(Stop V Stop V)` and `env(Voiced / # _ V)`, usable in `--where` and anywhere a predicate goes, with `and`, `or` and `not`. A pattern is items separated by spaces: a natural class by its token (`C`, `V`; the first column of `motif query --values classes`, written in brackets when it has spaces, `[Nasal Stop]`) or by its full FieldWorks name (`[Vowels]` for `V`; the second column; case does not matter, and Motif resolves it to the token before it sends the pattern, refusing a name two classes share), a feature bundle `[+voice -nasal]`, an alpha variable `[αvoice]`, a literal segment `/p/` (a bare letter is not a segment), `( )` and `( )*`, `#` for the word edge and `+` for a morpheme boundary.

PanGloss does the matching. It segments each word with the grammar's surface character table, the one `parse` uses, so a pattern sees the word the way the parser does. Motif sends the forms left after the cheaper predicates have run, in batches, to the resident `pangloss serve` of the project's Baseline; it never starts a process per word. Each result row then carries `matches`, the spans (segment and byte offsets, and the matched text) of each predicate. A word the grammar cannot segment is `unsegmentable`: it matches no pattern and is not matched by `not` of one. The result header counts such words and lists a sample (`phon.unsegmentable`, `phon.unsegmentableSample` in JSON); a word PanGloss stopped on at a work, deadline or match cap is counted as `incomplete` the same way; if it kept matches before the stop, they are returned flagged `partial`, and a `not` over that word still excludes it. With `--ids` the counts go to standard error so the ids stay pipeable. Nothing is dropped silently.

PanGloss's `match` op needs a release that declares `interfaces.serveOps.match` and lists `engine` and `identity` under its `segmentTests` (v0.31.0); with an older one the query is refused with `query.phon-unavailable`, naming the release. Feature bundles, alpha variables and `env` run on PanGloss 0.30.0 and later, and an older parser is refused with `query.phon-unavailable`. One alpha letter on two different features (`[αvoice] _ [αson]`) is refused with `query.phon-pattern-refused` carrying PanGloss's own code (`unsupported_construct`, construct `alphaAcrossFeatures`).  `+` needs words with marked boundaries, which Motif does not send yet, so on ordinary words it is refused the same way (`boundary_needs_marked_input`).

### Segment test: `engine` or `identity`

`--segment-test engine|identity` (JSON `segmentTest`, MCP `segmentTest`; the corpus `forms` command takes the flag too) chooses how a segment is tested against a pattern. The default is `engine`, rule application's own test, because the purpose of a pattern is to find the words a rule will touch.

- Under `engine` a literal `/i/` matches every segment with `i`'s feature bundle, and a segment-list `[class]` means the union of its members' features, so it can match segments the class does not list. The spans are a superset of what a rule rewrites: they include positions a rule leaves unchanged (its output equals its input) and overlapping spans, because a rule applies leftmost and non-overlapping. Only the target is widened: the sides of an `env` are exact, as they are in a rule, so under `engine` every position a rule's environment accepts is found.
- Under `identity` a literal names exactly one segment and a `[class]` exactly its members: use it for "exactly these letters". A literal or a segment-list class then may miss a segment a rule treats as the same, so the result carries `matchMode: "identity"` and `mayUnderReport: true`, the header says so, and `not` over such a pattern warns that absence is not proven.

Every `phon` and `env` result states the mode it ran under: `segmentTest` in the JSON `phon` object and a `SEGMENT TEST:` line in the text header.

`motif query --values classes --project "project.fwdata"` (or the MCP `motif_query_schema` with `values: "classes"`) lists the natural classes and phonological features of the Baseline: for each class the token to type, its full name (`fullName` in JSON; the label when the class has none) and its kind. The names are read from PanGloss's `inventory` op.
usage: Usage: motif query forms --project <fwdata> [--where <selector>] [--group <columns>] [--min-count <n>] [--distinct <column>] [--fold <set>] [--examples <n>] [--ids] [--raw-letters] [--segment-test engine|identity] [--trial <id>] [--limit <n>] [--as-of baseline|<proposalId> [--sides both] [--sort [baseline.|proposal.]<column>[:desc]]] [--json]

entries.title: Find affix pairs in words
entries.description: Reads a plain word list (a TSV of form and count, or a folder of text files) with no project and finds pairs of words that differ only by a suffix or prefix, with the bases, tokens and examples of each differing part and the parts each base takes. Optional regular expression on the differing part, bases having all of several parts, bounded and deterministic.
entries.helpPage:
# Query pairs

`motif query pairs --corpus <words.tsv|folder> --differ suffix|prefix` (or `motif query --corpus <words.tsv|folder> pairs --differ suffix|prefix`) finds pairs of words of a plain word list that differ only by an affix: a base and base+X (suffix) or X+base (prefix). It needs no project, Trial or parse, and changes nothing.

```powershell
motif query --corpus words.tsv pairs --differ suffix
motif query --corpus texts/ pairs --differ suffix --x 'an|in' --having an,in --json
```

## The corpus

A TSV has one word per line, `form<TAB>count<TAB>parse state`. The header is optional; a first line starting `form` or `word` names the columns (`count`, `tokens` or `frequency`; `state` or `parse.state`). A missing count is 1. A folder is every `.txt` file in it, tokenised on Unicode letters and combining marks; an apostrophe (U+0027, U+2019, U+02BC) or hyphen-minus between letters stays inside the word (`ng'ombe`), and `--split-hyphens` splits at hyphens. Forms are NFC; `--fold-case` also lower-cases them, and folds `--having` and matches `--x` ignoring case. Segments are code points and the result says `approximate`. `--segments <file>` lists multi-character graphemes, such as `ng ny ch`, separated by spaces, tabs, commas or lines, with `#` comments; the longest match wins.

## The result

Per X: the bases that take it, the tokens of those derived forms, the tokens of the bases and the example pairs with the most tokens. Per base: the Xs it takes. `--x <regex>` keeps the Xs the whole differing part matches (non-backtracking). `--having a,b` keeps the bases that take all of the listed Xs. `--max-x` (1 to 12, default 4) caps the length of X in segments, `--limit` (default 100) caps the X rows and the base rows, and `--examples` (default 5) caps the examples. A cut is stated: `TRUNCATED: showing 100 of 412 Xs`, and in JSON the `truncation` object holds the totals and shown counts. Rows are in a fixed order, so a run is reproducible. `--json` writes `motif.query.pairs.v1`.

entries.title: List pattern class names
entries.description: Lists the natural-class and phonological-feature names of a project's Baseline (--project) or of a grammar file (--grammar), for writing phon and env patterns; read from the grammar, because PanGloss does not list them.
entries.helpPage:
# Query values

`motif query --values classes --project <fwdata>` (or `--grammar <path>`) lists the natural classes and phonological features of the project's Baseline or of a grammar file: the names a `phon` or `env` pattern can use. The MCP tool `motif_query_schema` returns the same list with `values: "classes"`.

Each class line leads with the token to type in a pattern (in brackets when it has spaces), then PanGloss's label for the class and its kind: `segment` (an explicit segment list) or `feature` (a feature structure). The kind matters for matching: PanGloss tests literals and segment-list classes by identity (see `query forms`). PanGloss keeps one label per class (a FieldWorks project's Abbreviation; the Name FieldWorks shows is not kept), so a class is written by that label, case-sensitively, or by its id; a class whose label cannot be written in brackets shows `(none)`. Features list their values.

The list comes from PanGloss's `inventory` op, so it needs a PanGloss that declares `interfaces.serveOps.inventory` (release v0.30.0), starts the grammar once (a few seconds, where reading it with LibLCM took about three and a half minutes on a 170 MB project) and reads it as the parser loads it. When PanGloss refuses a name as `unknown_natural_class`, Motif reads the list, resolves a different case or an id to the class's token and tries again, or refuses with the closest (at most five) labels; if the list cannot be read or is empty the refusal says so. Text between `/.../` is never rewritten. `--verbose` prints the stage timing to standard error. The JSON gives each class a `token` and `kind` and each feature its `values`. `--json` writes `motif.query.values.v1`. See `query forms` for the pattern language.

entries.title: Export a record file
entries.description: Writes one record, or every record of a kind, from the saved project as the record file that import reads, and counts every value the file leaves out. It never changes the project. If the project changes after an export, export the record again and redo the edits; there is no merge.
entries.helpPage:
# Export a record file

`motif record export --project <fwdata> --out <path> (--record <guid> | --all) [--kind <kind>] [--json]` writes the saved project's records as the files `motif import` reads. The MCP tool `motif_record_export` takes `out`, `recordId`, `kind` and `all`, and writes only under the project's folder or the working directory.

`--record <guid>` writes one record to the file `--out`. `--all` writes every root record of the kind into the folder `--out`, one file each, named by the record's GUID. The kind is `lexicon/entry` (the default), `notebook/record` or `lists/item`. Nothing is replaced: an existing file at a target refuses the whole call with `record-export.output-unwritable` before anything is written.

The file holds what the record file format can hold. Every other value of the record's objects is counted in the response by class, field and reason (`unexported`, with `unexportedCount`), so a person editing the file knows what it does not carry; the values themselves are not printed. A record that cannot be written as a file is counted in `notWrittenCount` and listed under `(record)`, and the other records are still written.

Edit the file, then run `motif import --file` to plan it. The file carries a digest of the record as exported: if the project changes first, import refuses the file whole (`record-import.plan-refused`). Export again and redo the edits; there is no merge. Exporting twice from an unchanged project writes byte-identical files, and importing an unedited export plans no change.

entries.title: Decline a Proposal
entries.description: Declines a Proposal you do not want. It is kept with its Trials as history, and you can reopen it later.
entries.helpPage:
# Decline a Proposal

`motif reject --proposal <id>` declines a Proposal you do not want. It is kept, with its [Trials](term:trial), as a record of what was suggested; nothing reaches FieldWorks.

## When to use it

Use it after reading a Proposal you will not apply. A Proposal that is still a Draft is finalized first, so what you declined stays readable. Your own pending changes are not declined; take them out in **Proposals**, under **Your Changes Not Applied Yet**, instead.

## Example

```text
motif reject --proposal <id> --project <project> --json
```

## What it prints

The Proposal's id and its new status, `rejected`. In the window, **Decline** on the Proposal in **Proposals** does the same while the Proposal is open, and the card moves to **Closed** on **Proposals**.

## Related commands

See [Reopen a Proposal](cmd:reopen%20--proposal) and [Delete a closed Proposal](cmd:delete%20--proposal).

entries.title: Remove Draft operations
entries.description: Removes explicit operations from a Draft while respecting declared dependencies. Revise and measure the content again before Finalize. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Remove Draft operations

Removes explicit operations from a Draft while respecting declared dependencies. Revise and measure the content again before Finalize. Only a person can Apply.

entries.title: Reopen a Proposal
entries.description: Opens a declined or withdrawn Proposal again as a Draft under the same id, with its history kept. An applied or superseded Proposal is never reopened.
entries.helpPage:
# Reopen a Proposal

`motif reopen --proposal <id>` opens a declined or withdrawn Proposal again as a Draft, under the same id. Its earlier revisions and [Trials](term:trial) are kept.

## When to use it

Use it when you change your mind about a Proposal you declined, or want to take up one its author withdrew. An applied Proposal is final and is refused with `proposal.applied-final`. A superseded Proposal is refused with `proposal.superseded`, which names the Proposal that replaced it.

## Example

```text
motif reopen --proposal <id> --project <project> --json
```

## What it prints

The Proposal's id, the name of its Draft and how many changes it holds. In the window, **Reopen** on a closed card on **Proposals** does the same. Try the Proposal again before applying it.

## Related commands

See [Decline a Proposal](cmd:reject%20--proposal) and [Apply one Proposal](cmd:apply%20--proposal).

entries.title: Read an Assessment report
entries.description: Calculates a named report from an Assessment and project data. Use it to answer a focused question about words, Texts, or grammar without rerunning PanGloss.
entries.helpPage:
# Read an Assessment report

`report` calculates a named Report from one stored Assessment and the project's own data. It answers a focused question about measured evidence without running PanGloss again.

The kind list includes `parsimony`, but `report` reads one stored Assessment. Supplying that Assessment to `report --kind parsimony` is refused because the Parsimony producer needs a frozen Baseline evidence bundle, not an Assessment input. Create the result with [`parsimony --wait`](cmd:parsimony%20--wait) and read it with [`parsimony show`](cmd:parsimony%20show).

`report --kind coverage` is the share of a scope's words the parser analysed. It is a different measurement from [`coverage`](cmd:coverage), which counts every word type of a lane ledger as accounted for or Open and says whether the lane is Done.

## When to use it

Use a Report to inspect counts or findings for words, Texts, or grammar after an Assessment exists. First list the available kinds if you do not know which one matches your question.

## Example

```powershell
motif report --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --assessment <assessmentId> --kind <kind> --json
```

## What it prints

The response contains findings for the requested kind and can be narrowed to a word or Text. `--json` returns structured results. Reports are advisory; they do not decide whether an Apply is allowed.

## Related commands

- [List report kinds](cmd:report%20--list-kinds) shows accepted values for `--kind`.
- [Compare two Assessments](cmd:compare) stores a measured difference between runs.

entries.title: List report kinds
entries.description: Lists the report kinds accepted by report --kind. Run it first when you need to choose a report for stored evidence.
entries.helpPage:
# List report kinds

`report --list-kinds` prints the stable kind codes accepted by `report --kind`.

The list includes `parsimony`, but `report` reads one stored Assessment. Supplying that Assessment to `report --kind parsimony` is refused because the Parsimony producer needs a frozen Baseline evidence bundle, not an Assessment input. Use [`parsimony --wait`](cmd:parsimony%20--wait) to create that Report, then [`parsimony show`](cmd:parsimony%20show) to read it.

## When to use it

Run this when writing a script or choosing a Report and you need to know which kinds Motif supports. The returned codes are machine-readable identifiers; they are not display labels.

## Example

```powershell
motif report --list-kinds
```

## What it prints

The command lists available Report kinds. Add `--json` for a structured list that an AI agent or script can select from without parsing terminal text.

## Related commands

- [Read an Assessment report](cmd:report) runs one of the listed kinds.
- [Inspect parse timing](cmd:timing) reads recorded timing evidence directly.

entries.title: Ask again after a decline
entries.description: Makes a new open Request from the Request a declined Proposal answered, with the same target and note, so an assistant can try again.
entries.helpPage:
# Ask again after a decline

`request ask-again` makes a new open Request from the Request a declined Proposal answered, with the same target and note, so an assistant can try again.

## Example

```text
motif request ask-again <proposalId> --project <fwdata>
```

Give the full id of a declined Proposal that answered a Request. Asking twice returns the new Request while it is still open.

## Related commands

- [List the open Requests](cmd:list%20requests) shows the new one.

entries.title: Ask an assistant to fix this
entries.description: Stores a Request about a word, a Warning or a Compare matrix cell, with an optional note in the linguist's words. An assistant answers it with a Proposal.
entries.helpPage:
# Ask an assistant to fix this

`request create` stores a Request: something the linguist wants an assistant to fix, about a word, a Warning or a Compare matrix cell. An assistant answers it with a [Proposal](term:proposal).

## Example

```text
motif request create --project <fwdata> --kind word --target <word> --label <word> [--note "Please check the plural"]
```

`--kind` is `word`, `warning` or `matrix-cell`. `--target` is the word, Warning or cell as the window names it, and `--label` is a short name a person can read. The note is optional, at most 2000 characters, and stays the linguist's own words.

A Request is answered when the Proposal that answers it is finalized. It opens again if that Proposal is withdrawn or replaced before anyone decides, and stays answered if the linguist declines it.

## Related commands

- [List the open Requests](cmd:list%20requests) reads them.
- [Withdraw a Request](cmd:request%20withdraw) takes one back.

entries.title: Withdraw a Request
entries.description: Takes back an open Request the linguist no longer wants answered. An answered Request cannot be withdrawn.
entries.helpPage:
# Withdraw a Request

`request withdraw` takes back an open Request the linguist no longer wants answered.

## Example

```text
motif request withdraw <requestId> --project <fwdata>
```

Give the full `requestId` that [list requests](cmd:list%20requests) returns. Only an open Request can be withdrawn; an answered one stays as it is.

entries.title: Retire or merge forms
entries.description: Stages one connected Proposal to retire ordinary prefix or suffix alternates after their references move, or a duplicate stem alternate that nothing refers to; the sound-rule form also stages its natural class and rule. Dry Run shows bundle Morph and copied Form text changes, other references, and deletion together. Missing destinations are refused with counts for distinct unresolved Approved analyses, ad hoc rules, and other references; only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Retire or replace a form

Use this command to stage one ordinary prefix or suffix retirement in a Draft. Read the entry with detailed `motif_lexicon` output to copy its form identities and semantic digests. The closed intent names each retired form, its exact surviving form, and every bundle or ad hoc reference that must move.

```sh
motif retire-allomorph --project language.fwdata --draft remove-duplicate --intent '{"format":"motif-retire-allomorph","version":1,"retirement":{...}}'
```

The same standalone intent retires a stem alternate with `"scope":"stem"`, for a root or stem form that an exact duplicate in the same entry makes redundant. The duplicate must have the same morph type, spelling, stem name and environments, and it may be another alternate or the lexeme form. A stem retirement moves no references: if an analysis or restriction still refers to the retired form, or the form owns anything, the command refuses and names the reason. An entry always keeps the surviving duplicate, so its last stem form is never retired. A sound-rule replacement of stems stays refused.

For a listed allomorph replacement with a sound rule, use the `motif-allomorph-retirement` version 2 intent. It names the natural class, rewrite rule, each retired form, every destination, and the operation bindings in the same Proposal:

```sh
motif retire-allomorph --project language.fwdata --draft replace-listed --intent '{"format":"motif-allomorph-retirement","version":2,"naturalClass":{...},"rule":{...},"retirements":[...],"operations":[...]}'
```

The four displayed parts stay in that one Proposal: the sound class and rule; analyses whose bundle Morph moves, including the copied bundle Form alternatives; other references that move; and the retired forms. The dependency graph orders the writes. Dry Run reads back both Morph and native Form effects; no display order changes mutation order, and no part can be applied on its own.

The reference census refuses an incomplete or changed view, an unsupported reference, a form that no longer matches its authored identity, or an owned dependent that deletion would remove. When a destination is missing, the refusal names the number of distinct Approved analyses and ad hoc rules still unresolved, plus other references. Declare every destination and run Dry Run again.

Review the paired before and after reading evidence for every affected Approved reading. The review keeps each FieldWorks Opinion and surface spelling beside its parser result and rule attribution. Missing identity, parser completion, read-back, or rule trace is shown as unavailable; it is never counted as a preserved reading. Check that the detector finding is resolved in the rebuilt after Report, separately from whether a ruling is Suppressed, before a person Applies the whole Proposal.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` (at most 300 characters) to record the source on every operation this command produces.

entries.title: Retire an unused zero affix
entries.description: Stages deletion of one whole, unreferenced zero-affix entry when its only loaded realization is a recognized null marker, it adds no feature or class, every assigned slot is optional, and no assigned slot occurs in a template. Optional slot links are removed first and the slots remain; meaningful, referenced, or parser-distinguishing zeros are refused. Only a person can Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# Retire an unused zero affix

Use this command to stage deletion of a complete, unused prefix or suffix entry whose only loaded realization is a recognized null marker such as `^0`, `*0`, `&0`, or `∅`. An optional slot can remain in an inflectional template; deleting the entry removes its zero realization while preserving the slot and the template. The closed intent names the entry by canonical identity.

```sh
motif retire-redundant-zero-affix --project language.fwdata --draft remove-unused-zero --intent '{"format":"motif-retire-redundant-zero-affix","version":1,"retirement":{"entry":"<canonicalId>"}}'
```

The command includes the entry, its senses, analysis, form, and every owned dependent in one delete. It refuses feature, inflection-class, exception, condition, required-slot, or outside-reference contributions. References from the analysis to optional slots are removed before deletion; any template and its optional slot remain. Review the Dry Run and Trial before a person Applies the Proposal.

Add `--cite-source <text>` and optionally `--cite-locator <text>` (at most 300 characters) to record the source on every operation this command produces.

entries.title: Choose a Default Selection
entries.description: Saves which project Texts and words Motif should measure by default. Use it to focus repeated Assessments on material a linguist has chosen.
entries.helpPage:
# Choose a Default Selection

`selection set-default` saves which project Texts and added words Motif measures when a command does not name another Selection. It also saves the Selection's parser work limit and estimated or explicit time policy.

## When to use it

Use this to focus repeatable Assessments on a linguist-chosen set of material. Texts are identified by GUID, not by title, and added words can be included even when they do not occur in a Text.

## Example

```powershell
motif selection set-default --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --name "Verb examples" --texts <textGuid> --add-words "mala,ma" --parser-work-limit 20000000 --time-mode estimated
```

Use `--time-mode explicit --time-limit-ms <positive>` for a chosen time safety net, in milliseconds on this computer. `--time-mode estimated` rejects `--time-limit-ms`; `--parser-work-limit none` stores no step or time cap. To replace an existing Selection, first read its revision with [selection show](cmd:selection%20show) and pass it as `--expected-revision`.

## A word list with counts

`--words-file <path>` takes the added words from a UTF-8 file, in place of `--add-words`. Each line is a word, or a word, a tab and a whole-number count. There is no header line, and the file is at most 8 MiB.

- A plain list of words gives no counts. A word with no count has a count that is not known, which is not the same as zero.
- Words are stored in NFD. A word on several lines has its counts added up.
- Motif stores the file's name and its SHA-256 with the Selection, so you can tell which list the counts came from.
- A later save that names no file keeps the stored list when the Texts and added words are the same, and any other change to the Texts or words drops it.
- A Selection of chosen Texts ranks its words by places in those Texts. A Selection with no Texts ranks them by the file's counts, and the Overview then names its bands By Frequency Band, never Text Coverage.
- The window shows the same count beside each word in the word list of a Selection with no Texts, most often used first. A word the file gave no count has a blank there, and a count of zero shows as zero. Once the words are edited so they are no longer the saved list, the counts are blank until the Selection is saved with a list.

```powershell
motif selection set-default --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --name "Frequent words" --words-file .\frequencies.tsv
```

## What it prints

The command reports the saved Selection name and its settings. Add `--json` to receive the structured Selection response.

## Related commands

- [Show the Default Selection](cmd:selection%20show) reads what was saved.
- [List project Texts](cmd:texts%20list) finds Text GUIDs to select.
- [Set Selection limits](cmd:selection%20set-limits) changes limits without replacing the word list.

entries.title: Set Selection limits
entries.description: Changes only the saved Default Selection's parsing limits when its expected revision still matches. Use it to update the parser work limit or estimated-versus-explicit time policy without replacing the chosen Texts and added words.
entries.helpPage:
# Set Selection limits

`selection set-limits` changes the parsing limits on the project's current Default Selection. The chosen Texts, added words, name, and setup status stay in place.

## When to use it

Use this from Settings or **Analysis options** when you want later Default Selection parses to use a different parser work limit or time policy. Running and saved results keep their own resolved limits. A limit of exactly 20,000,000 (the default) counts as unset, so the project's `[parser] work-limit` applies; any other value beats the project setting.

## Example

```powershell
motif selection set-limits --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --name "Default" --expected-revision 3 --parser-work-limit 20000000 --time-mode estimated
```

Use `--time-mode explicit --time-limit-ms <positive>` to choose a time safety net, in milliseconds on this computer. Estimated mode rejects an explicit millisecond value. Use `--parser-work-limit none` for no step or time limit; an explicit time cap is not allowed with an unbounded parser work limit. Read the current revision with [selection show](cmd:selection%20show); if another write has changed it, read again and retry with the new revision.

## What it prints

The command returns the updated Selection and its new revision. Add `--json` to receive the structured projection.

## Related commands

- [Show the Default Selection](cmd:selection%20show) reads its current revision and policy.
- [Choose a Default Selection](cmd:selection%20set-default) also changes its Texts and added words.
- [Show project configuration](cmd:config%20show) reads named Assessment scopes from the project configuration file.

entries.title: Choose a Parsimony Selection
entries.description: Saves the Texts that Parsimony's Text group reads, apart from the Default Selection. Every Parsimony run reuses this set until you change it.
entries.helpPage:
# Choose a Parsimony Selection

`selection set-parsimony` saves the Texts that Parsimony's Text group reads. Every Parsimony run reuses the set until you change it, so the evidence for judging the grammar stays the same from run to run.

## When to use it

Use this once per project before running the Text group, or when you want different Texts as evidence. The Parsimony Selection is separate from the Default Selection: the Default Selection is what the project parses and times, and may be large, while the Parsimony Selection is the evidence a linguist chose by hand. Changing one never changes the other.

## Example

```powershell
motif selection set-parsimony --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --name "Evidence" --texts <textGuid>,<textGuid>
```

With `--texts` the command saves a Selection of that name. Without `--texts` the name must already be a saved Selection, and the command points Parsimony at it. A name that is the Default Selection is refused when `--texts` is given, because that would change the Default Selection's Texts.

## What it prints

The command prints the Default Selection, if any, and the Parsimony Selection with its Text count. Add `--json` for the structured response.

## Related commands

- [Show the Default Selection](cmd:selection%20show) shows both Selections.
- [List project Texts](cmd:texts%20list) finds Text GUIDs to select.

entries.title: Show the Default Selection
entries.description: Reads the saved Texts, added words, and limits that determine what an Assessment measures when no other Selection is supplied, and the separate Parsimony Selection.
entries.helpPage:
# Show the Default Selection

`selection show` reads the saved Default Selection for a FieldWorks project, and the Parsimony Selection that Parsimony's Text group reads. It reports the chosen Texts, added words, parsing policy, and revision used by later writes.

## When to use it

Use this before an Assessment when you need to know which words Motif will measure by default. Each Assessment keeps the exact words it resolved, so later edits to this setting do not change earlier evidence.

## Example

```powershell
motif selection show --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --json
```

## What it prints

The command prints the saved Selection name, Text ids, added words, the per-word parser work limit, and whether the time safety net is estimated or explicit. When the added words came from a word-list file with counts, it also names the file, its SHA-256, and how many words have a count. JSON returns the same saved policy and its opaque revision.

## Related commands

- [Choose a Default Selection](cmd:selection%20set-default) changes the saved word list.
- [Choose a Parsimony Selection](cmd:selection%20set-parsimony) saves the Texts Parsimony reads.
- [Set Selection limits](cmd:selection%20set-limits) updates its parsing policy without replacing its chosen words.
- [Measure a Selection](cmd:assess) uses it when no explicit source is supplied.

entries.title: Skip project setup
entries.description: Marks first-time Selection setup as skipped for this project. Use it when the project can be opened but a Default Selection should not be chosen yet.
entries.helpPage:
# Skip project setup

`setup skip` records that first-time Selection setup has been skipped for this project.

## When to use it

Use it when a project is ready to open but nobody should choose a Default Selection yet. This records the choice without creating a Selection or measuring any words.

## Example

```powershell
motif setup skip --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --json
```

## What it prints

The command confirms the setup choice, or returns it as structured JSON. Later, a Default Selection can still be set explicitly.

## Related commands

- [Choose a Default Selection](cmd:selection%20set-default) records the words to measure.
- [Read the project Overview](cmd:overview) reads the latest stored project evidence.

entries.title: Show a Proposal
entries.description: Reads one saved Proposal or Draft by id, with its status, label, Rationale, Comments and operations; --current adds the value each change's field holds now, and an Applied Proposal carries its appliedRecord: the effects and evidence counts Apply saved. In JSON Comments, missing findings means unchecked, [] means checked and clean, and a non-empty array lists findings. It returns the first 10 operations and names the next offset; --limit, --offset, --page and --all read the rest. It does not change the FieldWorks project.
entries.helpPage:
# Show a Proposal

Reads one saved Proposal by its canonical id, or a Draft by name or canonical id, with its status, label, Rationale, Comments and operations. The Rationale shows whether it is out of date and whether you have looked at it; the Comments show whether a person's is newer than the Rationale. It does not change the FieldWorks project.

In the JSON Comment objects returned by `show` and the MCP `motif_proposals` tool, a missing `findings` field means the Comment was not checked. An empty array (`[]`) means it was checked and clean; a non-empty array lists the findings.

`--current` (MCP `current: true`) also reads, from the saved project, the value each change's field holds now, so you can read "old to new" before any Dry Run or Trial. Each operation then carries `current`, a list of `{ target, field, value }` where `value` maps a writing-system tag to its text (empty when the field holds nothing). An operation whose target the Proposal itself creates, or whose field cannot be read, has no `current`. When the saved project cannot be read at all, the Proposal still comes back with `currentUnavailable` saying why. Without `--current` the read opens no project and needs no Trial.

An Applied Proposal also carries `appliedRecord`, read from what Apply saved and not recomputed, so it stays true after the project moves on: `appliedUtc`, `mode`, `message`, `user`, `intentDigest`, `effects` (each `{ target, field, before, after }` as the Apply read it back, in the order it made them) and `evidence` (the counts of each Difference saved for the Proposal before the Apply, newest first, at most 50: `words`, `occurrences`, `improvedWords`, `couldBeBadWords`). The words behind those counts were dropped when the Proposal was decided. A Proposal marked Applied without a saved Receipt has no `appliedRecord`.

## Output size

In JSON (`--json`, and every MCP `motif_proposals` read) `show` returns every operation, so a reader never gets a silent cut; `operationTotal` is the number of operations the Proposal holds, to check the list against. In text, `show` prints the first 10 operations and ends with the `--offset` that reads the next page, or `--all` or `--json` for every operation. `--limit <1-200>` sets the page size, `--offset <n>` or `--page <N>` picks the page (MCP `offset` and `limit`); in JSON a page like that carries `operationsTruncated: true` when it cuts, with `operationTotal`, `operationOffset` and, when more remain, `nextOffset`. An offset past the last operation gives an empty page that still names the total. An offset or limit outside that range is refused with `paging.invalid`.

`compose-batch --json` and the MCP `motif_compose_batch` and compose-steps tools likewise list every operation of every intent; the text report lists the first 25 and says how to read the rest.

entries.title: Show a Corpus
entries.description: Reads the provenance, tokeniser, and licence capabilities recorded for one Corpus. Use it to verify what a Corpus allows before using its text as evidence.
entries.helpPage:
# Show a Corpus

`show-corpus` reads the provenance, tokeniser, and licence capabilities recorded for one Corpus.

## When to use it

Use it before relying on Corpus material as evidence, especially when redistribution or derived use matters. The response preserves unknown licence capabilities instead of treating them as permission.

## Example

```powershell
motif show-corpus --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" stories --json
```

## What it prints

The command displays the selected Corpus and its recorded Documents. JSON returns the full detail response, including the three licence capabilities and their recorded basis.

## Related commands

- [List Corpora](cmd:corpora) finds Corpus ids.
- [Add a Corpus Document](cmd:add-document) records another Document's source.

entries.title: List Sources
entries.description: Lists the Sources the project's Motif Sources list holds, with their Context and any reason one cannot be used. Removed Sources are hidden unless asked for.
entries.helpPage:
# List Sources

`source list` reads the project's "Motif Sources" list from the current Baseline and prints one row per Source: its id, name, status, Context, and the reason when the item cannot be used. A bad item never hides the others.

## Example

```text
motif source list --project Koro.fwdata --json
```

Removed Sources are hidden; `--all` shows them. The list does not open the live FieldWorks project, so `isStale` says whether FieldWorks has saved since the Baseline. A project with no such list has no Sources. Two lists with the same name are refused as ambiguous.

## Related commands

- [Show one Source](cmd:source%20show) reads a Source's Context ranges and folder.
- [Place a chapter](cmd:source%20where) says where a chapter sits.

entries.title: Read a Source Passage
entries.description: Reads a bounded page of word places from a published Source index: a Paratext chapter or a FieldWorks Text. Missing or stale indexes require a refresh; reads never rebuild them and approved state is unavailable.
entries.helpPage:
Read one Passage of a Source as ordered word places: a chapter of a Paratext Source, or a Text of the project's FieldWorks Texts. Each place includes its stable verse anchor, spelling, writing system, wordform key and any indexed reading. Approved state is unavailable.

Use `source passage --project <fwdata> --source <id> --ref "MAT 5"`. For the FieldWorks Texts, name the Source `FIELDWORKS:TEXTS` and the Text by its id; a place is the Text's segment id and word position, and its wordform key keeps the FieldWorks wordform id so homographs stay apart. A Paratext word is a run of characters the project's vernacular writing system calls word-forming, as FieldWorks segments it: an apostrophe, hyphen or digit is part of a word only when the writing system's Valid Characters include it. An index built by an older Motif with a different tokeniser is rebuilt in the background and reads refuse as stale until it finishes. Pages contain 100 places by default, at most 200. Pass the returned opaque cursor unchanged to continue within the same Source, Passage and generation. If the generation changes, start again at the first page.

This read uses an existing index and never rebuilds it. Set the Source folder (Paratext) or capture the saved project to queue a refresh when the index is missing or stale; a saved-project change makes the FieldWorks Texts index stale until it is rebuilt.

entries.title: Show one Source
entries.description: Reads one Source: its Context as book and chapter ranges, how many chapters that is, its folder on this machine and its status.
entries.helpPage:
# Show one Source

`source show <id>` reads one Source from the current Baseline: its Context as book and chapter ranges, how many chapters that is, its status, and the folder recorded for it on this machine (or none). The id is matched ignoring case. A Removed Source can still be shown.

## Example

```text
motif source show --project Koro.fwdata WEB --json
```

The folder lives in a per-user local file and is never part of the project.

## Related commands

- [List Sources](cmd:source%20list) lists every Source.
- [Place a chapter](cmd:source%20where) says where a chapter sits.

entries.title: Place a chapter in the Sources
entries.description: Says whether a chapter is in each Source's Context, is the Current chapter, or comes later.
entries.helpPage:
# Place a chapter in the Sources

`source where <ref>` says where a chapter such as `MAT 5` sits in a Source: `InContext` when its Context includes it, `Current` when it is outside the Context but is the Current chapter, otherwise `Later`. With no `--source` it answers for every Active Source, one row each.

## Example

```text
motif source where --project Koro.fwdata "MAT 5" --source WEB --json
```

When the Source has a folder on this machine, the Paratext text is opened and a chapter the text does not hold is reported as an error on that row. With no folder, the place comes from the Context and the Current chapter alone.

## Related commands

- [Read the Current chapters](cmd:current%20get) reads the Current chapters.
- [Show one Source](cmd:source%20show) reads a Source.

entries.title: Query parse statistics
entries.description: Forwards statistics options to PanGloss using the grammar and cache recorded for an Assessment. Use it to inspect parser work after an Assessment is available.
entries.helpPage:
# Query parse statistics

`stats` forwards a PanGloss statistics query using the grammar and cache recorded for an Assessment. Motif preserves the PanGloss options after `--` instead of interpreting them. Add `--proposal <id>` to use the per-object statistics recorded by that Proposal's latest Trial.

## When to use it

Use this after an Assessment with statistics when you need a focused count or a JSONL result from PanGloss. Put `--json` before `--` to request structured rows from Motif.

## Example

```powershell
motif stats "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --json -- --group word
```

## What it prints

Without `--json`, PanGloss's text output is passed through. With `--json`, Motif returns the selected Assessment, grammar and cache paths, and parsed statistics rows.

## Related commands

- [Measure a Selection](cmd:assess) records Assessment evidence and statistics.
- [Inspect word analyses](cmd:analyses) reads manual and Assessment-backed analysis evidence.

entries.title: Back up a Motif store
entries.description: Writes a consistent copy of the project's Motif store and the files Motif owns for it into a new folder, while other Motif processes keep reading and writing. The receipt lists each file's size and sha256 and the store's schema version. It does not include the FieldWorks project file.
entries.helpPage:
# Back up a Motif store

`store backup` writes a consistent copy of a project's Motif store, and the files Motif owns for the project, into a new folder. It is the backup you take before switching Motif versions, or before anything else you may want to undo. It backs up only the Motif store: the project's `.fwdata` file is not included.

```powershell
motif store backup --project "D:\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata"
motif store backup --project "D:\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --to "D:\Backups\koro-before-switch" --json
```

Without `--to` the backup goes into a timestamped folder beside the store, named `<project>.motif-backup-<time>`. A folder named with `--to` must be missing or empty, and must not be the store file or lie inside a folder Motif owns: the store's `trial-exports` folder or `<project>.motif-backups` (`store.backup-destination-owned`), so a backup never contains a backup. The check follows symlinks and junctions to their real target, and Windows 8.3 short names to their long names, so a `--to` reached through a link into those folders is refused too.

The store is copied with SQLite's online backup, so the copy is one consistent snapshot even while a runner or another command is reading or writing the store. The command takes the same shared lease every reader takes, so it refuses only when another Motif process is resetting or restoring the store (`project.busy`). If the store stays locked past the busy timeout it refuses with `cli.store-busy`; repeat the call.

The folder holds `store.sqlite`, plus `Config.motif.toml` (the project's `.motif.toml`), `store.upgrade.json` and the `trial-exports` folder when they exist, and `motif-backup.json`, the receipt. The receipt, which is also the command's JSON, lists each file's path, size and sha256, the store's schema version and the project it belongs to: its LibLCM project GUID (when the project file has one), its identity and its path.

The FieldWorks project file is not included: `fwDataIncluded` is `false`. Back that up with FieldWorks' own store backup.

A project with no Motif store refuses with `store.backup-no-store`; a destination that already holds files refuses with `store.backup-destination-exists`. Restore a backup with [`store restore`](cmd:store%20restore).

entries.title: Prune project store
entries.description: Removes older Assessments that are no longer needed by retained evidence. It also reclaims available space in the project store.
entries.helpPage:
# Prune the project store

`store prune` removes older Assessments that are not needed by retained evidence and reclaims available store space.

Motif keeps the newest 20 standalone Assessments of each kind by default (5 for Object Timing, whose per-object tables are large), along with pinned, current, and cited evidence. Set `standalone-assessments-per-kind` in the `[retention]` section of the project configuration to change the count. Unneeded standalone and decided Proposal Assessments older than 90 days are removed, as are all but the newest 30 Assessments of each kind on a decided Proposal. The store targets 100 MB: when it holds more, the oldest evidence that nothing needs goes next, including evidence of Proposals already decided, and never evidence of an open Proposal. Authored and protected evidence may keep a store above the target. A decided Proposal keeps its summary and loses its word detail. When deleted rows leave a large share of the file free, this command rewrites the file to give the space back; the worker does the same once a day for the stores it has open. Motif also prunes after a successful Assessment, without the rewrite.

```powershell
motif store prune --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata"
```

A completed Trial holds its Before and After Assessments only while its Proposal is undecided; once the Proposal is applied, withdrawn, declined or superseded, its Trial evidence may go like the rest of that Proposal's evidence. After pruning the store, the command removes this project's run directories that the store no longer names once they are an hour old, and sweeps the per-user data folder with no size limit: every run, project source copy and Baseline that no project store names and that is an hour old goes, unless a parse is reading it.

The result reports the number of Assessments and invocation directories removed and the store file size before and after reclamation. It also reports the store's byte budget and the bytes in use, the kept Assessments counted by reason (such as `openProposal`, `current`, `pinned`, `report`, `openTrial`, `lineage` or `withinLimits`), the kept run directories by reason, and what the per-user data sweep removed and kept. Directories whose ownership cannot be proven are kept; the result reports their count, total size and parent path so they can be inspected. Active readers can postpone reclaiming some space; run the command again after they finish.

entries.title: Relocate a copied store
entries.description: After a project and its Motif store are copied or moved together, points the store at the project's new path so commands stop refusing it as another project's. It checks the new path holds the same project, needs confirmation, and records the old path, new path, time and basis in the store.
entries.helpPage:
# Relocate a copied store

`store relocate` points a project's Motif store at the project's new path. Use it after a project and its `.motif.db` file were copied or moved together, when other commands refuse the store as belonging to a different project.

```powershell
motif store relocate --project "D:\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --confirm "Point this Motif store at this project's new path?"
```

Pass the project at its new path. The store is the `.motif.db` file beside it. Without the confirmation phrase the command changes nothing and shows the phrase to pass.

The command relocates a store only to the same project. It compares the new file's FieldWorks language project GUID with the GUID in the store's Baselines or, when the store holds none, in the project file at the old path if that still exists. Different GUIDs refuse with `store.other-project` and leave the store untouched. When neither exists to compare, the command refuses with `store.relocate-identity-unproven`. If you know it is the same project, run it again with `--match-by-name`: the project name the store is bound to must still match, the result reports `identityEvidence` as `name`, and the store records that basis.

It refuses while another program has the project open, and while any Motif process has the store open. Close FieldWorks and Motif first.

The change and a record of it commit together: the store keeps the old path, the new path, the time and the basis in its `StoreRelocations` history. The result reports both paths, the time, and `changed`, which is `false` when the store already pointed at the new path. It also reports `oldProjectStillExists`, which is `true` after a copy: that old project and its own store are not touched, and this store now belongs to the new path.
usage: Usage: motif store relocate --project <fwdata> --confirm "Point this Motif store at this project's new path?" [--match-by-name] [--json]

entries.title: Restore a Motif store
entries.description: Puts a Motif backup back beside the project after checking every file against its receipt. It refuses while the store is open or busy, when the backup is of a newer schema or a different project (unless --force is given), and when a file does not match its sha256. It never deletes: the old store, its -wal and -shm, and any owned file the backup lacks move into a pre-restore folder before the restored files are renamed in.
entries.helpPage:
# Restore a Motif store

`store restore` puts a backup made by [`store backup`](cmd:store%20backup) back beside the project.

```powershell
motif store restore "D:\Backups\koro-before-switch" --project "D:\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata"
```

Pass the backup folder (or its `motif-backup.json`). Before it changes anything the command refuses when:

- the store is open or busy in another Motif process (`project.busy`); close the runner with `motif worker stop` and repeat;
- the backup's store schema is newer than this build understands (`store.restore-newer-schema`); update Motif first;
- a file's sha256 or size differs from the receipt (`store.restore-checksum-mismatch`), checked on the copy staged beside the target;
- the folder has no readable receipt, the receipt names a file outside the backup, lists a file twice or lists a file the folder lacks (`store.restore-invalid`);
- the backup is of another project (`store.restore-other-project`). The receipt records the project's LibLCM project GUID and its identity; a restore matches the GUID, or the identity when either file has no GUID. The path in the receipt is only information, so a project that was moved or renamed restores fine. Pass `--force` to restore a backup of a different project anyway.

Otherwise it takes the store's exclusive lease, stages every file beside its target, and folds the old store's write-ahead log into its main file so no committed transaction lives only in a sidecar (if that cannot finish, the restore refuses with `project.store-io` and changes nothing). Nothing is deleted. The old store, with its `-wal`, `-shm` and `-journal` files, and every other file it replaces or the backup lacks (the project's `.motif.toml`, the upgrade report, the `trial-exports` files) are moved into `<project>.motif-backups/pre-restore-<time>/moved`, and the staged files are renamed into place. That move is the only copy of the old store (its raw files reproduce it exactly), so nothing is stored twice, and a store too damaged to read is moved aside the same way, so a good backup can still replace it. The result lists each restored file, each file moved aside with its reason (`replaced` or `not-in-backup`), and the pre-restore folder.

A restore that fails while the process lives puts everything back and names the pre-restore folder. If the process dies partway, the project is in one of these states, and running the same restore again finishes it, into the same pre-restore folder (marked `restore-incomplete` until it finishes), and removes the leftover `*.restore-*` staged files:

1. Before anything moved: the old project is untouched.
2. Other owned files swapped, the old store not yet moved: the old store beside the new config and trial files.
3. The `-wal`, `-shm` and `-journal` files moved first, the old store not yet: the old store is live and complete, since its WAL was folded in first; no orphan `-wal` is left at the path.
4. The old store moved too, the new store not yet renamed: there is no store and no sidecar at the path, the complete old files are in `moved`, and the complete new store is staged. Motif sees no store, never a half one.
5. The new store renamed: done.
