An older backup is restored as it is; Motif upgrades it the next time it opens it. The FieldWorks project file is never touched.

entries.title: Upgrade project store
entries.description: Carries authored work into the current store and keeps a backup of the old store. Computed results are discarded and can be recreated.
entries.helpPage:
# Upgrade a project store

`store upgrade` carries authored work from an older Motif store into the current format. Motif keeps the old
store as a versioned backup and discards computed results, which can be recreated. The one computed result it
keeps is the saved Difference summary of each decided or deferred Proposal, because it cannot be recreated once
the Proposal is set aside; the word detail under it is discarded. Summaries are kept from schema 56 on; an upgrade from an
older schema drops them, because they are in a shape this Motif cannot read.

```powershell
motif store upgrade --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata"
```

Opening a project also upgrades its older store automatically. The upgrade report beside the store lists the
rows carried, tables discarded, and any Proposal revisions that the current Motif cannot read.

To inspect an older store without changing it, give an existing source and a new output path:

```powershell
motif store upgrade --source old.motif.db --out upgraded.motif.db --json
```

entries.title: List project Texts
entries.description: Lists Text records from the project's current Baseline with their identity and interlinearization data. Use it to find Text ids for a Default Selection or Assessment.
entries.helpPage:
# List project Texts

`texts list` reads Text records from the project's current Baseline and returns their GUIDs, titles, and interlinearization data.

## When to use it

Use this to find Text GUIDs before choosing them for a Default Selection or an Assessment. The command reads the Baseline, so capture one after saving project changes if you need to see newly added Texts. Titles help a person recognize a Text; the GUID is the stable selector.

## Example

```powershell
motif texts list --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --json
```

## What it prints

Human output lists each Text's title, interlinearization percentage, and GUID. JSON returns those details with a flag showing whether a Baseline was available; without a Baseline, human output asks you to capture one first.

## Related commands

- [Choose a Default Selection](cmd:selection%20set-default) stores Text GUIDs for later runs.
- [Measure a Selection](cmd:assess) can measure words from named Texts.

entries.title: Inspect parse timing
entries.description: Reads timing evidence for an Assessment, optionally narrowed to words or grouped by kind or rule. Use it to locate expensive parsing work after an Assessment. The result says whether parser work by object is available (parserWorkByObjectAvailable) and, when it is not, why (parserWorkByObjectAbsentReason): retried-words, word-without-work, object-without-work-or-identity, no-unattributed-row, sums-do-not-match, not-whole-run, or statistics-unavailable.
entries.helpPage:
# Inspect parse timing

`timing` reads timing measurements recorded in an Assessment. It can narrow the result to words and group costs by kind or rule. Add `--proposal <id>` to use the latest Trial's measurements.

## When to use it

Use this when an Assessment shows costly parsing and you want to identify which rules or kinds account for the parser's work. Name an Assessment when the project has more than one measurement.

Without `--assessment`, Timing reads the Default Selection's current results, including explicit replacements made with `assess --replaces`. Naming an Assessment reads its original words and measurements. Explicit timing overrides replace only words that run measured; they cannot add other words to it.

## Example

```powershell
motif timing --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --proposal <proposalId> --by rule --top 10
```

## What it prints

The command compares parser work only when the Trial retained a compatible Baseline Assessment for the selected words. It reports the percentage change for the selected scope and individual words. Object changes require complete work counters for the same words and a matching object identity on both sides. A new object, missing detail, a stopped search, a zero Baseline or an incompatible parser makes the affected comparison unavailable; the command gives a reason instead of estimating it.

`--rule` takes `kind:key`, such as `morph_rule:12345678-1234-1234-abcd-123456789abc`. Names are display labels; object identities distinguish rules with the same name. `--json` returns the comparisons as structured data.

JSON identifies each word's producing Assessment, invocation and measurement time. It also records the selected run's Baseline and captured FieldWorks save, when available. Its evidence relationship distinguishes Current, Historical, SavedSince and Unknown; current-project freshness is reported separately, so a new Baseline does not make an old measurement current.

## Related commands

- [Measure a Selection](cmd:assess) creates timing evidence.
- [Query parse statistics](cmd:stats) forwards a query to PanGloss for detailed counts.

entries.title: Trace a word
entries.description: Runs PanGloss for one word against the project's current Baseline and returns its diagnostic. Use it to inspect recorded analyses and trace events.
entries.helpPage:
# Trace a word

`trace` runs PanGloss for one word against the project's current Baseline and reads the diagnostic shown by Why This Analysis?. Add `--proposal <id>` to trace against that Proposal's Trial copy. It does not change the project or store a new Assessment. The trace runs under a parser work limit: the frozen limit of that Trial when you give `--proposal`, otherwise the limit a Trial would freeze now (a saved Default Selection's or scope's limit when it differs from the default of 20,000,000, then the project's `[parser] work-limit`, then the default). The response says which limit it used in `workLimitUsed`. A trace stops a word at the parser work limit, so a word that once traced to completion can now say "work limit reached" with its work count. To trace it further, raise the limit with `[parser] work-limit` in the project's `motif.toml` (see [Show the project configuration](cmd:config%20show)).

## Trace a word now

```powershell
motif trace --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --word mirusi
```

Add `--json` to get the typed response, including the shared `reading` and the diagnostic's recorded provenance. A clean process exit does not establish that the parser's work limit or time safety net was not reached; when the diagnostic cannot report that, completion is unknown.

If the project has no Baseline, capture one with `motif baseline capture --project <fwdata>` before tracing. Trace uses that saved grammar; it does not inspect unsaved FieldWorks changes.

For an unparsed word, text output names the shape whose recorded lexical lookup found no root and explains recorded refusal codes. A stem that reaches an unapplied required template has a different reason from an attempt that builds the wrong surface. A recorded code can be explained without an owner's detailed explanation; absent details remain unavailable. A trace without recorded reasons says so, and an unfinished search cannot establish that the word has no analysis.

When Motif captures a trace, `hostCapture.lexiconEntryCount` records the number of lexical entries in the exact Baseline or Trial copy used. A completed trace with an empty lexicon names that fact and the word, instead of guessing which affix or spelling is wrong. A missing count is unknown. Saved traces retain this count and their recorded reasons without opening the current project.

## Trace a Trial report case

A report-bound trace selects an exact case and side: `motif proposal trial --project <fwdata> <proposalId> --report <reportId> --case <caseKey> --trace --side after`. Motif uses the recorded parser, grammar and limits or explains that the exact inputs are unavailable. The diagnostic has its own identity and completion; it does not alter the batch report.

## Read a saved trace

```powershell
motif trace --load "C:\Temp\mirusi.trace.json"
```

`--load` reads the saved PanGloss diagnostic without opening a project or running a parser. It uses the same reader as a live trace, so the returned word, analyses, attempts, and recorded tree share one interpretation. Why This Analysis? translates the recorded refusal code into a sentence while retaining the code and the original evidence. A rule or required feature is named only when recorded; neighboring events do not establish which rule caused a failure. The window folds forward building events into Plain and keeps the full parser order in Expert.

## Related commands

- [Load a saved trace](cmd:trace%20--load) reads a diagnostic without a parser.
- [Prepare an AI Handoff](cmd:handoff) writes project context and retained parse evidence.
- [Measure a Selection](cmd:assess) records parse results for chosen words.
- [Why a word lost a Reading](cmd:proposal%20why-lost) compares one word's trace at the Baseline and on a Proposal's Trial copy.

entries.title: Trial a Proposal
entries.description: Measures a Proposal on a throwaway copy and records review evidence, always including declared gate word sets. Read named losses, incomplete cases and new second readings held for review before deciding what to do.
entries.helpPage:
# Trial a Proposal

A Trial measures a Proposal on a throwaway copy. It records a Dry Run and parser evidence so that you can review changes before deciding what to do.

Run `motif trial --project <fwdata> <proposalId> --wait`, which prints the report summary when the Trial completes (with `--json`, the same summary `motif_trial` returns). Its `gate` is `green`, `loss` or `unmeasured`, and the exit code is 0, 6 or 2 (see [Read Trial progress](cmd:trial%20--wait)); `--expect-loss <file>` lists words you mean to lose. Read the saved report again later with `motif proposal trial --project <fwdata> <proposalId>`; it needs no developer setting. Select named review sets with `--review-set <id,...>`, or use `--review-set none` to omit optional sets. Sets required by `[gate] word-sets` in `<project>.motif.toml` are always included. Word files contain one word per line and are limited to 8 MiB of valid UTF-8 text.

The summary names observed red flags and separately reports incomplete evidence. No red flags means only “not bad”, never “good”. Use `--detail failures` for bounded samples and `--detail full` for pages of all captured cases. Select a section with `--section`, and use its continuation cursor to read another page. With `--case`, choose the `readings`, `expectations`, `memberships` or `sources` section to page that case’s details; `--side` selects before or after readings. `--word-results` is an alias for the first full word page.

Use `--job` or `--report` to select a particular Trial or saved report. `--refresh-report` explicitly produces a new report from retained evidence; a normal read does not rerun the parser. A report can have limitations when the original Trial did not retain a comparable check, set or other evidence.

For one exact case, use `--case <caseKey> --trace --side before` or `--side after`. Tracing may run a diagnostic against the report’s recorded grammar, parser and settings; a missing input requires a new Trial. A diagnostic can differ from the saved batch evidence and does not change the report.

Add `--wait-terminal` when running a Trial to cancel its job at the wait limit or on Ctrl+C. Motif allows up to eight more seconds to record cancellation and confirm cleanup. The refusal includes the job ID, the last observed status and whether cleanup was confirmed.

After Motif's own Apply, the next Trial captures a new Baseline. After a save made outside Motif, measuring pending changes is refused with `change.refresh-required` until you capture a new Baseline with `motif baseline capture`.

A new second reading on an attested word is held for review: `report.heldWords` lists the words and the gate is `unmeasured` until the added reading is independently approved and a fresh Trial captures that approval. The named holds, losses and attributed stops survive the detail budget, including stops with no morphology packet. An undispatched case remains not measured and has no invented per-word stop.

A Trial that loses words or confirmed readings names them in `report.regressions` (the summary prints them as `Regressed words`). There is one group per cause, `new-word-failures` (no parse, or an Approved reading lost) and `confirmed-readings-lost`. A group lists at most 10 words, each with its reading counts and its analyses before and after (up to three per side; `no analysis` when the word no longer parses), then the count of the rest and a `nextStep` command that pages all of them: `motif proposal trial --project <fwdata> <proposalId> --detail full --section wordforms --flag <cause> --limit 200`. The text summary shows the first two words of each cause on one line (`--json` has all 10), and also stops the `Unexpected losses` and `Expected losses` lists at 10 words; `--json` gives every one. It names the words and what changed for them, not the operation that caused it. Each word also carries the ids of its analyses, the `motif parse <word> --trace --at baseline` and `--at <proposalId>` commands that trace it, and `touchedBy`, the Proposal operations that name an object its Baseline analysis uses. That list is an overlap of ids, not a cause; null means it was not computed and a `regression-overlap-not-computed` Limitation says why. A report whose saved word detail cannot be read keeps its summary and carries the limitation `regressions-unavailable` instead.

Older saved reports without compact gate facts are explicitly `unmeasured`. Use `--refresh-report` to rebuild named facts from the original retained evidence, or rerun the Trial when those inputs are unavailable. Motif never guesses lost-word names from counts.

Autonomous Apply also requires a [declared gate](cmd:config%20show), the current declaration and exact required word-set scope, a green newest Trial, and unchanged live project and writing-system state.

## Working-set Trials

`motif trial --project <fwdata> <proposalId> --words <file> --no-base-sample --wait` (MCP `no_base_sample`) parses exactly the words in the file and adds no review word set, including the sets `[gate] word-sets` requires. Use it in development loops of up to 500 chosen words; run the ordinary Trial, with its base sample, once per round. It needs `--words`, and it cannot be combined with `--all-words` or `--review-set`.

The report and the saved Trial record `sample: "working-set"` (an ordinary Trial records `stratified`) with `sampleWords` and `wordListDigest`. A working-set Trial is never a gate or a baseline: it has no declared gate, Autonomous Apply and ordinary Apply readiness ignore it, and `difference produce` refuses it. `proposal compare` compares working-set Trials only with each other, over the same `wordListDigest`.

## Touched words

`--touched` (MCP `touched`) needs `--words` and adds to the list every attested word whose stored Baseline analysis uses an object the Proposal edits, so a change to a stem or affix is measured on the words that carry it, not only on the words you chose. The Proposal's touched objects are each operation's target, the owner a create adds to and the neighbours an ordering is placed against. An entry stands for its lexeme form, alternate forms and grammatical infos, a sense for its grammatical info, and an environment for the allomorphs that use it. Matching is by exact id, never by spelling, against the Baseline Assessment of the current Baseline, so it reaches only the words that Assessment holds and ignores a disapproved analysis. At most 500 words are added; standard error says how many matched and were not added. It is refused with `trial.touched-needs-words` without `--words`, `trial.touched-no-baseline` when no Assessment matches the Baseline, and `trial.touched-no-objects` when no edited object is in the Baseline (a Proposal that only creates new objects touches no existing word). Rules, slots, features, inflection classes and other objects a reading does not name are not matched, and are never dropped silently: standard error (and the MCP tool's next step) names each kind not traced to words with a count and says the touched set may be incomplete, so add `--words` for the words those edits affect. It also says how many Baseline words were searched, and of how many attested when the Assessment covers fewer, so "added 0" is not read as "nothing is touched". If every target is of a kind that is not matched, `trial.touched-no-objects` names them.

## Foreground-only

`--no-background` (MCP `no_background`) needs `--wait`. A Baseline recapture the Trial needs runs inline, and no Parsimony job is queued after the Trial completes, so nothing commits after the command returns.

Add `--verbose` with `--wait` to print the Trial's phase timings (where the time went, and whether the before-side parse was reused) to standard error after the report.

The default wait is 120 seconds (`--wait-timeout-ms 120000`). When it expires the job keeps running, and the command exits with code 3 and the `job.wait-timeout` refusal, which is not a failed Trial: its `jobId` fact names the job, and `motif jobs wait <jobId> --project <fwdata> --wait-timeout-ms <ms>` resumes the wait.

entries.title: Read Trial progress
entries.description: Waits for a Trial job and reads its state. Read the stored review report after the Trial completes.
entries.helpPage:
# Read Trial progress

Waits for a Trial job and reads its state. When the job completes, `motif trial --wait` prints the Trial's review summary; with `--json` it is the same summary `motif_trial` returns, with a `gate` that a script can exit on.

| Gate | What it means | Exit code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `green` | No unexpected loss, blocking incomplete evidence or review hold remains; every declared required case was measured. | 0 |
| `loss` | A measured word went from analysed to no analysis, or lost a confirmed reading, and the word was not listed as an expected loss. A loss wins over `unmeasured`. | 6 |
| `unmeasured` | The Trial measured no words, left required cases unmeasured, was interrupted, did not finish (for example the parser was killed), or stopped a word by budget or timeout that had an analysis before the change. A new second reading held for review, or a declared gain/Parsimony hold, also prevents green. | 2 |

A word that was stopped but had no analysis before the change does not change the gate. The gate names stopped words that had a Baseline analysis under `stoppedWords`, expected losses under `expectedLosses` and unlisted losses under `unexpectedLosses`. The report also keeps every stopped word in `report.stoppedWords`, including words with no Baseline analysis: each names its before or after side, reason codes and specific parser explanation. For `invalid-evidence`, the explanation identifies the invalid shape or morphology evidence. These diagnostics remain available when the optional detail index is not retained.

The gate reads the Trial's retained evidence, so `--review-set none` does not hide a loss. `--expect-loss <file>` names words, one per line (blank lines are ignored, and a word matches whatever its Unicode normalisation), that the change intends to lose, such as retirements; it needs `--wait`. Listed words do not make the gate a loss; any other lost word still fails. The summary prints whatever the gate. Read the saved report later with [Read a Trial report](cmd:proposal%20trial).

If PanGloss is killed by a signal or terminated by the operating system, the Job is `failed` with `failureCategory` `parser-killed` and `failureCode` `assess.parser-killed`. The waited command exits 2, even when the parser wrote partial or complete-looking output. If there is memory evidence, the category is `out-of-memory` and the code is `assess.out-of-memory` instead. A completed Dry Run and retained partial review evidence remain available; the failed run does not publish a completed Trial.

With `--json`, a terminal Job that could not finish the Trial is printed as one JSON object on stdout, with its status and failure category. Warnings and diagnostics go to stderr. An enqueue refusal is a FailureEnvelope on stderr.

The stored result keeps its `gate` and `report.losses`: `newNoParseWords` and `newApprovedLossWords` name every affected word, and `newlyLostReadings` names each word and frozen reading identity. These lists survive when the optional detail index exceeds the store budget. For each word listed in `--expect-loss`, `newlyLostReadings` also carries one row per lost Reading with its canonical `signature` (ordered morphemes), the lost copy `count` and `remainingReadingCount` (lexicon-backed Readings still emitted); a word that lost every Reading lists them all with zero remaining. `losses.retirementAttestation` is bound to the report digest and its `complete` is true only when those rows cover the full retirement multiset of the waived words across every measured case; `limitations` says why not. The saved report keeps every retirement row; a read returns the rows filled to a 16 KB bound and `retirementAttestation.page`, `pageCount` and `rowCount` say how many exist, and `--page <N>` reads the others (`--report` pins the exact saved report). Nothing is refused for size. Rows with a `signature` (the retirement multiset) and rows without one (confirmed losses of frozen expectations) describe the same loss from two sides: a gate must read each kind on its own and must not sum across the two kinds. Expected losses are frozen when the Trial is queued; later reads keep that Trial’s verdict.

When a word had a Baseline analysis but its spelling cannot be segmented by the candidate phoneme inventory, the parser may mark it `skipped`. This is a named loss, including any confirmed readings it lost, rather than a pass or an unknown search result. Malformed evidence cannot establish that loss. A listed intended inventory loss is covered by the Trial's saved expected losses.

`report.regressions` names up to 10 lost or regressed words per cause with their analyses before and after, the count of the rest and a `nextStep` to page them; see [Trial a Proposal](cmd:trial). The printed `Unexpected losses` list stops at 10 words (`--json` lists all).

Sets required by `[gate] word-sets` are measured even with `--review-set none`; [config show](cmd:config%20show) documents the declaration. Held second readings are named in `report.heldWords`, independently of the detail budget. Independently approve the added reading and run a fresh Trial to clear that hold. Older reports without compact gate facts are unmeasured: use `proposal trial --refresh-report` with retained inputs, or rerun the Trial.

Add `--wait-terminal` to cancel the exact Trial at the wait deadline and return after its execution and parser processes have stopped. The `job.wait-timeout` refusal reports the terminal job `status` and `jobId`. With an ordinary wait, the Trial can keep running after the wait expires.

entries.title: Read grammar warnings
entries.description: Reads stored grammar findings and allomorph refusals from parsing, with filters by code or warning level. Confirmed uses of Selection words stay separate from spelling and membership matches. It returns the first 10 findings with the full counts and names the next offset; --limit, --offset, --page and --all read the rest.
entries.helpPage:
# Read grammar warnings

`warnings` reads grammar-check findings and allomorph refusals already recorded by parsing for a project. It can filter by diagnostic code or show only findings at warning level. Add `--proposal <id>` to read the check stored with that Proposal's latest Trial. When the current Baseline has not been checked, `warnings` refuses and tells you to run `grammar check`; it does not return an empty findings list.

PanGloss reports an unreadable phonological environment as a warning. Roots ignore that restriction but keep valid ones; ordinary affixes add an unrestricted pass beside valid passes; an infix with no valid position is skipped.

## When to use it

Use it after [Check a grammar](cmd:grammar%20check) when you want to inspect reported findings. Combine `--kind` and `--left-out` to narrow a large result without rerunning the check.

## Example

```powershell
motif warnings --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata" --left-out --json
```

## What it prints

The response includes separate error, warning, and information counts, plus findings with PanGloss-owned titles, explanations, guidance, optional background, verified FieldWorks places, subjects, and links where available. Information can identify a stored analysis that PanGloss no longer reproduces, name the rule that changed its surface, or explain why the loss could not be attributed. Each finding retains the report locale. Missing references and project settings have explicit statuses and unavailable-link reasons. `--left-out` keeps warning-level findings only. Without a Baseline, the command refuses and tells you to run `motif baseline capture --project <fwdata>`. When a Baseline has no stored check, it refuses and tells you to run `motif grammar check --project <fwdata>`.

The response includes the Baseline's lexical entry and rule counts when that inventory is available. Motif advisories are listed separately from parser findings.

Motif findings include `grammar.required-slot-empty` when a required inflectional slot in a template has no affixes. Each finding names the template, part of speech, slot and canonical slot ID. The slot is marked required, but FieldWorks and PanGloss currently treat an empty required slot as optional.

Motif findings also include `grammar.negated-feature-value` for a stored negated feature value, which FieldWorks' parser loader cannot read. Each finding names the feature, the value and the object that holds it, and, for a stem or inflectional affix, points to [removing the feature value](cmd:compose-remove-feature-value); for other objects it says Motif has no command for it.

Motif findings also include `grammar.derived-stem-keeps-from-class` for a derivational affix with a From Inflection Class and no To Inflection Class. Each finding names the affix and the class its derived stems keep, and says to set a To Inflection Class when they belong to another class.

Motif findings also include `grammar.template-has-no-slots` for an affix template with no slot, which the parser cannot use. Each finding names the template and its part of speech and says to add a slot.

Motif findings also include `grammar.phoneme-case-alias-missing` when a featured lowercase phoneme lacks titlecase or uppercase spellings on the same phoneme. It names the missing aliases and points to [Edit a phoneme](cmd:compose-edit-phoneme), so implicit featureless capitals do not admit unintended analyses.

Motif findings also include `grammar.phoneme-spelling-ambiguous` for a phoneme whose spelling is other phonemes' spellings joined (`ng` beside `n` and `g`), which the parser always reads as the longest spelling, and `grammar.allomorph-environment-ignored-by-parser` for a form whose environment the parser cannot read and so drops, leaving the form unrestricted by it. Each finding names the phoneme or form and says what to change.

Motif findings also include `grammar.allomorph-repeats-environment-material` for a form that already spells the material its environment asks of its neighbour (`batan-ung` before `ng`); it is a second look, not a refusal.

Motif findings also include three lexicon hygiene warnings: `lexicon.stem-typed-as-content-word` for a Noun, Verb or Adjective stem that is a single letter, a cross-reference stub or a function word by its gloss, `lexicon.duplicate-entry` for entries with the same form and first gloss, and `lexicon.affix-hyphen-on-wrong-side` for a prefix written `-i` or a suffix written `i-`. They report only; see [`grammar-check`](cmd:grammar%20check) for what each looks for and how to fix many at once.

When a stored Assessment matches the Baseline and Selection, all recorded allomorph segmentation refusals are included under `parse.allomorph.unsegmentable`, labelled **Parse all words**. Their descriptions preserve the parser's reason, without truncating the allomorph list or inventing guidance. These findings can differ from the whole-grammar check's findings.

## Your words

When a stored Assessment from [Measure a Selection](cmd:assess) matches the current Baseline and Selection, each finding lists the words in the Selection reached by its subjects, with their meanings, such as Lost or Kept. The headline counts exact uses only, once per word, and says how many of those don't parse. Membership and spelling candidates have separate counts and never enter that headline. Each kind of finding gets the same separate counts.

Motif finds the words from the object the finding names, by its FieldWorks identity:

- an allomorph or grammatical info: the FieldWorks or parser analyses that use it;
- an entry or an environment: the FieldWorks or parser analyses that use its allomorphs;
- a sense: the FieldWorks or parser analyses that use its grammatical info;
- a natural class: the allomorphs its environments condition, and the words the phonological rules that name it ran in;
- a rule: the words its stored per-word timings say it ran in.
- a feature definition, value or specification: the allomorphs, grammatical infos and rules whose feature specifications name it;
- a stem name or inflection class: the allomorphs or grammatical infos that refer to it;
- a boundary: the allomorphs and rules whose contexts name it.

Templates and slots reach words using their affixes as **membership candidates**. Inflection types, ad hoc prohibitions, phoneme sets and feature systems also reach members as candidates: using a member does not prove a parse selected the named resource.

Letters and phonemes reach **spelling candidates; not confirmed uses of the phoneme**. Spelling uses case-insensitive, canonically decomposed substring matching, which cannot establish phoneme identity. A feature owned by a phoneme keeps that same limit, including when reached through its feature system. A phoneme set follows its members' grammar references and omits spelling candidates.

For a word with no analysis, an allomorph or entry also reaches spelling candidates through the vernacular forms recorded for the Baseline. This includes typed words the parser refused. The window calls these **spelling matches**, lists the words, and never presents the spelling alone as an exact use.

For each finding, exact uses take precedence over membership candidates, then spelling candidates. The lists never share a word. The overall counts apply that precedence across all findings, too. The words show use, not cause: a word that uses what a warning names may fail for some other reason.

Every finding has an attribution state. A supported route with no matching word says **none in this Selection**. A project resource without word attribution says **project-wide**. A **missing object** distinguishes a GUID absent from the checked Baseline from one belonging to a different FieldWorks class. **Unresolved identity** distinguishes no subject, a named subject without a project GUID, and a class with no supported route.

Features also follow shared references to their enclosing complex specifications. If some feature owners have no supported route or no word attribution, the finding retains those attribution limits alongside any exact uses or candidates. When no owner has a supported route, the finding reports the limit rather than claiming there are no words in the Selection.

Without a matching Assessment, supported routes say **evidence unavailable**; their counts are absent rather than zero. Missing and unresolved subjects retain their specific reasons. Motif refuses stores with an older shape and asks the developer to delete the database so it can recreate it.

## Related commands

- [Check a grammar](cmd:grammar%20check) records fresh findings.
- [Read the project Overview](cmd:overview) includes the warning count with other stored evidence.

## Output size

`warnings` returns the first 10 findings. The counts, the per-code rows (`byKind`) and the word attribution always describe every finding; `findingsTotal`, `findingsOffset` and, when more remain, `nextOffset` say which page this is. The text ends with the `--offset` that reads the next page. `--limit <1-200>` sets the page size, `--offset <n>` or `--page <N>` picks the page, and `--all` returns every finding (MCP `all: true`). Narrow with `--kind` before paging. An offset or limit outside that range is refused with `paging.invalid`. The text lists the 20 largest finding codes and names how many more `--json` holds.

entries.title: Why a word did not parse
entries.description: Asks PanGloss whether a word parses as each morph sequence you expected, and for a rejection names the first failing constraint, the morphs and the grammar object it is about. Use it to see why a word did not parse as these morphs.
entries.helpPage:
# Why a word did not parse

`why-not <word> --expect <morphs>` answers one question: why did this word not parse as the morphs you expected? You give the word and one or more candidates, each a morph sequence in surface order. For every candidate PanGloss says whether the word parses along it and, if not, the first constraint that fails. It reads the project's current Baseline, or a Proposal's Trial copy with `--at <proposal-id>`, and changes nothing. Motif reasons about no grammar itself: every answer is something PanGloss reported. The MCP tool `motif_why_not` takes the same fields, with `expect` as a list.

```text
motif why-not kibakek --project <fwdata> --expect kib,ak,ek --expect kib,ak|ik,ek --json
```

## Writing a candidate

- `,` separates positions, in surface order. `|` offers several choices at one position, and the answer says which one worked.
- A morph is its `grammar.xml` id. `id@allomorph-id` pins an allomorph.
- To name a morph by FieldWorks identity, write `entryGuid:msaGuid`; each side is a GUID or a Motif id. `id=entryGuid:msaGuid` gives the id and has PanGloss check the guids belong to it.
- Candidates by id and by guid can share one call; naming a morph by guid alone needs a PanGloss that declares `interfaces.whyNot.expectGuidChoices`, and Motif refuses the call otherwise. Pinning an allomorph on a guid-only choice works only when the guid names a single morpheme; otherwise PanGloss refuses it.
- Up to 16 candidates, 32 positions each and 16 choices per position. `--expect` repeats.

## What you get

- **Accepted, rejected or unknown, per candidate.** An accepted candidate lists the morphs of the derivation. A rejected one gives the failure `kind`, a sentence, the 0-based `position`, the morphs involved, and whether HermitCrab reported it or PanGloss inferred it. An unknown one gives the stop reason, such as `work_cap`, and what was reached.
- **The kinds that can be answered.** The output lists the failure kinds the installed PanGloss answers, read from its `--describe`. Any other failure comes back unknown, never guessed.
- **The grammar object and its FieldWorks target.** A rejection names the object a fix would touch: its type, its `grammar.xml` id and, when PanGloss supplies one, its FieldWorks guid. An environment failure also gives the allomorph, the environment's place in its list, its authored text such as `/[V]_` and the text around the allomorph. An allomorph's environments are any-of, so when every one failed the output names the allomorph and lists each environment with its text and guid. A co-occurrence prohibition lists every morph it names, with the entry, analysis and form guids. Guids appear when the grammar came from a FieldWorks project snapshot; the output says `no FieldWorks target yet` where PanGloss gave none, as for a hand-written grammar or a prohibition the parser cannot tell from an equal one.
- **Best.** The first accepted candidate, otherwise the rejected one that got furthest.

## Bounds

The output keeps at most 16 morphs and 8 feature clashes per answer and cuts each parser sentence at 400 characters; it counts what it left out. PanGloss spends at most 30 seconds on each concrete morph sequence before it answers unknown.

## When it refuses

It refuses, with its own code and a sentence, a request it cannot send, a PanGloss that does not declare the why-not capability in `--describe`, input PanGloss rejects (an unknown morph id, a guid that is not the morph's), a report Motif cannot use, and a run that did not finish. It uses the same machine parser queue, time limits and cancellation as the other parse questions.

## Related commands

- [Explain a word's parse](cmd:parse) shows where each candidate path of the word stopped, without naming a morph sequence you expected.
- [Trace a word](cmd:trace) returns the full diagnostic tree for one word.

entries.title: Withdraw a Proposal
entries.description: Takes back an open Proposal and keeps its history. A person can reopen it later as a Draft.
entries.helpPage:
# Withdraw a Proposal

`motif withdraw --proposal <id>` takes back an open Proposal and marks it withdrawn. The Proposal and its Trials stay in the project's closed list; the changes are not applied.

## When to use it

Use it when an author no longer wants an open Proposal to go forward. Motif finalizes a Draft before withdrawing it, so its content remains available if someone reopens it. This command does not withdraw your own pending changes; take those out in **Proposals**, under **Your Changes Not Applied Yet**, instead.

Assistants need Advanced AI mode to use the MCP tool. Turn it on in **AI Assistants** or run `motif settings advanced-ai on`. In a sandbox, set `MOTIF_ADVANCED_AI_MODE_PATH` to a writable preference file.

## Example

```text
motif withdraw --proposal <id> --project <project> --json
```

## What it prints

The Proposal's id and new status, `withdrawn`. A person can reopen a withdrawn Proposal as a Draft under the same id, with its history kept.

## Related commands

- [List Proposals](cmd:proposals) shows withdrawn Proposals with `--include-set-aside`.
- [Reopen a Proposal](cmd:reopen%20--proposal) opens a withdrawn Proposal as a Draft.
- [Delete a closed Proposal](cmd:delete%20--proposal) removes a withdrawn Proposal that never applied.

entries.title: Read one word's context
entries.description: Reads a word's captured FieldWorks presence and every stored analysis with its individual Opinion. Uses the current Baseline without requiring a Selection or an Assessment, and reports whether FieldWorks has saved since.
entries.helpPage:
# Read one word's context

`word-context` reads one word's captured FieldWorks presence and all of its stored analyses, including Approved, Disapproved and Unknown opinions. It uses the same query as the word panel and does not require an Assessment or membership in a Selection.

## Example

```text
motif word-context --project Koro.fwdata --word dogs --json
```

## What it prints

The response includes the exact Baseline identity, its source-save and publication times, word membership, each stored analysis with its identity and individual opinion, and an exact Word Analyses link when available. `isStale` says whether the saved FieldWorks project is newer than the Baseline's source save. A later save does not replace the captured analyses.

Before a Baseline exists, membership is unknown and no analysis context is supplied; this does not mean the word is absent. A missing Baseline file is refused. When several wordforms have the same form, their stored analyses retain their own identities and no unique navigation target is invented.

## Related commands

- [Capture a Baseline](cmd:baseline%20capture) records the saved project state.
- [Inspect approved analyses](cmd:analyses) reads the approved-analysis aggregate.
- [Trace a word](cmd:trace) records the parser's search.

entries.title: Give word types a disposition
entries.description: Records that word types are names, loans, other-language words, abbreviations, numerals, non-words or misspellings, with the evidence, so Coverage can count them as accounted for. It writes Motif's store only, never the FieldWorks project.
entries.helpPage:
# Give word types a disposition

`wordform dispose` records that a corpus word type is not a word to analyse: a name, a loan, a word of another language, an abbreviation, a numeral, a non-word, or a misspelling of another word. Each disposition carries the evidence for it, so Coverage can count the type as accounted for instead of leaving it open. It writes Motif's own store beside the project and never the FieldWorks project, so it needs no Proposal and no Apply.

## Example

```text
motif wordform dispose Nairobi Mombasa Kisumu --project <fwdata> --as name --evidence "place names in the Gazetteer"
motif wordform dispose recieve --project <fwdata> --as misspelling --intended receive --evidence "typo for receive in the 1998 print"
motif wordform dispose Kenya --project <fwdata> --as loan --evidence "English toponym" --replace
```

`--as` is one of `name`, `loan`, `other-language`, `abbreviation`, `numeral`, `non-word` or `misspelling` (`artifact` is accepted for `non-word`). `--evidence` is required. A `misspelling` also needs `--intended <form>`, and no other category accepts it. The intended form may be several words, for a run-together misspelling such as `newyork` for "New York"; a form with `;` is refused, so pick one candidate.

- A disposition belongs to a word type, not to one occurrence: it holds for every use of the word in the corpus. Spellings that differ only in Unicode composition are one type. Case is not folded, so give the form as the corpus word list spells it.
- A type that already stands with the same category and intended form is left alone and reported as `already-recorded`.
- A type that stands with a different category or intended form is refused with `disposition.contradiction`, and nothing in the call is written. Add `--replace` to end the standing disposition and record the new one, or [clear it](cmd:wordform%20undispose) first. Either way the earlier disposition stays in the type's history.
- A call writes every form or none. `--by <name>` records who made the call; it defaults to the signed-in user.
- Only the command line writes dispositions. Assistants can read them with [disposition show](cmd:disposition%20show) and [disposition list](cmd:disposition%20list).

## Related commands

- [Clear word type dispositions](cmd:wordform%20undispose) removes one.
- [Show a word type's disposition](cmd:disposition%20show) shows what stands and what stood before.
- [List word type dispositions](cmd:disposition%20list) pages through everything recorded.

entries.title: Dispose word types from a file
entries.description: Reads word types and their dispositions from a TSV, a JSONL file or a grammar lane ledger and records them in one transaction. Rows that cannot be recorded are refused with their line numbers and nothing is written unless --skip-refused is given; --dry-run reports what would change.
entries.helpPage:
# Dispose word types from a file

`wordform dispose --from-file <path>` records the dispositions listed in a file, in one transaction, so a lane can account for thousands of names, loans and misspellings in one call. It does what [wordform dispose](cmd:wordform%20dispose) does for each row: the same categories, the same evidence rule, the same contradiction refusal and `--replace`. It writes Motif's own store, never the FieldWorks project.

## Example

```text
motif wordform dispose --from-file dispositions.tsv --project <fwdata> --dry-run
motif wordform dispose --from-file dispositions.tsv --project <fwdata> --by swh-lane
motif wordform dispose --from-file ledger.tsv --project <fwdata> --format ledger --skip-refused
```

## Files

The format is detected from the first line, or set with `--format tsv|jsonl|ledger`.

- **TSV**: a header row naming `form`, `category` and `evidence`, and optionally `intended`, in any order. Without a header the columns are form, category, intended, evidence.
- **JSONL**: one object per line with the string fields `form`, `category`, `evidence` and `intended`.
- **Ledger**: a grammar lane ledger with its eight columns. Only rows whose state is `Disposition` are read, and the others are counted and left out. The `class` column is the category. A misspelling's `intended=<form> | <evidence>` prefix is split at the first " | ", as Coverage splits it; an intended form may be several words, for a run-together misspelling, but one with `;` (several candidates) is refused on its row: pick one. Rows are read less strictly than Coverage reads a ledger (blank lines skipped, tokens and revision not checked). Evidence longer than the limit is cut and counted. A class that is not a category, such as `mixed`, is refused on its row.

## One transaction, with refusals

Every row is checked before anything is written. A row with a bad category, no evidence, a missing intended form, an empty form, or a word type that already stands with another disposition is refused with its line number. If any row is refused, nothing is written. Add `--skip-refused` to write the rows that are accepted and report the rest, or `--replace` to end a standing disposition that a row contradicts. A word type that appears twice with the same disposition counts once; with different dispositions, the later row is refused.

A word type that already stands as the row asks is left alone, and evidence it does not yet hold is appended to its evidence, so running the same file again changes nothing.

## Dry run and output

`--dry-run` reports the counts a real run would give and writes nothing. The text output gives the counts of added, replaced, unchanged and refused rows and the first refusals. `--json` gives the response as one object. `--format json` prints one JSON object per row, then a last object with the counts. The exit code is non-zero when rows were refused and nothing was written.

## Related commands

- [Give word types a disposition](cmd:wordform%20dispose) records a few forms given on the command line.
- [Clear word type dispositions](cmd:wordform%20undispose) removes one.
- [List word type dispositions](cmd:disposition%20list) pages through everything recorded.

entries.title: Clear word type dispositions
entries.description: Removes the standing disposition of each word type. The removed disposition stays in the type's history, and a type that had none is reported and left alone.
entries.helpPage:
# Clear word type dispositions

`wordform undispose` removes the standing disposition of each word type you name, so the type is analysed like any other word again. The removed disposition is not deleted: it stays in the type's history with who cleared it, when, and the reason.

## Example

```text
motif wordform undispose Nairobi Mombasa --project <fwdata> --reason "attested as a common noun in the Gazetteer"
```

A type that has no disposition is reported as `not-recorded` and left alone, so repeating the command is safe. `--by <name>` records who cleared it and defaults to the signed-in user. See the earlier dispositions of a type with [disposition show](cmd:disposition%20show).

## Related commands

- [Give word types a disposition](cmd:wordform%20dispose) records one.

entries.title: Stop the background runner
entries.description: Ends the background runner that holds a project's store open, or the one for the current worker root, so a store upgrade or a stuck queue can proceed. Jobs it was running are taken back by the next runner.
entries.helpPage:
# Stop the background runner

`worker stop` ends the background runner process that is holding a project store open or that serves the current worker root.

## When to use it

A command that needs the store to itself, such as `store upgrade`, refuses with "The project store is in use" while a runner still has the store open. The refusal names the runner (`holderPid`, `holderBuild`, `holderRoot`) when one is recorded. A queued job that nothing claims for a minute names the job in front of it and the runner's pid for the same reason. Run this command to end that runner. The next command that queues work starts a new one.

## Examples

```powershell
motif worker stop --project "C:\FieldWorks\Projects\Koro\Koro.fwdata"
motif worker stop
```

With `--project`, it stops every runner that records itself as holding that project's store, whichever worker root it serves. Without it, it stops the runner the current worker root (`MOTIF_WORKER_ROOT`, or the per-user default) records.

## What it prints

One line for each runner it ended, with its pid, build and worker root, for example `Stopped the runner (pid 4121, build 0.31.0 [3f2a], worker root /home/ann/.local/share/SIL/Motif).` It ends a process only when its name and start time match the record. A pid that now belongs to another program, or whose start time differs, is left alone and reported with the reason and the operating system command (`kill <pid>`, `taskkill /PID <pid> /F`) to end it by hand if it is the runner. A live process whose record carries no start time, or whose start time cannot be read, makes the command refuse with `worker.stop-failed` and the same hint; its record is kept. When no runner is running it says so and still succeeds. `--json` returns the same facts as `workers`.

The runner is ended at once. A job it was running stays Running until the next runner takes it back, so wait for that rather than cancelling it. If the runner is still alive ten seconds later the command refuses with `worker.stop-failed` and names the pid.

## Related commands

- [List queued jobs](cmd:jobs%20list) shows the queue a stalled runner is working through.
- [Upgrade the project store](cmd:store%20upgrade) is the command that most often needs the runner stopped.

entries.title: Show writing systems
entries.description: Reads fonts, features, direction and style sizes from the current Baseline, in FieldWorks writing-system order. Change these settings in FieldWorks, then capture a new Baseline to read them here.
entries.helpPage:
# Show writing systems

`motif writing-systems --project <fwdata> [--json]` reads the current [Baseline](term:baseline)'s writing systems without opening the FieldWorks project. Before the first capture, it reports that no Baseline exists.

Each current vernacular and analysis list keeps FieldWorks' order and default. The response includes the id, name, abbreviation, requested default font family, verbatim feature string, direction, and each style's effective font, features and point size. A writing system in both lists appears once per membership; positions in JSON count from zero.

The command includes every project style; a missing style uses that writing system's effective Normal settings. Normal without a size uses FieldWorks' 10-point default. Sizes contain no window units or zoom.

For which FieldWorks style each part of the window uses and where to change its writing-system settings, see [Writing systems in the window](guide:writing-systems).

The font name is the project's request. The command reports saved settings and does not inspect installed fonts.

entries.title: A recorded measurement
entries.description: An Assessment is one immutable measurement of one kind, made by an Assessor. A PanGloss run may produce several Assessments, such as parse timing and correctness for a Selection.

entries.title: A saved project starting point
entries.description: A Baseline is a saved, minimal, file-backed copy of a project from which Motif can make independent Dry Run copies. When captured from a project FieldWorks holds open, it reflects FieldWorks' last save.

entries.title: Where a change came from
entries.description: A citation records the work a change was taken from, such as a grammar section or a dictionary entry, with an optional page or section. It is shown beside the change and never changes what the Proposal does.

entries.title: Words measured by default
entries.description: A project's Default Selection is the chosen Texts plus any added words Motif measures when no other Selection is named. Motif resolves it to an exact word list for each run.

entries.title: Evidence no longer matches

entries.title: Effects measured on a copy

entries.title: Motif's project workflow records
entries.description: The Motif store keeps project workflow records and frozen Report bindings in the project's paired database. Parsimony judgments remain durable FieldWorks project data, while analysis artifacts are disposable files.
entries.helpPage:
# Motif store

The Motif store keeps a project's Proposals, jobs, Assessments, Reports, Receipts, and other workflow records. Parsimony judgments belong with the FieldWorks project; the files used to analyse a grammar can be rebuilt.

entries.title: The latest stored evidence
entries.description: The Overview presents project counts and measurements already recorded by Motif. Reading it does not start a Refresh or a parse.

entries.title: Parse every chosen word
entries.description: Parse all words asks PanGloss to parse the words you chose and saves the result against the Baseline. A search stopped at a limit is saved as not finished, never as a word that cannot parse.

entries.title: Fewer repeated grammar statements
entries.description: Parsimony is the axis that favors fewer or less-duplicated grammar statements while preserving known valid readings. It is distinct from restrictiveness, which asks how narrowly a statement licenses forms.
entries.helpPage:
# Parsimony

Parsimony favors fewer or less-duplicated grammar statements while preserving known valid readings. It is one of the two axes in a [Parsimony review](term:parsimony-review), alongside [restrictiveness](term:restrictiveness).

entries.title: A specific grammar recommendation
entries.description: A Parsimony recommendation names one grammar object or group, its evidence, and a recipe or limitation. Its stable finding identity is separate from the digest of evidence supporting it.
entries.helpPage:
# Parsimony recommendation

A Parsimony recommendation identifies one grammar object or group worth examining, shows the evidence for it, and gives a recipe or explains what information is missing. Its evidence remains attached to the exact item it concerns.

entries.title: Advice about grammar statements
entries.description: A Parsimony review offers specific grammar recommendations along the parsimony and restrictiveness axes. It records evidence and limitations, and never decides whether to Apply a change.
entries.helpPage:
# Parsimony review

A Parsimony review gives specific, advisory recommendations about a grammar's parsimony and restrictiveness. Each finding shows whether it comes from grammar structure, Text evidence, or a parser Assessment, and states what that evidence cannot establish.

entries.title: Phonology Example Set
entries.description: A Phonology Example Set is a saved list of underlying forms with the surface forms an author expects, kept as advisory evidence that never changes Readiness or Apply. Its subcommands are phonology-examples save, list, show, check and results.
entries.helpPage:
# Phonology Example Set

A Phonology Example Set is a list you write down of what a form should become: an underlying form such as `n+baya`, the surface form you expect, such as `mbaya`, and the lexical entry that supplies the context. Each example can carry a citation to its source. Motif keeps each saved version unchanged, so a later edit is a new revision and the earlier one can still be read.

A set is advisory evidence. A [Phonology Check](cmd:phonology-examples%20results) can measure the current grammar against it and report, for every example, whether the expected surface form was produced (agree), the search finished without it (disagree), or the question could not be answered (unavailable). None of that changes Readiness, and Apply ignores it.

## Commands

- `phonology-examples save` records a new revision of a set. Assistants need Advanced AI mode to use it as an MCP tool.
- [List phonology examples](cmd:phonology-examples%20list) shows the current revision of each saved set.
- [Show phonology examples](cmd:phonology-examples%20show) reads the examples of one saved revision, a page at a time.
- `phonology-examples check` queues a check of a saved revision against the current Baseline. It is an advanced AI command and needs a captured Baseline.
- [Read phonology check results](cmd:phonology-examples%20results) reads a finished check as summary pages or one complete example.

entries.title: The final fit check
entries.description: The CLI's preflight command checks changes against the live model before Apply. A change whose required inputs changed or disappeared no longer fits.

entries.title: A reviewable set of changes
entries.description: A Proposal groups related Motif operations so a person can inspect, measure, and apply them as one unit.

entries.title: A finding from frozen evidence
entries.description: A Report presents statistics and findings from stored evidence. A Parsimony Report may use a frozen evidence bundle without an Assessment and is always advisory; other Report kinds retain their configured regression behavior.
entries.helpPage:
# Report

A Report presents findings from stored evidence. A Parsimony Report can describe frozen grammar and Text evidence without an Assessment, and its advice never decides whether a person may Apply a change.

entries.title: The narrowest statement that still fits
entries.description: Restrictiveness favors the narrowest grammar statement that covers known valid forms and excludes explicitly forbidden readings. An unattested form is not a negative without suitable evidence.
entries.helpPage:
# Restrictiveness

Restrictiveness favors the narrowest grammar statement that still covers known valid forms and excludes readings people have explicitly forbidden. A form missing from the chosen Texts is unobserved; that absence alone does not make it bad.

entries.title: A human-confirmed forbidden form or reading
entries.description: A reviewed negative is a human-confirmed form or reading the grammar must not accept. A FieldWorks Disapproved analysis is negative for that reading only, not for the whole word.
entries.helpPage:
# Reviewed negative

A reviewed negative is a form or reading that a person has explicitly confirmed the grammar must not accept. A FieldWorks Disapproved analysis rejects that reading only; it does not reject every analysis of the word.

entries.title: A durable choice about a recommendation
entries.description: A Ruling records fix, keep, ask, or defer for one Parsimony recommendation and its relevant evidence. It belongs to durable FieldWorks project data; its storage shape is defined separately.
entries.helpPage:
# Ruling

A Ruling records what a person wants to do with one [Parsimony recommendation](term:parsimony-recommendation): fix it, keep it (with an optional reason), ask a question, or defer it. An applied keep or defer moves the recommendation to the Suppressed set, where you can list it again with its reason and history. It stays tied to the exact evidence considered; relevant new evidence returns it to Active with the previous decision and reason. Fix and ask remain Active. A pending choice stays Active until Apply.

entries.title: Share of your text that parses
entries.description: Text Coverage is the share of the Default Selection's words, and of their occurrences in the chosen Texts, that parse. The same share measured over a Corpus is called grammar coverage.

entries.title: A Proposal tried on a copy
entries.description: A Trial applies a Proposal to a throwaway copy of the project and parses words again, so its numbers can sit beside today's. A Trial is out of date once the project or the Proposal changes; the window then says it needs another try.
entries.helpPage:
# Trial

A Trial applies a [Proposal](term:proposal) to a throwaway copy of the project and parses words again, so its numbers can be read beside today's. It never changes the real project.

A Trial goes out of date when the project is refreshed or the Proposal changes. The window then says the Proposal needs another try; nothing re-runs until you ask.

entries.title: A tested window guide
entries.description: A Walkthrough is a script that tests the real Motif window using fixed data and produces screenshots at marked steps. It can also render a short, silent clip.

entries.title: Reading a Handoff
entries.description: Start with handoff.md for the included files and reading examples; use the separate pastedHeader text for the prepared chat prompt.
entries.helpPage:
# Reading a Handoff

Start with `handoff.md` for the included files and reading examples; use the separate `pastedHeader` text for the prepared chat prompt.

An assessed Handoff lists files alphabetically: `grammar.json`, `handoff.md`, `parse-results.json`, `read_results.py`, then `texts.json`. A Baseline-only Handoff omits `parse-results.json`. The App's one-word Handoff contains `grammar.json`, `handoff.md`, `read_results.py`, `texts.json`, then `traces/<word>.trace.json`; it carries the raw diagnostic and omits batch parse results.

| File | Description |
|---|---|
| `grammar.json` | The grammar Motif exports for PanGloss to parse. |
| `handoff.md` | Explains the included material and gives reading examples. |
| `parse-results.json` | One result for each selected word, including its parser outcome and timing. |
| `read_results.py` | Queries the Handoff's JSON files from a terminal. |
| `texts.json` | The selected Texts with the analyses the project stores. |
| `traces/<word>.trace.json` | The raw diagnostic for the selected word, including parser fields Motif does not interpret. |

Read the files as linguistic project data; they may contain real grammar rules, lexicon entries, and text.

Use the helper’s own help to see its commands, then ask focused questions against the supplied files:

```powershell
python read_results.py --help
python read_results.py word --help
```

For an assessed folder, the current CLI exports a retained Assessment invocation rather than silently running a fresh one. To create one, first run [assess](cmd:assess) with `--json`, read `invocationId` from its response, then pass that value to [handoff](cmd:handoff):

```powershell
motif handoff "C:\Projects\Sena.fwdata" --out "C:\handoffs\Sena" --invocation <invocationId> --json
```

The successful JSON response reports `outputDirectory`, `baseline`, `selection`, `files`, `assessmentIds`, optional `invocationId`, `pastedHeader`, and `handoffMarkdown`. Use `--no-assess` for a folder without `parse-results.json`; `--texts <guid,guid>` is accepted only with that option, to select texts.

Treat every file as potentially sensitive and share it only with a service approved for that project.

entries.title: Measuring a grammar
entries.description: These commands answer different questions. grammar check asks PanGloss to inspect the whole grammar and stores findings for the current Baseline. It does not parse selected words. assess parses a Selection and records one or more Assessments. overview reads stored summaries; stats queries statistics from a stored run.
entries.helpPage:
# Measuring a grammar

These commands answer different questions. `grammar check` asks PanGloss to inspect the whole grammar and stores findings for the current [Baseline](term:baseline). It does not parse selected words. `assess` parses a Selection and records one or more [Assessments](term:assessment). `overview` reads stored summaries; `stats` queries statistics from a stored run.

Capture a Baseline explicitly with [baseline capture](cmd:baseline%20capture) when you want to name that step:

```powershell
motif baseline capture --project "C:\Projects\Sena.fwdata" --json
```

Then use [assess](cmd:assess) to measure the saved Default Selection, or name a source such as all wordforms. Read stored summaries with [overview](cmd:overview) and query statistics by replaying the retained parser evidence and cache for a stored Assessment with [stats](cmd:stats):

```powershell
motif assess "C:\Projects\Sena.fwdata" --all-wordforms --json
motif overview --project "C:\Projects\Sena.fwdata" --json
motif stats "C:\Projects\Sena.fwdata" --json
```

`assess` is synchronous in the current CLI. If you give no Selection flags, it uses the saved Default Selection. Other supported sources include `--texts <guid,guid>`, `--words <file>`, and retry options such as `--retry-failed --retry-source-assessment <id>`. The command ensures a Baseline exists if needed.

The successful `assess --json` response includes the invocation identifier and the Assessment records produced. For example, its relevant fields have this shape:

```json
{
  "invocationId": "<invocation-id>",
  "assessmentIds": ["<assessment-id>"],
  "measurements": [
    {
      "assessmentId": "<assessment-id>",
      "kind": "ObjectTiming",
      "invocationId": "<invocation-id>"
    }
  ]
}
```

Use `invocationId` when you need to create a [Handoff](cmd:handoff) for this exact retained run. The number and kinds of `measurements` can vary with the Assessor’s supported kinds; do not assume a fixed Assessment count.

Use [grammar check](cmd:grammar%20check) to check the whole grammar. [warnings](cmd:warnings) reads findings that have already been stored:

```powershell
motif grammar check --project "C:\Projects\Sena.fwdata" --json
motif warnings --project "C:\Projects\Sena.fwdata" --json
```

`warnings` reads findings already stored for that Baseline; it does not rerun the check. Without a Baseline, `grammar check` refuses and tells you to run `motif baseline capture --project <fwdata>`. Use **Working with jobs** for commands that enqueue background work.

entries.title: Output and exit codes
entries.description: Use the process exit code as the success signal. Successful text output goes to stdout; handled failures go to stderr. With --json, successful responses are usually the command’s JSON object itself, using camelCase fields, not a common success wrapper. Some enqueue-only commands return a bare job ID even with --json.
entries.helpPage:
# Output and exit codes

Use the process exit code as the success signal. Successful text output goes to stdout; handled failures go to stderr. With `--json`, successful responses are usually the command’s JSON object itself, using camelCase fields, not a common success wrapper. Some enqueue-only commands return a bare job ID even with `--json`.

Handled failures requested with `--json` write a failure object to stderr and nothing to stdout. Its shape is:

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "reason": "Busy",
  "message": "<human-readable reason>",
  "detail": { "project": "<project path>" }
}
```

`code` and `detail` are optional. The `reason` is a stable failure class; `message` is for a person. Exit codes are `1` for an invalid invocation, `2` for a refusal, missing item, or cancellation, `3` when the request cannot be attempted now (such as a busy project), `4` for an inconsistent store or unexpected failure, and `5` when an Assessment stops at its whole-run time limit. Retry a `3` later; do not retry a refusal unchanged.

The `help` command has its own plain stderr errors and exits `2` for invalid help syntax or an unknown entry; it does not use the failure object. An unexpected exception escaping the top-level command handler exits `4`; with `--json` it writes the failure object with code `cli.unexpected`, and without it a plain `error: ...` line. A command stopped by Ctrl+C exits `2` with code `cli.cancelled`, as a failure object with `--json` or a plain `cli.cancelled: ...` line without it. Treat any nonzero exit as failure and keep stdout and stderr separate.

With `--json`, stdout is exactly one JSON document, or empty when the command refused; progress, warnings and `error:` lines go to stderr. A script that merges the streams with `2>&1` must not parse the merge. `--pick <path,...>` keeps only the named fields of that document, so no script is needed: `motif proposal trial --project P ID --json --pick gate.state,summary.wordforms` prints `{"gate.state": ..., "summary.wordforms": ...}`. A path is names joined by dots; `items[].name` takes `name` from every element of an array and `items[2]` takes one element. An element that lacks the field gives `null`. A path that matches nothing is refused with `cli.pick-path`, which lists the names that exist; so is `--pick` without `--json`. A verb that streams its output to stdout, such as `evidence export` without `--out`, has no single document to pick from.

entries.title: Using Motif from an agent
entries.description: Call Motif as motif <verb> .... Each process handles one command; durable project state is stored between calls, so commands do not depend on a setup command in the same process. Use an explicit project path with commands that accept --project or take the .fwdata path as a positional argument.
entries.helpPage:
# Using Motif from an agent

Call Motif as `motif <verb> ...`. Each process handles one command; durable project state is stored between calls, so commands do not depend on a setup command in the same process. Use an explicit project path with commands that accept `--project` or take the `.fwdata` path as a positional argument.

Prefer `--json` when the command’s usage line supports it, and read the response from stdout. Do not parse the human text rendering. For example:

```powershell
motif overview --project "C:\Projects\Sena.fwdata" --json
motif assess "C:\Projects\Sena.fwdata" --all-wordforms --json
motif jobs list --json
```

To list help entries in one call, run `motif help --all --json`. The JSON has a `locale`, a `siteRoot`, and `entries` for available CLI commands, glossary terms and Guide pages. Each entry has a kind, code, slug, title, description, a `helpPage` field containing the full Help page Markdown when a page exists, and a URL; command entries also include usage lines and a surface. For one entry, `motif help <code>` prints its title, description, URL, and (for a command) usage. Add `--full` to print the expanded page, or `--json` to get that entry's metadata, including its full Help page when available. The documentation website also publishes `llms.txt`, a plain-text index of every page. With no arguments, `motif` prints the usage catalog to stderr and exits with code 1.

Assistants need Advanced AI mode to use MCP tools. In the window, open **AI Assistants**, select **Let Assistants Use Motif's Tools**, then choose which assistants to connect. The **AI Assistants** Guide page explains the client steps. A person can also enable it with `motif settings advanced-ai on`. The MCP server starts with `motif mcp`; each project tool takes a Known project name or recorded path in its `project` argument. Use the workflow resource to draft, Dry Run, Trial, revise and Finalize for a person to review and Apply. Most commands run synchronously, but `baseline-refresh`, `dry-run`, and `trial` enqueue jobs. See **Working with jobs**. For errors and retry decisions, see **Output and exit codes**.

Before composing rules, read the encoding guide for the phenomenon: `motif help` lists the guides, and `motif help guide:encoding/workflow --full` shows the working order. Over MCP the same text is the `motif_guide` tool.

A completed Trial has a saved report. Read its summary and limitations, then use failures or full detail to page through the cases needed for review. In MCP, `motif_trial` reads and refreshes reports explicitly, and `motif_difference` reads a particular report or its cases; a trace is an explicit diagnostic. No red flags means only not bad, never good.

entries.title: Working with jobs
entries.description: The Motif job runner handles durable work that outlives the command that queued it. baseline-refresh, dry-run and trial enqueue jobs. A synchronous assess command is not a job.
entries.helpPage:
# Working with jobs

The Motif job runner handles durable work that outlives the command that queued it. [baseline-refresh](cmd:baseline-refresh), `dry-run` and `trial` enqueue jobs. A synchronous [assess](cmd:assess) command is not a job.

```powershell
motif jobs list --json
motif jobs show <jobId> --project "C:\Projects\Sena.fwdata" --json
motif jobs assessments <jobId> --project "C:\Projects\Sena.fwdata" --json
motif jobs cancel <jobId> --project "C:\Projects\Sena.fwdata" --json
motif jobs requeue <jobId> --project "C:\Projects\Sena.fwdata" --json
motif jobs move <jobId> --project "C:\Projects\Sena.fwdata" --to-top --json
```

[`jobs list`](cmd:jobs%20list) spans every Known project and reports active work in queue order; it is the jobs command that does not take `--project`. [`jobs show`](cmd:jobs%20show) returns the job’s status, attempt, update time, cancellation request, failure category, version, and queue position when available. Status values are lower-case hyphenated strings such as `waiting-for-project-host`. A status response has fields like:

```json
{
  "jobId": "<job-id>",
  "projectKey": "<project-key>",
  "found": true,
  "kind": "trial",
  "status": "waiting-for-project-host",
  "attempt": 1,
  "updatedUtc": "<UTC timestamp>",
  "cancellationRequested": false,
  "failureCategory": null,
  "version": 1,
  "queueOrder": 1
}
```

A job whose claiming runner stopped adds `"claimLost": true` and a `warnings` array to the status response; each warning has a `code` and a `message`, and the code for this case is `job.claim-lost`. If the job was parked waiting for something that now exists, `status` is `queued`, the status the next runner gives it. A job parked on purpose, such as `waiting-for-project-host`, has released its claim, so it shows that status with no warning. `claimLost` and `warnings` are left out otherwise. The CLI starts a runner when `jobs show` or `--wait` sees a queued or claim-lost job; the MCP `motif_job` tool only reports, so run any command that queues work, or start `SIL.Motif.Worker`, to restart a runner.

The queue-list response is `{ "jobs": [...] }`. Each entry includes `jobId`, `projectKey`, `projectPath`, `kind`, `status`, `attempt`, `updatedUtc`, and `queueOrder`. `jobs assessments` returns `jobId` and an `assessments` array whose entries contain `assessmentId`, `assessor`, `kind`, and `savedUtc`.

[`jobs cancel`](cmd:jobs%20cancel) on a queued or parked job moves it to cancelled. Cancelling a running job requests cancellation; the runner completes it. [`jobs requeue`](cmd:jobs%20requeue) is for a terminal job and creates a fresh attempt with a new job ID. Use [`jobs assessments`](cmd:jobs%20assessments) to read the Assessment IDs produced by a completed job.

Without `--wait`, enqueueing `dry-run` or `trial` returns a bare job ID, including under `--json`. With `--wait`, the CLI waits up to two minutes by default; `--wait-timeout-ms <ms>` changes the bound. See **Output and exit codes** for the failure shape and exit mapping.

entries.title: Connect an assistant
entries.description: Claude is not in Motif's window. The window has no Ask Claude, no Assistant Connections and no API key. You work with Claude only through the MCP in Claude Desktop, where Claude can use Motif's project tools. The assistant still cannot Apply a Proposal; a person reviews and Applies it in Motif.
entries.helpPage:
# Connect an assistant

Claude is not in Motif's window. The window has no Ask Claude, no Assistant Connections and no API key. You work with Claude only through the MCP in Claude Desktop, where Claude can use Motif's project tools. The assistant still cannot Apply a Proposal; a person reviews and Applies it in Motif.

For Claude Desktop, add `motif mcp` to Claude's MCP configuration, upload the Motif plugin ZIP (`motif-plugin.zip`) in **Customize → Plugins**, and restart Claude Desktop. Upload the latest ZIP again after a Motif update to refresh the skills saved to your Claude account.

Changing the setup affects new Claude sessions. Restart Claude Desktop to apply it to a session that is already open.

Name a word, warning, Proposal or Grammar Guide section to Claude and it records a Request. Configuring Claude does not prove a live Claude connection. ChatGPT connection status belongs to its own tunnel only. See [Working with Claude](guide:ask-claude).

entries.title: AI Handoff
entries.description: AI Handoff writes a folder you can share with a chat model. It includes project context for the words you parsed and a starter question. Settings shows what it plans to write and a data-sensitivity notice before you start; the folder can include real grammar rules, lexicon entries, and sentences from the selected Texts.
entries.helpPage:
# AI Handoff

**AI Handoff** writes a folder you can share with a chat model. It includes project context for the words you parsed and a starter question. Settings shows what it plans to write and a data-sensitivity notice before you start; the folder can include real grammar rules, lexicon entries, and sentences from the selected Texts.

Only one parse can run for a project at a time. A Handoff that needs a fresh parse runs it before writing. Motif refuses another parse request for the project until the Handoff finishes.

A Handoff requested for a traced word keeps the displayed trace and the Baseline captured with it. Motif does not parse the word again or make a replacement trace; this Handoff includes the raw diagnostic and leaves out measured results from a separate parse.

1. Open **Settings** at the bottom of the navigation rail. Turn on **Show Hand Off by Copying Files** and scroll to the Handoff controls. Read the notice. If it says the files will include only words chosen on the Texts page, choose **Hand off every parsed word instead** to use every word from the last parse.
2. Choose **Write the AI Handoff**. If you have already written one, the button says **Write the AI Handoff again**.
3. Choose an output folder when prompted and wait for Motif to finish writing.
4. Review the files, then drag the files into your chat or use the copy actions for the prompt and paths.

The utility shows when the files were last written and marks them out of date when a newer parse finishes. Times use your local clock; a timestamp from another day includes its weekday and date. The `read_results.py` reader works over `parse-results.json` and `texts.json`. Write the Handoff again when you want the chat model to receive newer results. Only share the files if you are comfortable sending their linguistic data to that service.

![AI Handoff files ready to share](shot:handoff-cancel-retry/completed-files)

A Handoff from a parse records refused words with a refusal code and reason in `parse-results.json`. Word forms use composed Unicode for reading and searching. `texts.json` is an empty array when no Texts were chosen; added words can still have measured parse results.

entries.title: Apply to FieldWorks
entries.description: In Proposals, open the Proposal you want to apply and read its proposed changes, Rationale and evidence. Complete Before you apply, then choose Apply…. Motif activates that Proposal, reads its current review and checks whether Apply is available.
