- **[black-2018]** — H. Andrew Black. 2018. “Introduction to Parsing.” SIL FieldWorks technical document, 12 April 2018. [Source](https://software.sil.org/fieldworks/help/technical-documents/). Describes how environments condition allomorphs, without establishing that any duplicate is linguistically redundant.

entries.title: Literal host contexts
entries.description: This check finds an environment side or a phonological rule context made only of literal segments: no natural class, variable, repetition or option. A side is flagged when it spells three or more segments, or two or more segments next to a word anchor, a morpheme boundary or an affix hyphen. / # w o r d  is the shape: it limits an allomorph to one host word, which is a lexical listing written as phonology. Each finding names the environment or rule and every allomorph that uses the environment.
entries.helpPage:
# Literal host contexts

This check finds an environment side or a phonological rule context made only of literal segments: no natural class, variable, repetition or option. A side is flagged when it spells three or more segments, or two or more segments next to a word anchor, a morpheme boundary or an affix hyphen. `/ # w o r d _` is the shape: it limits an allomorph to one host word, which is a lexical listing written as phonology. Each finding names the environment or rule and every allomorph that uses the environment.

## Analyse

Read `statement-usage` for the environment and `allomorph-context` for each allomorph that names it. A rule context has no view; the finding names the rule, its right-hand side and the segments. Boundaries are not counted as segments: a word anchor, a morpheme boundary and a segment spelled without a letter or digit, such as the hyphen of an affix, all count as boundaries. Sides with a class, a variable or a repetition are never flagged, nor are one-segment sides.

## Ruling

An applied keep or defer is tied to this finding's exact evidence. See [Ruling](term:ruling) for how it appears in Active and Suppressed lists and returns after relevant evidence changes.

This finding has no closed Notebook subject mapping yet, so it cannot be recorded with a ruling. Read it as a review prompt.

## Ask the linguist

Ask whether the literal string is a true sound pattern or a way of listing one word. Include the environment or rule, its text and the allomorphs that use it.

## Update

No typed action rewrites a context yet. If the string lists a word, state the word's allomorph on its entry instead and retire the environment, or replace the segments with the natural class that explains the pattern.

## Verify

Re-run the check and confirm the side is gone, then confirm every Approved reading that used the allomorph still parses.

## Grounding

Engineering check: a literal-only context of this length; no linguistic claim.

- **[black-2018]** — H. Andrew Black. 2018. “Introduction to Parsing.” SIL FieldWorks technical document, 12 April 2018. [Source](https://software.sil.org/fieldworks/help/technical-documents/). Sections 3.1.3 and 6.1.2.2 describe environments and rule contexts; they do not call a literal-only context an error.

entries.title: Features with few carriers
entries.description: This check finds exception features that fewer than four entries carry on stem MSAs, yet that an affix MSA requires or a phonological rule uses. An exception feature restricts an affix or rule to the stems that carry it. When only one to three stems carry it, the restriction lists words instead of describing a productive pattern. A feature with no carrier at all, and no affix or rule that uses it, is left to unused-statement reporting.
entries.helpPage:
# Features with few carriers

This check finds exception features that fewer than four entries carry on stem MSAs, yet that an affix MSA requires or a phonological rule uses. An exception feature restricts an affix or rule to the stems that carry it. When only one to three stems carry it, the restriction lists words instead of describing a productive pattern. A feature with no carrier at all, and no affix or rule that uses it, is left to unused-statement reporting.

## Analyse

Read the finding: it names the carrier entries, the affix MSAs that require the feature, and the rules that require or exclude it. Open each requiring MSA with `affix-context`. A rule that uses a feature with exactly one carrier is a rule that applies to a single word. The finding also states how many of PanGloss's 64 feature slots the grammar uses (inflection classes including subclasses, exception features and entry inflection types), so a reader sees the headroom before adding another feature. The count is approximate where PanGloss dedupes differently.

## Ruling

This finding has no closed Notebook subject, so it cannot be recorded with a ruling yet. Note the decision in the review conversation instead.

Classify the result as a listed word, a genuine rare restriction, or a feature still being filled in. A feature with no carrier cannot restrict anything yet.

## Ask the linguist

Ask whether the affix is attested on only these stems and is not productive. Name the feature, its carriers, and every affix or rule that requires it.

## Update

No typed action is available for this finding. If the affix is not productive, the honest model is one lexical entry per attested word, each a complex form of its base, and the feature and its requirers go away. If it is productive, record a `defer` and fill in the carriers.

## Verify

Re-run the check and confirm the feature is gone or carried by four or more entries, and that every Approved reading that used the affix is unchanged.

## Grounding

Black 2018 describes exception features as a way to mark the stems on which an affix is wrong or right when no phonological or categorial property separates them; the listed alternative is a separate entry per word.

- **[black-2018]** — H. Andrew Black. 2018. “Introduction to Parsing.” SIL FieldWorks technical document, 12 April 2018. [Source](https://software.sil.org/fieldworks/help/technical-documents/). Describes exception ("produce restriction") features on stems and affixes; the four-carrier threshold is this check's own.

entries.title: Gloss that echoes the form
entries.description: This check finds senses whose gloss is only the entry's form written in capitals: XYZ on xyz-, or the capitals followed by a dotted suffix (XYZ.V). Hyphens and = are ignored, and any allomorph form of the entry counts. A gloss that adds only a dotted suffix is the mark of a clone entry made to carry a feature. A gloss written in the same case as the form, such as a proper name or a loanword (radar on radar), is not reported, because it can be a real gloss.
entries.helpPage:
# Gloss that echoes the form

This check finds senses whose gloss is only the entry's form written in capitals: `XYZ` on `xyz-`, or the capitals followed by a dotted suffix (`XYZ.V`). Hyphens and `=` are ignored, and any allomorph form of the entry counts. A gloss that adds only a dotted suffix is the mark of a clone entry made to carry a feature. A gloss written in the same case as the form, such as a proper name or a loanword (`radar` on `radar`), is not reported, because it can be a real gloss.

## Analyse

Read the entry in `allomorph-context` and compare its forms with the sense's glosses in every analysis writing system. Process affixes with no form text are not read, because there is no form to echo.

## Ruling

An applied keep or defer is tied to this finding's exact evidence. See [Ruling](term:ruling) for how it appears in Active and Suppressed lists and returns after relevant evidence changes.

No ruling mapping exists for this finding yet, so it cannot be recorded with a Notebook ruling. Note the decision in the review instead.

## Ask the linguist

Ask what the morpheme means or does, so the gloss can say it. Include the entry, its form and the gloss that echoes it. A dotted suffix suggests a clone entry: ask whether it should be merged with its homograph.

## Update

No typed action is available for this finding. Replace the gloss with a meaningful one in FieldWorks, or merge the clone into its homograph.

## Verify

Re-run the check and confirm the sense is no longer listed.

## Grounding

- **[black-2018]** — H. Andrew Black. 2018. “Introduction to Parsing.” SIL FieldWorks technical document, 12 April 2018. [Source](https://software.sil.org/fieldworks/help/technical-documents/). Advises making a gloss as meaningful as possible; it does not rule on any particular gloss, so the finding asks rather than concludes.

entries.title: Entries differing in spelling
entries.description: This check finds entries whose forms differ only in case, Unicode form or a fold rule the project declares ([parsimony] fold, for example iy>y for Cebuano). They are bucketed by a folded form, never compared pairwise.
entries.helpPage:
# Entries differing in spelling

This check finds entries whose forms differ only in case, Unicode form or a fold rule the project declares (`[parsimony] fold`, for example `iy>y` for Cebuano). They are bucketed by a folded form, never compared pairwise.

## Analyse

Read each group of entries that share one folded form and decide whether they are one lexeme.

## Ruling

An applied keep or defer is tied to this finding's exact evidence. See [Ruling](term:ruling) for how it appears in Active and Suppressed lists and returns after relevant evidence changes.

No ruling mapping exists for this finding yet, so it cannot be recorded with a Notebook ruling. Note the decision in the review instead.

## Ask the linguist

Ask whether the entries are one word or two.

## Update

No typed action is available for this finding yet. Merge or variant-link the entries in FieldWorks.

## Verify

Re-run the check and confirm the finding is gone, then confirm that no Approved reading changed.

## Grounding

- **[black-2018]** — H. Andrew Black. 2018. “Introduction to Parsing.” SIL FieldWorks technical document, 12 April 2018. [Source](https://software.sil.org/fieldworks/help/technical-documents/). Describes how an affix attaches to a stem by category; it does not say that a stem without one is wrong, so the finding asks rather than concludes.

entries.title: Stem with no part of speech
entries.description: This check finds stem MSAs that name no part of speech. A stem with no category takes no affix that is restricted to a category, so a linguist meets it as an unexplained gap. Each finding names the entry and says whether its senses have glosses: an entry with no glosses is usually a stub, and one with glosses is usually missing its category.
entries.helpPage:
# Stem with no part of speech

This check finds stem MSAs that name no part of speech. A stem with no category takes no affix that is restricted to a category, so a linguist meets it as an unexplained gap. Each finding names the entry and says whether its senses have glosses: an entry with no glosses is usually a stub, and one with glosses is usually missing its category.

## Analyse

Read the MSA in `affix-context` to confirm that it has no category. Then read the entry's senses: if none has a gloss, the entry is a stub left from an import or a first pass; if some do, the entry was analysed but never given a part of speech. Count only stem MSAs; inflectional and derivational MSAs name their categories in other roles and are not read here.

## Ruling

An applied keep or defer is tied to this finding's exact evidence. See [Ruling](term:ruling) for how it appears in Active and Suppressed lists and returns after relevant evidence changes.

No ruling mapping exists for this finding yet, so it cannot be recorded with a Notebook ruling. Note the decision in the review instead.

## Ask the linguist

Ask whether the entry is a stub to delete or a stem whose part of speech was never chosen. Include the entry, its glosses if any, and its MSA identity.

## Update

No typed action is available for this finding. Set the part of speech on the stem MSA in FieldWorks, or delete the stub entry.

## Verify

Re-run the check and confirm the MSA is no longer listed, then confirm that no Approved reading changed.

## Grounding

- **[black-2018]** — H. Andrew Black. 2018. “Introduction to Parsing.” SIL FieldWorks technical document, 12 April 2018. [Source](https://software.sil.org/fieldworks/help/technical-documents/). Describes how an affix attaches to a stem by category; it does not say that a stem without one is wrong, so the finding asks rather than concludes.

entries.title: Unused grammar statements
entries.description: This check finds environments and natural classes that the parser never applies. A statement is used when some grammar object applies it: an affix process, a rule context, an infix position, or an allomorph environment. A statement that no reference the parser applies is reported as unused, and its finding names the referrers that do not apply it.
entries.helpPage:
# Unused grammar statements

This check finds environments and natural classes that the parser never applies. A statement is used when some grammar object applies it: an affix process, a rule context, an infix position, or an allomorph environment. A statement that no reference the parser applies is reported as unused, and its finding names the referrers that do not apply it.

## Analyse

Read `statement-usage` for each statement's references and their parser effect. Every reference in the grammar facts counts, so a reference from an affix process, a rule context or an infix position is seen the same way as one from an allomorph environment. A statement is used for parsing when one reference is `applied`. A statement whose references are all not applied, such as `ignored`, `unresolved` or `owner_not_loaded`, is unused for parsing. A statement with no reference at all is unused. The finding names each referrer that does not apply it.

## Ruling

An applied keep or defer is tied to this finding's exact evidence. See [Ruling](term:ruling) for how it appears in Active and Suppressed lists and returns after relevant evidence changes.

A statement with an applied reference is used for parsing and is never reported here. An unused statement that only references the parser does not apply may have a broken reference rather than an unused statement, so check those references before deciding.

## Ask the linguist

Ask whether an unused statement is reserved for planned work or can be retired. Include its identity, its referrers, and their parser effects.

## Update

No typed retirement action is available for this finding. After confirming that a statement is unused, record a `defer` with the referrer evidence until a semantic removal action can name the supported deletion scope. A statement that a reference the parser does not apply still names needs that reference fixed first, not removal.

## Verify

Re-run the view and confirm the retired statement is absent while every applied reference and Approved reading remains intact.

## Grounding

Engineering check: exact redundancy in the authored grammar; no linguistic claim.

- **[bender-poulson-drellishak-evans-2007]** — Emily M. Bender, Laurie Poulson, Scott Drellishak, and Chris Evans. 2007. “Validation and Regression Testing for a Cross-linguistic Grammar Resource.” In *ACL 2007 Workshop on Deep Linguistic Processing*, 136–143. Association for Computational Linguistics. [Source](https://aclanthology.org/W07-1218/). Grounds the use of regression checks when changing grammar resources.

entries.title: Tag the context implies
entries.description: This check finds a tag whose carriers all already match a rule's context. The context alone may select the same stems, so the tag may be redundant.
entries.helpPage:
# Tag the context implies

This check finds a tag whose carriers all already match a rule's context. The context alone may select the same stems, so the tag may be redundant.

## Analyse

Compare every carrier with the rule context. When all match, the tag selects nothing the context does not.

## Ruling

An applied keep or defer is tied to this finding's exact evidence. See [Ruling](term:ruling) for how it appears in Active and Suppressed lists and returns after relevant evidence changes.

No ruling mapping exists for this finding yet, so it cannot be recorded with a Notebook ruling. Note the decision in the review instead.

## Ask the linguist

Ask whether the tag marks a lexical property beyond the context or only repeats it.

## Update

No typed action is available for this finding yet. Remove the tag from the rule and its carriers in FieldWorks after checking readings are unchanged.

## Verify

Re-run the check and confirm the finding is gone, then confirm that no Approved reading changed.

## Grounding

- **[black-2018]** — H. Andrew Black. 2018. “Introduction to Parsing.” SIL FieldWorks technical document, 12 April 2018. [Source](https://software.sil.org/fieldworks/help/technical-documents/). Describes how an affix attaches to a stem by category; it does not say that a stem without one is wrong, so the finding asks rather than concludes.

entries.title: Tag on most possible hosts
entries.description: This check finds a tag that at least half of a rule's possible hosts carry. The tag is then the default, and the rule is better stated as applying everywhere with the minority tagged instead. It is computed from per-rule host counts that PanGloss already holds, in one pass over the tag and rule facts.
entries.helpPage:
# Tag on most possible hosts

This check finds a tag that at least half of a rule's possible hosts carry. The tag is then the default, and the rule is better stated as applying everywhere with the minority tagged instead. It is computed from per-rule host counts that PanGloss already holds, in one pass over the tag and rule facts.

This check is partial. It counts possible hosts by the rule's category scope and does not see its phonological context, so a rule chosen by the form of the stem is not detected. No finding does not mean the tags are fine.

## Analyse

Read how many stems satisfy the rule context and how many of them carry the tag. A majority means the polarity is inverted: the exception is the stems that lack the tag.

## Ruling

An applied keep or defer is tied to this finding's exact evidence. See [Ruling](term:ruling) for how it appears in Active and Suppressed lists and returns after relevant evidence changes.

No ruling mapping exists for this finding yet, so it cannot be recorded with a Notebook ruling. Note the decision in the review instead.

## Ask the linguist

Ask whether the stems that lack the tag are a lexical minority or evidence of a missing condition.

## Update

No typed action is available for this finding yet. Flip the rule to apply by default and tag the minority in FieldWorks.

## Verify

Re-run the check and confirm the finding is gone, then confirm that no Approved reading changed.

## Grounding

- **[black-2018]** — H. Andrew Black. 2018. “Introduction to Parsing.” SIL FieldWorks technical document, 12 April 2018. [Source](https://software.sil.org/fieldworks/help/technical-documents/). Describes how an affix attaches to a stem by category; it does not say that a stem without one is wrong, so the finding asks rather than concludes.

entries.title: Variants of one shape
entries.description: This check finds five or more added variants that share one variant type, environment, feature and string correspondence. One alternation may cover them. A package adding such a group must carry a recorded rule attempt, or a reviewer holds it.
entries.helpPage:
# Variants of one shape

This check finds five or more added variants that share one variant type, environment, feature and string correspondence. One alternation may cover them. A package adding such a group must carry a recorded rule attempt, or a reviewer holds it.

## Analyse

Group the variants by shape and read the correspondence, such as final-vowel loss, then read whether a rule attempt is recorded for the shape.

## Ruling

An applied keep or defer is tied to this finding's exact evidence. See [Ruling](term:ruling) for how it appears in Active and Suppressed lists and returns after relevant evidence changes.

No ruling mapping exists for this finding yet, so it cannot be recorded with a Notebook ruling. Note the decision in the review instead.

## Ask the linguist

Ask whether a rule was tried, what its prediction test showed, and why it failed.

## Update

No typed action is available for this finding yet. Author the rule and retire the variants it covers, or record the failed rule attempt.

## Verify

Re-run the check and confirm the finding is gone, then confirm that no Approved reading changed.

## Grounding

- **[black-2018]** — H. Andrew Black. 2018. “Introduction to Parsing.” SIL FieldWorks technical document, 12 April 2018. [Source](https://software.sil.org/fieldworks/help/technical-documents/). Describes how an affix attaches to a stem by category; it does not say that a stem without one is wrong, so the finding asks rather than concludes.

entries.title: A broad variant competes
entries.description: An unconditioned allomorph may be an intentional final fallback. Its selection order and other grammatical restrictions determine what to change.
entries.helpPage:
# A broad variant competes

An unconditioned allomorph may be an intentional final fallback. Its selection order and other grammatical restrictions determine what to change.

## Analyse

Read effective selection order, sibling conditions, load facts, and the contexts in which each variant is chosen.

## Ruling

An applied keep or defer is tied to this finding's exact evidence. See [Ruling](term:ruling) for how it appears in Active and Suppressed lists and returns after relevant evidence changes.

Use `EditAllomorphCondition` to attach a confirmed condition to the exact broad variant. Use `OrderAllomorphs` when a confirmed broad variant should follow its conditioned siblings as the final fallback. Keep a confirmed fallback or free variant with a recorded reason and no grammar repair among the changes not applied yet; ask about morphological gates; defer invalid conditions to grammar health.

## Ask the linguist

Ask whether the broad form is a final fallback or should be limited to particular contexts. Include any unwanted-reading witness.

## Update

Stage a change with `EditAllomorphCondition` for a confirmed restriction or `OrderAllomorphs` for a confirmed fallback order. Both actions retain the existing allomorph identities; condition edits leave other allomorph users alone.

## Verify

Use the Proposal in Proposals to inspect what the edit would write, then compare parser results from the current and edited scratch copies for the same words. Check the exact Approved readings, the attributed unwanted reading and reviewed negatives, held-out positives, and any elsewhere fallback cases. If `effective-allomorph-order` is unavailable, name it and defer.

## Grounding

- **[black-2018]** — H. Andrew Black. 2018. “Introduction to Parsing.” SIL FieldWorks technical document, 12 April 2018. [Technical documents index](https://software.sil.org/fieldworks/help/technical-documents/). Describes allomorph environments, ordered alternatives, and default or elsewhere behavior.
- **[bender-poulson-drellishak-evans-2007]** — Emily M. Bender, Laurie Poulson, Scott Drellishak, and Chris Evans. 2007. “Validation and Regression Testing for a Cross-linguistic Grammar Resource.” In *ACL 2007 Workshop on Deep Linguistic Processing*, 136–143. Association for Computational Linguistics. [ACL Anthology](https://aclanthology.org/W07-1218/). Supports checking intended and unwanted parser outcomes with regression examples.

This is an engineering check grounded in FieldWorks practice; no general linguistic rule makes a final fallback harmful.

entries.title: Environment may be too broad
entries.description: Unobserved contexts are not bad forms. The first check covers one neighboring phoneme or an explicit boundary on one side; unsupported shapes and ambiguous alignments abstain.
entries.helpPage:
# Environment may be too broad

Unobserved contexts are not bad forms. The first check covers one neighboring phoneme or an explicit boundary on one side; unsupported shapes and ambiguous alignments abstain.

## Analyse

Read `environment-excess` for the effective contexts after compiled sibling order, OR alternatives, observed triggers, extra contexts, and missed triggers. Reading the whole view, each list shows its first 30 names; reading one object (`--object-id`, which a finding's evidence links use) lists every name. The row's `totals` give the full count of every list and of the loaded context universe. A limit line in the Report names the first dozen contexts and counts the rest. Filter by an environment identity to inspect the other measured users. `approved-morph-sequences` carries the aligned word evidence. Ambiguous alignment or a condition outside the one-neighbor capability is reported as inconclusive.

## Ruling

An applied keep or defer is tied to this finding's exact evidence. See [Ruling](term:ruling) for how it appears in Active and Suppressed lists and returns after relevant evidence changes.

Ask by default when the only evidence is that a context has not appeared in the Texts. An extra licensed context is not evidence that the context is wrong. A finding needs an extra context and at least three Approved word types across two stems; that support floor ranks a question but does not decide it. Keep a productive extension and defer unsupported context shapes.

## Ask the linguist

Ask whether a contrasting form in the extra licensed context is possible. Offer valid, invalid, or unknown as the response.

## Update

Only after a linguist confirms a wrong-context example, stage changes with `AuthorEnvironment` and `EditAllomorphCondition`, declaring the environment creation as a dependency of the relink. Relink only the intended allomorph user; leave shared users attached to their current environment. Do not narrow globally to the observed segments by default. Use the named word-boundary context for a word edge; do not infer a word edge from a displayed `#` marker.

## Verify

Use the Proposal in Proposals to inspect what the edit would write, then compare parser results from the current and edited scratch copies for the same words. Check every exact Approved reading, held-out positive forms, and reviewed wrong-context negatives; confirm the shared users remain unchanged. The view reports extra and missed trigger sets; a missed trigger prevents an excess score. Show context counts, not a correctness rate. If the context universe, compiler order, or unique alignment is unavailable, name it and defer.

## Grounding

- **[prince-tesar-2004]** — Alan Prince and Bruce Tesar. 2004. “Learning Phonotactic Distributions.” In *Constraints in Phonological Acquisition*, 245–291. Cambridge University Press. DOI: 10.1017/CBO9780511486418.009. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511486418.009). Shows that positive evidence can leave different grammars making different predictions about unseen forms.
- **[tenenbaum-griffiths-2001]** — Joshua B. Tenenbaum and Thomas L. Griffiths. 2001. “Generalization, Similarity, and Bayesian Inference.” *Behavioral and Brain Sciences* 24(4):629–640. DOI: 10.1017/S0140525X01000061. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0140525X01000061). Derives a preference for smaller extensions under a specified strong-sampling model and explains how priors affect it.
- **[gold-1967]** — E. Mark Gold. 1967. “Language Identification in the Limit.” *Information and Control* 10(5):447–474. DOI: 10.1016/S0019-9958(67)91165-5. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0019-9958(67)91165-5). Shows that positive-only learning depends on the hypothesis class and the form of the evidence.
- **[wexler-1993]** — Kenneth Wexler. 1993. “The Subset Principle is an Intensional Principle.” In Eric Reuland and Werner Abraham (eds.), *Knowledge and Language: Volume I, From Orwell’s Problem to Plato’s Problem*, 217–239. Dordrecht: Springer. DOI: 10.1007/978-94-011-1840-8_10. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-94-011-1840-8_10). States a smallest-language choice for a nested hypothesis space under its learning assumptions.
- **[wexler-manzini-1987]** — Kenneth Wexler and M. Rita Manzini. 1987. “Parameters and Learnability in Binding Theory.” In Thomas Roeper and Edwin Williams (eds.), *Parameter Setting*, 41–76. Dordrecht: D. Reidel. DOI: 10.1007/978-94-009-3727-7_3. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-94-009-3727-7_3). Identifies a distinct parameter-setting and learnability chapter in binding theory; it is background, not evidence about Motif's environment detector.

The finite context universe and support floor are engineering choices, not a learned probability model or linguistic law.

entries.title: Class contains extra segments
entries.description: Extra natural-class members may be productive. Review every usage site, its Approved triggers, the feature intersection, and unknown membership before changing the class. A feature intersection is a deterministic set calculation, not a probability; it cannot show that an unobserved member is wrong.
entries.helpPage:
# Class contains extra segments

Extra natural-class members may be productive. Review every usage site, its Approved triggers, the feature intersection, and unknown membership before changing the class. A feature intersection is a deterministic set calculation, not a probability; it cannot show that an unobserved member is wrong.

## Analyse

Read `natural-class-excess` for each measured usage site, the current effective extension, observed triggers, missed triggers, feature-intersection extension, and unknown members. Reading the whole view, each list shows its first 30 names; reading one object (`--object-id`, which a finding's evidence links use) lists every name. The row's `totals` give the full count of every list and of the loaded context universe. A limit line in the Report names the first dozen members and counts the rest. `approved-morph-sequences` contains aligned Approved words. The shared feature assignments determine the set of possible class members from the loaded chart; this calculation has no sampling model and is not a probability. Missing feature values remain unknown, and a class may intentionally generalize beyond its current observations.

## Ruling

An applied keep or defer is tied to this finding's exact evidence. See [Ruling](term:ruling) for how it appears in Active and Suppressed lists and returns after relevant evidence changes.

Fix only an independently reviewed leak; keep a productive extension with a reason; ask for contrasts; defer incomplete feature or context attribution. The measure reports definite extras at a uniquely attributed site, including sparse support, and makes no automatic change. A p-only observation with held-out b and m positives supports keeping B={p,b,m} when those members remain productive.

## Ask the linguist

Ask whether the process applies to the additional segments and request independent examples, not endorsement of the smallest observed set.

## Update

Use `EditNaturalClass` to change the segment members of one explicitly scoped class. Its review lists every environment, rewrite rule, and morphological insertion that uses the class. When users have different meanings, use `AuthorNaturalClass` to create a separate class and `RelinkNaturalClass` to move only the confirmed typed environment or rule contexts. The other users stay on the original class. Neither route changes a feature chart.

## Verify

Use the Proposal in Proposals to inspect what the edit would write, then compare parser results from the current and edited scratch copies for the same words. A confirmed correction must make the reviewed wrong form complete with no accepted reading, preserve every Approved reading, and retain valid held-out positives such as b and m. For a relink, verify the intended user changes and the other users still parse through the original class. A Keep records its reason against the finding evidence and makes no grammar edit. The view reports the definite feature-intersection extension and unknown members; when membership is unknown, do not claim an exact excess rate or a tightest class. If class extension or unique context attribution is unavailable, name it and defer.

## Grounding

- **[chomsky-halle-1968]** — Noam Chomsky and Morris Halle. 1968. *The Sound Pattern of English*. New York: Harper & Row. [MIT Press publisher record](https://mitpress.mit.edu/9780262530972/the-sound-pattern-of-english/). Its notation-specific evaluation metric illustrates one proposal for comparing grammar economy.
- **[albright-hayes-2003]** — Adam Albright and Bruce Hayes. 2003. “Rules vs. Analogy in English Past Tenses: A Computational/Experimental Study.” *Cognition* 90(2):119–161. DOI: 10.1016/S0010-0277(03)00146-X. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0010-0277(03)00146-X). Uses segmental features to generalize conditioning environments from paradigm examples.
- **[gold-1967]** — E. Mark Gold. 1967. “Language Identification in the Limit.” *Information and Control* 10(5):447–474. DOI: 10.1016/S0019-9958(67)91165-5. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0019-9958(67)91165-5). Supports keeping an unobserved class member distinct from a disconfirmed one.

Feature intersection is a deterministic way to describe a possible class from the loaded chart. It is not a probability, and an unobserved segment is not thereby shown to be wrong.

entries.title: A required slot blocks a form
entries.description: This Text-tier finding shows an Approved form that fits no applicable template with all obligatory slots filled. A template accepts the reading when it embeds the sequence in order and all its obligatory slots are filled; one accepting template prevents a finding. The measure does not run a parser counterfactual and does not establish that the parser blocked the form.
entries.helpPage:
# A required slot blocks a form

This Text-tier finding shows an Approved form that fits no applicable template with all obligatory slots filled. A template accepts the reading when it embeds the sequence in order and all its obligatory slots are filled; one accepting template prevents a finding. The measure does not run a parser counterfactual and does not establish that the parser blocked the form.

## Analyse

Read each Approved sequence against every applicable template that embeds it in order. Inspect the obligatory slots left unfilled in each failed template; alternative templates can leave different slots as joint or ambiguous causes. Read every slot user and any possible feature-bearing zeroes. The slot-context evidence must include every template and category that shares the slot, including subcategories, because optionality changes all of those users.

## Ruling

An applied keep or defer is tied to this finding's exact evidence. See [Ruling](term:ruling) for how it appears in Active and Suppressed lists and returns after relevant evidence changes.

Ask whether the pattern calls for an optional slot, a separate template, or a null affix. Keep an obligatory marker when it carries a grammatical distinction; defer when the evidence does not distinguish the choices.

## Ask the linguist

Ask whether these forms use an optional slot, a separate template, or a null affix. Show every compatible template, its unfilled obligatory slots, every template that shares each slot, and the Approved morph sequences.

## Update

For a one-slot comparison, make a change whose only edit is `EditAffixSlot` setting the implicated slot optional. A separate template through `AuthorAffixTemplate`, or a meaningful null affix through the appropriate lexical action, is a different change and needs its own evidence. The optionality change affects every template and subcategory that uses the shared slot.

## Verify

Use the Proposal in Proposals to inspect what the edit would write. Compare parser results from the current and edited scratch copies for the same words. Check before and after production of the exact Approved target reading, every previously produced Approved reading, and each reviewed negative. Recommend making the slot optional only when the target is newly produced, no Approved reading is lost, and no reviewed negative becomes accepted. If parser results are incomplete, the target remains missing, an Approved reading is lost, or a reviewed negative becomes accepted, name that reason and leave the change unrecommended.

## Grounding

- **[black-2018]** — H. Andrew Black. 2018. “Introduction to Parsing.” SIL FieldWorks technical document, 12 April 2018. [Technical documents index](https://software.sil.org/fieldworks/help/technical-documents/). Explains obligatory and optional slots, null affixes, and alternative templates.
- **[bender-poulson-drellishak-evans-2007]** — Emily M. Bender, Laurie Poulson, Scott Drellishak, and Chris Evans. 2007. “Validation and Regression Testing for a Cross-linguistic Grammar Resource.” In *ACL 2007 Workshop on Deep Linguistic Processing*, 136–143. Association for Computational Linguistics. [ACL Anthology](https://aclanthology.org/W07-1218/). Supports paired positive and negative regression checks after a grammar change.

The one-slot counterfactual and zero-loss, no-new-negative requirements are engineering safeguards, not a linguistic frequency rule.

entries.title: Order excludes a valid form
entries.description: An Approved reading may conflict with the order declared by a template. Alternative templates and ambiguous placements must remain visible.
entries.helpPage:
# Order excludes a valid form

An Approved reading may conflict with the order declared by a template. Alternative templates and ambiguous placements must remain visible.

## Analyse

Read complete slot placements, category inheritance, all alternative templates, and both attested directions. A certain contradiction requires complete assignment enumeration and no order-compatible applicable template; pair-order variability is descriptive evidence on its own.

## Ruling

An applied keep or defer is tied to this finding's exact evidence. See [Ruling](term:ruling) for how it appears in Active and Suppressed lists and returns after relevant evidence changes.

Fix an incorrect order; keep a real alternative with an accurate representation; ask about dialect differences; defer uncertain attribution.

## Ask the linguist

Ask whether the template should reverse its slots or whether the forms belong to a separate template. Show both directions when attested.

## Update

Use `EditAffixTemplate` to reorder an existing template when the linguist confirms one order. When both directions are Approved, preserve the existing order and use `AuthorAffixTemplate` to add an explicit alternative with its own slot membership. Do not infer a derivation that chains multiple templates.

## Verify

Use the Proposal in Proposals to inspect what the edit would write. Compare parser results from the current and edited project for the same words. Check the exact Approved readings in both directions: the intended reading must be produced and every previously produced Approved reading must remain. Look for reviewed mixed-branch combinations, slot swaps, and double fills that become accepted. If one is newly accepted or an Approved reading is lost, do not apply the change. If none of those combinations has a reviewed label, report structural improvement only. Incomplete parser results or unavailable `template-embeddings` leave the order claim unverified; name the gap and defer it.

## Grounding

- **[black-2018]** — H. Andrew Black. 2018. “Introduction to Parsing.” SIL FieldWorks technical document, 12 April 2018. [Technical documents index](https://software.sil.org/fieldworks/help/technical-documents/). Distinguishes slot order, optionality, and alternative templates.
- **[hyman-2003]** — Larry M. Hyman. 2003. “Suffix Ordering in Bantu: A Morphocentric Approach.” In *Yearbook of Morphology 2002*, 245–281. DOI: 10.1007/0-306-48223-1_8. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/0-306-48223-1_8). Presents a default Bantu suffix template alongside language-specific ordering constraints.
- **[hyman-mchombo-1992]** — Larry M. Hyman and Sam Mchombo. 1992. “Morphotactic Constraints in the Chichewa Verb Stem.” In *Proceedings of the Eighteenth Annual Meeting of the Berkeley Linguistics Society: General Session and Parasession on The Place of Morphology in a Grammar*, 350–364. DOI: 10.3765/bls.v18i1.1579. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.3765/bls.v18i1.1579). Provides a language-specific analysis of constraints on Chichewa verb-stem morphology.
- **[stump-1993]** — Gregory T. Stump. 1993. “Position Classes and Morphological Theory.” *Yearbook of Morphology 1992*, 129–180. DOI: 10.1007/978-94-017-3710-4_7. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-94-017-3710-4_7). Discusses alternative position-class representations and limits of simple linear ordering.
- **[ryan-2010]** — Kevin M. Ryan. 2010. “Variable Affix Order: Grammar and Learning.” *Language* 86(4):758–791. DOI: 10.1353/lan.2010.0032. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1353/lan.2010.0032). Shows that affix order may be variable and that position-class formalisms can undergenerate some systems.

The embedding search, cap, and certain-contradiction rule are Motif engineering choices; preserve attested alternatives instead of averaging away variable order.

entries.title: A Disapproved reading parses
entries.description: A word can have both an Approved reading and a Disapproved one. Narrow only the condition that licenses the unwanted morphology.
entries.helpPage:
# A Disapproved reading parses

A word can have both an Approved reading and a Disapproved one. Narrow only the condition that licenses the unwanted morphology.

This measure reads a saved parser run bound to the exact Baseline or proposed source. Without one, the result is `not-run`.

## Analyse

Compare the ordered Form, MSA, and inflection-type identities under ADR 0020. The finding says that PanGloss produced the same morphology as a Disapproved analysis; it does not declare the whole word impossible. Approved and Unknown readings stay separate.

Inspect its retained parser case with `parsimony view` (parser cases) and the finding's exact case key. Incomplete searches and surfaces that cannot be joined to one writing-system wordform do not count as completed evidence.

## Ruling

An applied keep or defer is tied to this finding's exact evidence. See [Ruling](term:ruling) for how it appears in Active and Suppressed lists and returns after relevant evidence changes.

Fix an identified condition; keep when rejection concerns sense rather than morphology; ask about missing conditions; defer unknown attribution.

## Ask the linguist

Ask whether the Disapproved reading has a distinct grammatical condition. Include all Approved readings on the same word.

## Update

Change only the confirmed allomorph condition, preserving identity, feature requirements, and selection order.

## Verify

Check that the exact Disapproved morphology disappears and every Approved morphology remains. If `parser-signatures` is unavailable, name it and defer.

## Grounding

- **[bender-poulson-drellishak-evans-2007]** — Emily M. Bender, Laurie Poulson, Scott Drellishak, and Chris Evans. 2007. “Validation and Regression Testing for a Cross-linguistic Grammar Resource.” In *ACL 2007 Workshop on Deep Linguistic Processing*, 136–143. Association for Computational Linguistics. [ACL Anthology](https://aclanthology.org/W07-1218/). Supports comparing parser outcomes against labeled positive and negative examples.
- **[kol-nir-wintner-2014]** — Sheli Kol, Bracha Nir, and Shuly Wintner. 2014. “Computational Evaluation of the Traceback Method.” *Journal of Child Language* 41(1):176–199. DOI: 10.1017/S0305000912000694. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0305000912000694). Reports computational evaluation exposing flaws in predicted analyses.

The exact morphology identity and Opinion meaning used here follow Motif's project contract; these sources support outcome testing, not that local identity rule.

entries.title: A reviewed negative parses
entries.description: A reviewed negative that parses is direct evidence of a possible restriction problem. The repair must target the witnessed structure and preserve valid readings.
entries.helpPage:
# A reviewed negative parses

A reviewed negative that parses is direct evidence of a possible restriction problem. The repair must target the witnessed structure and preserve valid readings.

## Analyse

Read the negative judgment, its provenance, the parser's returned morphs, and the current slot order. Check positive forms and alternate readings.

## Ruling

An applied keep or defer is tied to this finding's exact evidence. See [Ruling](term:ruling) for how it appears in Active and Suppressed lists and returns after relevant evidence changes.

Fix a confirmed order error; correct mistaken evidence separately; ask about register or reading differences; defer an unsupported cause.

## Ask the linguist

Ask whether the reversed order is impossible in this category or valid in another use. Show the actual analyses and a matching positive.

## Update

Edit the existing template order for the confirmed category. Keep the reviewed-negative judgment unchanged.

## Verify

Require a completed search with no target reading, preserved Approved readings, and stable held-out controls. If `reviewed-negative-expectations` is unavailable, name it and defer.

## Grounding

- **[gold-1967]** — E. Mark Gold. 1967. “Language Identification in the Limit.” *Information and Control* 10(5):447–474. DOI: 10.1016/S0019-9958(67)91165-5. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0019-9958(67)91165-5). Distinguishes positive-only text from an informant that labels membership and nonmembership.
- **[bender-poulson-drellishak-evans-2007]** — Emily M. Bender, Laurie Poulson, Scott Drellishak, and Chris Evans. 2007. “Validation and Regression Testing for a Cross-linguistic Grammar Resource.” In *ACL 2007 Workshop on Deep Linguistic Processing*, 136–143. Association for Computational Linguistics. [ACL Anthology](https://aclanthology.org/W07-1218/). Supports keeping positive recovery and negative rejection as separate regression outcomes.
- **[prince-tesar-2004]** — Alan Prince and Bruce Tesar. 2004. “Learning Phonotactic Distributions.” In *Constraints in Phonological Acquisition*, 245–291. Cambridge University Press. DOI: 10.1017/CBO9780511486418.009. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511486418.009). Explains that grammars consistent with positive data can differ on unseen forms, while negative judgments are distinct evidence.

An absent word or an accepted parser probe alone is not a negative judgment.

entries.title: Passage
entries.description: Passage is the reader in Texts. Each word shows where it stands: approved, a guess, needing an analysis, or waiting for Apply because you staged a change. Words that need an analysis are the gaps; Tab moves to the next word without an approved analysis.
entries.helpPage:
# Passage

**Passage** is the reader in **Texts**. Each word shows where it stands: approved, a guess, needing an analysis, or waiting for **Apply** because you staged a change. Words that need an analysis are the gaps; Tab moves to the next word without an approved analysis.

## Keeping a reading at chosen places

Choose a word to open the word panel beside the reader, or under it in a narrow window. It lists the places the word occurs, twenty at a time, with a check box for each and a count of how many are ticked. Places that already hold an approved analysis cannot be ticked. Choose **Check Gaps** to tick the shown places that still need one.

Pick the analysis to keep, then choose **Approve**. The button names the number of places. Motif stages one pending change for each ticked place, and a place shows as staged only after its change has been written. Nothing reaches FieldWorks until you choose **Apply** in [Proposals](guide:proposals). A reading that Motif only guessed is staged the same way, so it stays your decision.

The panel also holds **Not a Word**, which marks the spelling as not a word for the whole project, not only at the ticked places.

## Keys

Enter keeps the focused word's analysis. Shift+Enter keeps it at all the places like this one; when you have chosen a reading in the word panel, it keeps that reading at the focused word and the places ticked in the panel. Tab moves to the next gap, Space opens the word card and Escape closes it. [Keyboard Shortcuts](guide:keyboard-shortcuts) lists them all.

![A pending choice shown on its word card](shot:explained-word-card/unknown-staged)

entries.title: Pending Changes
entries.description: Changes staged from a word stay pending until a person applies them. Open Proposals to inspect the pending document and its Comments and evidence. Staging does not write changes to FieldWorks.
entries.helpPage:
# Pending Changes

Changes staged from a word stay pending until a person applies them. Open **Proposals** to inspect the pending document and its Comments and evidence. Staging does not write changes to FieldWorks.

## Keeps staged from the Passage

Keeping a reading in **Texts**, whether with Enter, Shift+Enter or **Approve** in the word panel, stages one pending change for each place. Each change records the word, the place it belongs to and the reading you chose, and a place shows as staged only after its change has been written. Keeping the same reading at a place that is already staged does nothing, so nothing is staged twice.

A keep of a reading that only the parser offered is a new analysis. FieldWorks creates it only when you choose **Apply**, and it is still your decision until then. Before applying, open the pending document in [Proposals](guide:proposals), which lists the staged changes by Text. Proposals has no button to undo one; to take back the last staged choice, press Ctrl+Z (⌘+Z on macOS) in the window.

If a keep is refused, the sentence beside the word panel or in the status line says why, and no place that was not written is shown as staged.

**Undo** and **Redo** (Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y, ⌘+Z and ⌘+Shift+Z on macOS) affect staged changes only, one staging action at a time, and the window has no on-screen Undo button. Before applying, check that the changes still fit the project and explicitly measure what they do. Missing or outdated evidence is not a successful check. See [Apply to FieldWorks](guide:apply-to-fieldworks) and [When a Change No Longer Fits](guide:when-a-change-no-longer-fits).

entries.title: Progress
entries.description: Progress shows supported next actions for the current project. A Proposal appears here when its stored standing says it is waiting for a decision. When no supported action is available, the page leaves it out.
entries.helpPage:
# Progress

**Progress** shows supported next actions for the current project. A Proposal appears here when its stored standing says it is waiting for a decision. When no supported action is available, the page leaves it out.

**Next** is a plain list. Choose a waiting-Proposal row to open **Proposals** and review the stored Trials. Use Tab to reach a row and Enter or Space to open it.

While the list is being read again, old rows disappear. If some actions cannot be read, the page says so and offers **Try Again**. Missing information is not a count of zero.

Chapter approval totals and **This Week** activity are unavailable. Motif does not turn parse completion or approved wordform counts into a percentage of approved places in your texts.

The health strip shows available project facts. Open its details for the recorded median parser work, when one exists, and to turn on Diagnostics. Opening this page or the health details does not start a parse. See [Progress and project health](guide:overview).

entries.title: Proposals
entries.description: Proposals lists every set of changes people and assistants have proposed. A Proposal shows Built by, Model and Question only when an MCP session recorded them. Choose a name in Open Proposals. Each selected Proposal stays open as a document, with its own Rationale, Comments and evidence. Choose an open document's name to return to it. Switching documents keeps your typing; Close Proposal asks you to save or cancel an unsaved edit first.
entries.helpPage:
# Proposals

**Proposals** lists every set of changes people and assistants have proposed. A Proposal shows **Built by**, **Model** and **Question** only when an MCP session recorded them. Choose a name in **Open Proposals**. Each selected Proposal stays open as a document, with its own Rationale, Comments and evidence. Choose an open document's name to return to it. Switching documents keeps your typing; **Close Proposal** asks you to save or cancel an unsaved edit first.

Selection and comparison are separate. Check two Proposals to choose the pair for Compare. Checking a third cannot silently replace either choice: uncheck one first. Closed history remains available through **Show Closed**. See [Compare Proposals](guide:compare-proposals).

**Will Fill In** lists words whose complete parser searches establish no analysis before and an analysis afterward. **Will Change** lists supported reading or spelling acceptance changes. These are effects, rather than sums of advisory categories. Evidence names the single FieldWorks Text it covers. Listed words may be only part of that Text's results; absent, expired, unreadable, incomplete and outdated evidence never means zero. Exact approved places and whole-Context totals remain unavailable when the stored evidence cannot establish them.

Start with **Proposed changes**. Each row describes a change in the Proposal. When its most recent try still applies to the saved project, the row shows recorded before and after values where available.

Follow **Before you apply**. Choose **Try It** or **Try Again** to measure the Proposal on a copy. Choose a Text and **Make Difference** to compare its words. Choose **Run Dry Run** to check and record what would change in FieldWorks. When the checklist is complete and the changes are ready, **Apply…** opens the confirmation and backup reminder. Opening a Proposal starts no checks.

Read [Review a Proposal](guide:review-a-proposal) and [Apply to FieldWorks](guide:apply-to-fieldworks) before applying.

To bring in changes you made in an edited record file, choose **File > Open Record File…**, browse for the file and choose **Preview**. The window lists the operations the file would make and, under **Not imported**, each change it cannot make, with its code, class, field and reason. Give the Draft a name and choose **Stage**; Motif then opens the new Draft on this page. Nothing is applied until you apply it yourself.

entries.title: Reading project health
entries.description: The health strip reports facts available from the saved project and stored results. A warning is a finding to inspect, not an instruction to change the grammar. Open Diagnostics when enabled to read stored warnings and rule timing.
entries.helpPage:
# Reading project health

The health strip reports facts available from the saved project and stored results. A warning is a finding to inspect, not an instruction to change the grammar. Open **Diagnostics** when enabled to read stored warnings and rule timing.

Parser work measures the work recorded by the parser. It is distinct from elapsed time on a particular computer. A missing or stale measurement does not mean that the parser did no work; Motif leaves unavailable health facts out. The median, when recorded, is in the health details.

Opening these views does not run the parser. After saving in FieldWorks, choose **Refresh** to read the saved project, then parse the current Selection when you need new results. See [Progress and project health](guide:overview).

The Progress page’s Next rows open waiting Proposals and open Requests. Their counts come from stored records, and rows disappear while those records are read again. Neither parser completion nor a wordform’s approved analysis proves that a person approved every occurrence. See [Progress](guide:progress).

entries.title: Refresh the project
entries.description: Use Refresh after saving changes in FieldWorks when you want Motif to read that saved state. Refresh captures a new Baseline and checks the grammar for Warnings. It does not parse words. Choose Parse all words after Refresh to measure the current Default Selection.
entries.helpPage:
# Refresh the project

Use **Refresh** after saving changes in FieldWorks when you want Motif to read that saved state. Refresh captures a new [Baseline](term:baseline) and checks the grammar for **Warnings**. It does not parse words. Choose [Parse all words](term:parse-all-words) after Refresh to measure the current [Default Selection](term:default-selection).

1. Save your work in FieldWorks.
2. In Motif, choose **Refresh** (the ⟳ beside the project name in the top bar) and let it finish.
3. If setup opens after the first Baseline, choose what to measure and press **Start First Run**. Otherwise, open the project card (choose the project name in the top bar) and choose **Parse all words**.
4. Check **Progress**. Refresh updates the project counts and checks the grammar; parsing updates the parse results.

If you cancel **Parse all words** or the parser refuses it, Refresh's new Baseline remains; parse results do not describe it until a parse completes. Opening Motif again does not refresh a project that already has a Baseline.

![Refresh captures a Baseline before a separate parse updates the numbers](shot:review-apply-refresh-parse/refreshed)

entries.title: Replace a Pending Change
entries.description: Return to the word in Texts. Press Ctrl+Z (⌘+Z on macOS) to take back the last staged choice, or stage the new choice for the same place. There is no on-screen Undo button, and Ctrl+Z takes back only the most recent staging action. Read the word's current context before making another choice. Undo affects staging only and does not reverse an applied Proposal.
entries.helpPage:
# Replace a Pending Change

Return to the word in **Texts**. Press Ctrl+Z (⌘+Z on macOS) to take back the last staged choice, or stage the new choice for the same place. There is no on-screen Undo button, and Ctrl+Z takes back only the most recent staging action. Read the word's current context before making another choice. **Undo** affects staging only and does not reverse an applied Proposal.

After replacing a staged change, measure the exact new content again before applying. Earlier evidence does not establish readiness for the replacement. Read [Pending Changes](guide:pending-changes) and [Apply to FieldWorks](guide:apply-to-fieldworks).

entries.title: Review a Proposal
entries.description: Select a Proposal in Proposals. Read its Rationale and supported effects above Comments. You can keep several documents open, including Drafts and Waiting Proposals, without sharing their edits or Trial results.
entries.helpPage:
# Review a Proposal

Select a Proposal in **Proposals**. Read its Rationale and supported effects above **Comments**. You can keep several documents open, including Drafts and Waiting Proposals, without sharing their edits or Trial results.

Earlier versions called a Waiting Proposal Ready.

Before a Proposal is tried, each change shows the value the project holds now beside the proposed one. A Deferred Proposal offers **Bring Back to Waiting**, on the page and in the Apply confirmation. An Applied Proposal shows what was applied: when and by whom, each field before and after, and what the Differences saved before the Apply found.

The evidence names its Text and any limits. **Will Fill In** requires complete searches on both sides. **Will Change** requires an actual reading or spelling acceptance change. The window does not infer approved places lost from a regression count. Missing detail is unavailable, and incomplete listings do not establish a total of zero.

Comments use FieldWorks Markdown. While a Proposal is open, people may add, edit or delete Comments. A failed save keeps your typing. Refresh reconciles external changes without overwriting an edit; if the Comment changed elsewhere, cancel to read its stored version. Once the Proposal is decided, Comments freeze. Any unsaved typing stays available to copy or cancel.

Use **Before you apply** to follow the three checks on the Proposal document. Choose **Apply…** to open the confirmation once the checks and readiness rules are met. Only confirming **Apply** writes to FieldWorks. See [Apply to FieldWorks](guide:apply-to-fieldworks).

entries.title: Review Changes in a Proposal
entries.description: Review changes within the selected document on Proposals. Read its Rationale, supported evidence and Comments, then prepare Apply using the current command readiness. There is no separate Review Changes page.
entries.helpPage:
# Review Changes in a Proposal

Review changes within the selected document on **Proposals**. Read its Rationale, supported evidence and Comments, then prepare Apply using the current command readiness. There is no separate Review Changes page.

See [Review a Proposal](guide:review-a-proposal) and [Apply to FieldWorks](guide:apply-to-fieldworks).

entries.title: Settings
entries.description: Open Settings from the bottom of the left navigation rail to change how Motif looks and to find its keyboard shortcuts, project parsing limits, grammar-check defaults, problem reports, and version information. Help beside it opens guidance for the current page. Display choices are remembered for this user on this computer; a project's parsing limits are saved with that project's Default Selection.
entries.helpPage:
# Settings

Open **Settings** from the bottom of the left navigation rail to change how Motif looks and to find its keyboard shortcuts, project parsing limits, grammar-check defaults, problem reports, and version information. **Help** beside it opens guidance for the current page. Display choices are remembered for this user on this computer; a project's parsing limits are saved with that project's [Default Selection](term:default-selection).

Settings opens as a page. **Back** returns to the page you were using; Escape does the same after handling any field edit. The section navigator is the page's side panel and collapses in a narrow window. Select **Settings** again to open it, then choose a section or collapse the side bar to use the page's full width. [The Motif window](guide:the-window) describes how the panels fold away and return.

## Display

Zoom changes the Motif window's layout and text together. At higher zoom the usable page area is smaller, so scroll within a page to reach its content. Display shows the available zoom choices; [Keyboard shortcuts](guide:keyboard-shortcuts) lists their keys.

**Reset to 100%** is always visible and is disabled when zoom is already 100%.

The **Diagnostics** switch shows or hides the optional Diagnostics page and is remembered for this person. It starts off for a new preference store.

Theme can follow the operating system or use Light or Dark. The change applies while Settings is open.

## Parsing

The Parsing group edits the current project's Default Selection. Setup, Settings, and **Analysis options** edit that same saved limit policy; the next parse uses it, while earlier results keep the limits from their own run. See [Default Selection](guide:default-selection) and [first-run setup](guide:first-run-setup) for choosing what to parse.

Choose Sources and Texts on **Texts**. Settings does not provide a second Source or Text-selection editor.

When the parser work limit is finite, the time limit can follow Motif's estimate or use an explicit value. An explicit value remains in force when the parser work limit changes until you choose the estimate again. When it follows the estimate, a parse gives each word ten times the estimated time as a safety net, so a slow computer reaches the parser work limit first; Setup, Settings and the command line all work this way. With no parser work limit there is no time limit, and an explicit override is cleared. Enter commits a number; leaving the field also commits it. If Motif refuses the value because it is not a positive whole number or the time is out of range, it says why beside the field and keeps what you typed there; nothing is saved and the Selection a run uses stays as it was. Escape, leaving the Parsing group, or leaving Settings puts the last saved value back in the field. If the value is fine but Motif cannot save it, for example because the Selection was changed elsewhere first, Motif restores the saved limits and says why.

## Default Proposal Checks

Default Proposal Checks sets how thorough Motif's grammar check is when it runs by itself or for a Proposal. **Compare Stored Analyses** checks that each word's saved analyses still parse, which is the one part of a grammar check that slows down as a project grows. Choose one:

- **Within a work budget (recommended)** compares words until a fixed amount of work is spent, then says how many were left. It gives the same result on every computer.
- **Every word** compares all of them. A large project can take half a minute or more.
- **Off** skips the comparison; the other grammar checks still run.

The choice is remembered for this user on this computer and applies to the next grammar check. Results already shown keep the choice they were checked with. The command line's [Check a grammar](cmd:grammar%20check) accepts `--stored-analyses` to override it for one run.

## File Handoff

Settings has no Assistant Connections and no API key. **Assistant Access** has one switch, Let Assistants Use Motif's Tools, which lets assistants such as Claude Desktop use Motif's tools through the MCP (see [Connect an assistant](guide:ai-assistants)).

Turn on **Show Hand Off by Copying Files** to use the file Handoff controls in Settings. When you request a Handoff for selected words, Motif opens those controls with the words selected. Choose the write action yourself and review the data-sensitivity notice before sharing the files.

## Writing Systems

For the project's writing-system settings and how to change them in FieldWorks, see [Writing systems in the window](guide:writing-systems).

## Help and reports

Settings lets you preview a problem report. Read [When something goes wrong](guide:when-something-goes-wrong) for what a report includes and how local details are handled.

## About and data folders

About shows Motif, PanGloss, and operating-system versions and can copy those lines. Its folder button opens the managed data root, which holds Motif's paired project data and parser artifacts; FieldWorks projects remain in their own folders. See [When something goes wrong](guide:when-something-goes-wrong) for report contents and privacy choices.

entries.title: Sources
entries.description: Open Texts, then its Sources side panel. A Source names external material; its Context is the books and chapters the project works on. Current Chapter records where you are working on this machine, including a chapter outside that Context. The folder on this machine and Current stay local.
entries.helpPage:
# Sources

Open **Texts**, then its **Sources** side panel. A Source names external material; its **Context** is the books and chapters the project works on. **Current Chapter** records where you are working on this machine, including a chapter outside that Context. The folder on this machine and Current stay local.

The window reads Paratext Source names, saved Context and local settings. Select a Source to inspect these facts. **Stage Context in Proposal** proposes a change; it does not change the saved Context until you review and Apply the Proposal. **Add Paratext Source** also stages a Proposal. Enter the Source ID, name, versification and chapter range; an optional folder is saved locally when the Source is staged.

External Passage text is unavailable through this reader. Paratext text is never imported into the FieldWorks project. The window does not offer .txt or JSONL Source ingestion, because the Source command contract does not support those kinds.

Choose **FieldWorks Texts** to return to the available Text reader. Check Texts for the current Selection and choose a Text in Passage to read its stored analyses. FieldWorks Text selection is separate from the external Source Context. An existing Corpus is not treated as a Source.

Removed, unreadable and outdated Sources are shown as such. Refresh the project to read a newer Baseline. No missing count is shown as zero, and opening Sources never starts a parse.

Source changes use the pending Proposal. If another Proposal is the current staging target, choose **Return to Current Project** before staging a Source change. Folder and Current remain local commands.

entries.title: Switching projects
entries.description: Use the project menu at the top of the Motif window to move between FieldWorks projects.
entries.helpPage:
# Switching projects

Use the project menu at the top of the Motif window to move between FieldWorks projects.

1. Choose **Select new…** to browse for a `.fwdata` file, or choose **Open recent** and select a project Motif already knows.
2. Wait for the project’s Baseline, Selection, and stored results to load.
3. Check the project name on **Progress** before taking an action.

Each project has its own Motif workflow information. Switching away does not move its pending changes into another project; when you open it again, its changes are shown with that project. If Parse all words or AI Handoff is running, switching projects cancels that work before Motif loads the new project.

Choose **Configure…** from the project menu to reopen the project’s saved Selection and parsing limits. Use **Refresh** to read the saved project and capture a new Baseline, then choose **Parse all words** to measure the saved Selection; opening the project alone only reads stored results.

entries.title: Text Coverage
entries.description: Text Coverage measures how much of the Default Selection produced a completed parse in the saved results. The Overview command reports selected words and their places separately: one written form can appear many times in a Text.
entries.helpPage:
# Text Coverage

[Text Coverage](term:text-coverage) measures how much of the Default Selection produced a completed parse in the saved results. The [Overview command](cmd:overview) reports selected words and their places separately: one written form can appear many times in a Text.

Parse completion is not human approval. It does not establish that a person kept an analysis at each place. Progress does not use this measure to fill a chapter approval strip or calculate an approval percentage.

A completed search with no analysis differs from an incomplete search that stopped at a work limit or the time safety net. Missing, unreadable or stale results do not mean zero. Digit-only places and places in other writing systems are counted separately where the stored Text summaries provide those counts.

The command can also group recorded parse coverage by frequency band. A word list's supplied counts describe that list, not places in a Text. Choose **Texts** to inspect the current Selection's words and places, and see [Parse all words](term:parse-all-words) for the stored run's scope. See [Progress](guide:progress) for the window's Next rows and health details.

entries.title: Texts
entries.description: Texts shows the reader and the current Selection in Sources and Passage. Open the side panel to inspect Paratext Source metadata or choose FieldWorks Texts. Check the FieldWorks Texts to include in the current Selection, then choose a Text in the reader to open its Passage and available analyses. Opening Texts does not start a parse.
entries.helpPage:
# Texts

**Texts** shows the reader and the current Selection in **Sources** and **Passage**. Open the side panel to inspect Paratext Source metadata or choose **FieldWorks Texts**. Check the FieldWorks Texts to include in the current Selection, then choose a Text in the reader to open its Passage and available analyses. Opening Texts does not start a parse.

Selecting a Paratext Source shows its saved Context, local folder and Current chapter. External Passage text is unavailable; Motif does not substitute a FieldWorks Text with the same name. See [Sources](guide:sources) for the supported kinds and the difference between Source, Context and Current.

Choose a word to inspect its recorded analysis and available actions, and to see every place the word occurs in the word panel; see [Passage](guide:passage). To inspect the word rows for the whole Context, open [Words](guide:words). To save the material measured for future runs, configure a [Default Selection](guide:default-selection).

entries.title: The Motif window
entries.description: The window has five main pages: Progress, Texts, Words, Grammar Guide, and Proposals. Choose a page in the rail on the left. Settings stays at the bottom of the rail.
entries.helpPage:
# The Motif window

The window has five main pages: **Progress**, **Texts**, **Words**, **Grammar Guide**, and **Proposals**. Choose a page in the rail on the left. **Settings** stays at the bottom of the rail.

**Progress** shows available project facts and next actions. **Texts** opens the reader and the current Selection. **Words** lists the words in the whole Context. **Grammar Guide** reads the project's saved Guide sections. **Proposals** shows saved Proposals and their standing, rationale, and Comments.

Each page owns its controls and any side panel it needs. In a narrow window a side panel can fold away; use its labelled reveal to open it again. The window adapts as you resize it or change zoom.

The health strip shows the project facts that are available. Open its details by hovering over it or moving keyboard focus to it. When a recorded median parser-work value is available, it appears in those details. Opening the strip does not start a parse.

Diagnostics is off by default. Turn it on from the health details or **View → Diagnostics** to add **Diagnostics** to the rail. Its two tabs show recorded grammar **Warnings** and **Speed by Rule**. Turning Diagnostics off hides the page and returns to Progress if it was open.

[Settings](guide:settings) contains display preferences, project options and the optional file Handoff. For keyboard navigation, see [Keyboard shortcuts](guide:keyboard-shortcuts).

entries.title: Speed by Rule
entries.description: Turn on View → Diagnostics, open Diagnostics, and choose Speed by Rule. This tab reads recorded rule work for the current parse and its contributing reruns. Opening it never starts a parse.
entries.helpPage:
# Speed by Rule

Turn on **View → Diagnostics**, open **Diagnostics**, and choose **Speed by Rule**. This tab reads recorded rule work for the current parse and its contributing reruns. Opening it never starts a parse.

Each count is the rule's recorded parser steps divided by the number of words that recorded parser work. The denominator states both the measured-word count and the requested word count. Motif does not turn milliseconds or statistics call counts into parser steps. Missing work or a missing denominator stays unavailable. The unattributed remainder is retained.

Complete aggregate totals may remain available when individual-word detail was retained for only part of the run. The tab labels that limit. If aggregates do not cover the selected words, the tab does not show them as complete totals. Outdated or mismatched parse results are discarded.

When Motif cannot attribute parser work to objects, the [Timing command](cmd:timing) reports `parserWorkByObjectAvailable: false` and a `parserWorkByObjectAbsentReason`, one of: `retried-words` (some words were retried), `word-without-work` (a counted word recorded no work), `object-without-work-or-identity` (an object total has no work or no usable identity), `no-unattributed-row` (the unattributed remainder is missing), `sums-do-not-match` (the objects do not add up to the words' work), `not-whole-run` (the words are not the whole run) or `statistics-unavailable` (the run kept no statistics). Raw counts are never printed.

Select a rule to resolve its exact **Open in FieldWorks** destination. An unresolved or synthetic identity has no inferred link. Motif displays no rule definition or editing form. Use FieldWorks to inspect or edit the rule, then measure again to compare its recorded work. No Fast or Slow classification is inferred from these counts.

The [Timing command](cmd:timing) remains available independently of this window tab. See [Diagnostics](guide:diagnostics) for warning and Proposal evidence.

entries.title: Warnings
entries.description: Turn on View → Diagnostics, then open the Warnings tab on Diagnostics. It reads the stored grammar check for the current project. Opening the page never starts a check or a parse.
entries.helpPage:
# Warnings

Turn on **View → Diagnostics**, then open the **Warnings** tab on **Diagnostics**. It reads the stored grammar check for the current project. Opening the page never starts a check or a parse.

Each row groups findings with the same recorded diagnostic code and shows the actual finding count. Uncoded findings stay separate. Motif does not invent categories or interpret a missing check as no warnings. Select a row to read its explanation, guidance, named objects and exact parser message. Report text stays in the language in which it was recorded.

Named FieldWorks objects open only through verified destinations supplied with their evidence. Missing objects and project settings have no object link. Motif shows evidence and names; read and edit rules in FieldWorks.

Word evidence distinguishes exact identity uses, possible membership matches and spelling matches. A membership or spelling match alone does not establish that a word uses the object. A partial or unavailable full count stays unavailable. **Show Words** brings the selected finding's recorded word list into view. **Hide This Warning** hides one finding (its rule plus its object) for you only. Hidden warnings are listed under **Settings → Hidden Warnings**, where you can unhide them. The warning count shows how many are hidden. Hiding never changes the grammar.

Save grammar edits in FieldWorks and refresh Motif to obtain current evidence. A warning is advice, not an additional Apply condition. See [Diagnostics](guide:diagnostics) for the page's other tab and Proposal evidence.

entries.title: What Motif does
entries.description: Motif reads a saved FieldWorks project and records how its parser handles a Selection of words. It helps you inspect texts, word analyses, stored grammar warnings and Proposals for changes. FieldWorks remains the place where you edit the project; Motif writes changes only when you choose Apply.
entries.helpPage:
# What Motif does

Motif reads a saved FieldWorks project and records how its parser handles a Selection of words. It helps you inspect texts, word analyses, stored grammar warnings and Proposals for changes. FieldWorks remains the place where you edit the project; Motif writes changes only when you choose Apply.

The interface uses Source Sans 3 and Lora. Linguistic text uses the fonts selected in the project's writing systems. Motif includes Andika, Charis SIL, Doulos SIL and Gentium Plus for projects that use them.
