To start, [install Motif](guide:install), [open your project](guide:open-a-project), and press **Refresh**. Choose the words to parse and run the parser when you want new measurements. Opening the window reads stored results; it does not start a parse.

Use **Progress** to see available next actions, **Texts** to read the selected texts, **Words** to inspect their word rows, **Grammar Guide** to read the saved Guide sections, and **Proposals** to inspect saved Proposals. The optional **Diagnostics** page shows stored warnings and rule timing. See [The Motif window](guide:the-window) for the page layout and [Settings](guide:settings) for display and connection choices.

You can choose to make a file Handoff for an assistant. Review the data-sensitivity notice before sharing its files: they can contain grammar, lexicon and text data.

entries.title: When a Change No Longer Fits
entries.description: A staged change names the project content it was made against. A later FieldWorks save can leave that change unable to fit, or leave its occurrence uncertain. Apply stays unavailable until the engine can establish that the changes fit.
entries.helpPage:
# When a Change No Longer Fits

A staged change names the project content it was made against. A later FieldWorks save can leave that change unable to fit, or leave its occurrence uncertain. Apply stays unavailable until the engine can establish that the changes fit.

**Refresh** to read the current project, then inspect the affected word in **Texts**. Use **Undo** (Ctrl+Z, or ⌘+Z on macOS) to take back the last staged choice if it is no longer wanted, or stage a different choice for the place, or check it against the current context before staging a replacement. Motif never forces an uncertain change onto a different place. See [Replace a Pending Change](guide:replace-a-pending-change).

entries.title: When something goes wrong
entries.description: If a command or action is refused, first read the message in Motif. It often explains what needs to change, such as saving in FieldWorks, refreshing the Baseline, or removing a change that no longer fits.
entries.helpPage:
# When something goes wrong

If a command or action is refused, first read the message in Motif. It often explains what needs to change, such as saving in FieldWorks, refreshing the Baseline, or removing a change that no longer fits.

You can open the same report preview from [Settings](guide:settings). It is also available from a refusal or a stalled parse.

For a problem report, choose **Report a Problem** in Settings (or **Report a problem** in the status bar) and review the preview. By default it includes Motif and PanGloss versions, your operating system, the window action, the refusal code, the command's exit status when available, and a stack without file locations. It leaves out project paths and names, words, grammar, and raw parser output. You can choose **Include Local Details** to add the error text and facts, which include everything shown under Details and sometimes more, such as the places Motif looked for a missing PanGloss; those may contain project or language data. Copying the report or opening the issue form happens only after you review the preview, and the issue form is not submitted automatically.

Send feedback through [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/sillsdev/motif/issues). If you cannot use GitHub, copy the reviewed report and email it to [john_lambert@sil.org](mailto:john_lambert@sil.org). Review any local details before sharing them.

If Motif says the project store was made by a different version and offers **Delete Motif's store and reopen**, read the confirmation before continuing. That action deletes Motif's store and recreates it; changes not applied yet are lost, but the FieldWorks project is not touched.

If Motif says its file for this project is damaged, close every Motif window. Keep a copy of the matching `.motif.db` file beside the project's `.fwdata` file if support may need it. Remove only that Motif file, then reopen the project; changes not applied yet will be lost, but the FieldWorks project is unchanged. If you cannot confirm the file belongs to Motif, leave it in place and ask for help.

If Motif cannot read its machine store, close every Motif window and keep a copy of the `motif.db` file at the path shown in the recovery instructions. Move or remove that file only if you can confirm it is Motif's machine store, then reopen Motif. Its Known projects and local usage history will be cleared; FieldWorks projects and their pending changes are unchanged. If you cannot confirm the file belongs to Motif, leave it in place and ask for help.

The parser trace in **Why This Analysis?** is visible when **View → Diagnostics** is on. You can save or copy diagnostic information for a particular word. It can include real word forms and morphological details, so review it before sharing.

If the app stops after an error, the separate **Motif Has Stopped** window keeps the full error under **Details** and offers **Report a Problem**. The same preview shows what will be copied or placed in the issue form. The local **Details** may contain project paths or linguistic information; they are added to a report only when you choose **Include Local Details**.

![Recorded Diagnostics evidence](shot:try-word-typing/trace)

entries.title: Why This Analysis?
entries.description: Why This Analysis? is a grey fold in the word panel on Texts. It is visible only when View → Diagnostics is on. With Diagnostics off the word panel is unchanged and Motif does no diagnostic work.
entries.helpPage:
# Why This Analysis?

**Why This Analysis?** is a grey fold in the word panel on **Texts**. It is visible only when **View → Diagnostics** is on. With Diagnostics off the word panel is unchanged and Motif does no diagnostic work.

The fold starts folded. Open it to ask the parser for a trace of the selected word, against the Baseline the window is showing. Motif does not run the parser until you open the fold. Folding it, selecting another word, switching projects, refreshing to a different Baseline or turning Diagnostics off cancels the request and discards what it returned. A trace for another word or another Baseline is never shown.

## What the fold shows

- **Analyses**: the recorded analyses, each with its morphemes. Each name has an **Open in FieldWorks** link when the trace recorded a verified FieldWorks target. Motif shows names only; rules and entries are read and edited in FieldWorks.
- **Rules on the best path**: each rule's name, with an **Open in FieldWorks** link. The fold shows no rule definitions.
- **Failed branches**: the recorded attempts that did not parse, with where each stopped. The first 20 are listed and the rest are counted.
- **Parser work**: counted in steps, never in milliseconds.

When the search stopped at its work limit or its safety net, the fold says so and shows **at least** the failed branches it recorded. An incomplete or missing trace never means that there were no failed branches, and a missing count is not zero.

## Full Trace

Choose **Full Trace** to read every recorded event inside the word panel. It never opens a page or a new window. **Copy Trace** copies the diagnostic exactly as recorded; review it before sharing, because it can contain real project data. Each event shows its address, which identifies it within this saved trace only.

A **Tried** rule was not necessarily applied, and **Blocked** names a recorded event without naming an unrecorded blocker. A reason PanGloss did not record is shown as not recorded.

![Diagnostics for a project](shot:try-word-typing/trace)

To trace a word saved earlier or to run a trace from the command line, see the [trace command](cmd:trace).

entries.title: Words
entries.description: Words lists every written shape in the whole Context: all the chapters or documents you have chosen to work on, and none of the ones left for Later. Choosing a different Current chapter in Texts does not change this list or its counts.
entries.helpPage:
# Words

**Words** lists every written shape in the whole Context: all the chapters or documents you have chosen to work on, and none of the ones left for Later. Choosing a different Current chapter in [Texts](guide:texts) does not change this list or its counts.

## One row for each written shape

A spelling that occurs in many places has one row. The row counts every place it occurs, in every chosen Text. Spellings are matched after the same Unicode normalisation Motif already uses, so a word typed with a combining accent and the same word typed with a single accented letter are one row. Two writing systems that happen to spell a word alike are never joined: each keeps its own row and its own font and direction.

Motif does not work out stems, families of related words or sound patterns here. If the same spelling has different analyses in different places, the row says how many readings it has, and each reading stays separate when you keep one.

When the parser has read a word, its row shows how many analyses it built, for example 2 analyses.

## Opening a word

Choose a row to open its word card and, beside it, the list of places it occurs. This is the same panel [Passage](guide:passage) uses. Tick the places you mean, pick the reading to keep, then choose **Approve**. Only the ticked places are staged, and nothing reaches FieldWorks until you choose **Apply**. **Not a Word** marks the spelling as not a word for the whole project.

The filter chips narrow the rows by where the project stands, and the search box narrows them by spelling. The rows load as you scroll, so a long list stays quick.

## Sources that are not FieldWorks Texts

This page reads the FieldWorks Texts in your Context. Words from a Paratext project, a text file or a JSONL file are not listed until Motif can read their words with the same exact places; they are not hidden under another count.

## Keys

Up and Down move between rows, Page Up and Page Down move a screen, Home and End go to the first and last row, and Enter or Space opens or closes the word card. A, D and U stage an opinion for the focused analysis. [Keyboard Shortcuts](guide:keyboard-shortcuts) lists them all.

entries.title: Writing systems in the window
entries.description: Motif uses the writing-system settings saved in the Baseline when it displays project language text. Text keeps its FieldWorks direction and style size in the window.
entries.helpPage:
# Writing systems in the window

Motif uses the writing-system settings saved in the Baseline when it displays project language text. Text keeps its FieldWorks direction and style size in the window.

Most word forms, glosses and interlinear fields use the **Normal** style. A line in **Texts** uses the source paragraph's style. Motif includes Andika, Charis SIL, Doulos SIL and Gentium Plus, and prefers an installed copy of those fonts when it is available. It treats **Charis** and **Charis SIL** as names for the same family. If another requested font is missing, Motif uses an available fallback and shows one quiet notice the first time it draws text in that writing system.

In FieldWorks, change a writing system's font, font features or direction under **Format › Set up Vernacular Writing Systems…** or **Format › Set up Analysis Writing Systems…**. Choose the **Font** or **General** tab. Change style-specific fonts and sizes under **Format › Styles…**.

Capture a new [Baseline](term:baseline) after changing these settings so Motif reads the saved values. [Show writing systems](cmd:writing-systems) lists the values Motif recorded.
